СтраницаPage 67 · 75 hours and a design strategy
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

75 hours and a design strategy

Four blocks from the original programme
A, hours 1-20: 10 h theory + 10 h practice. Sketches, constraints, dimensions and parameters;
extrusions, revolutions, patterns, holes and fillets; parts, assemblies, revolute joints and
intersections. Deliverable: a link, a bracket and a joint assembly with three labelled axes.
B, hours 21-40: 10+10 h. Fasteners, inserts, bearings, shafts and couplings; fits, datums,
tolerance stacks and GD&T fundamentals; cables and maintenance access. Deliverable: drawings,
an exploded view, a bill of materials (BOM) and specimens for checking fits.
C, hours 41-60: 10+10 h. Free-body diagrams, equilibrium, load transfer, stress and strain,
shear, beam deflection, factor of safety and load uncertainty. Deliverable: a hand calculation for an
unfavourable configuration and a comparison of two link versions.
D, hours 61-75: 5+10 h. FEA: restraints, mesh and convergence; FDM anisotropy, orientation
and layers; PLA, PETG and TPU; printing and a static test of one assembled leg. Deliverable: a
comparison of hand calculations, FEA and measurements, with limitations stated. Total: 35 h of
study and analysis and 40 h of practice.

Study rhythm and production
Study the theory in two-hour sessions; split the final 5 h into 2+2+1. Divide each ten-hour practical
block into five two-hour sessions. Print small test specimens first, then the critical assembly, and
print the entire leg only after checking the fits. Waiting for a print to finish does not count towards
study hours; prepare drawings, calculations or the log while the printer runs.
Dates come from the overall plan. Sessions from an adjacent module may occur at the M05
boundary; rest days, holidays and integration stages remain in place. Allocate work hours
sequentially across available sessions, without counting hours twice or adding hours. Plan printing
in advance so that verification does not depend on the final night of the month.

Priorities when time is limited
First ensure that geometry rebuilds reliably and that connections are justified, then address
strength and maintenance access, and finally appearance. If you fall behind, omit photorealistic
images, elaborate enclosure styling and a second CAD environment. Retain the three-joint
assembly, critical drawings, BOM, hand calculation, a simple FEA check and physical specimens.
Before testing, record the calculated load range and the fixture's permissible loads; a previous
result does not automatically carry over after a change in material, layer direction or geometry. No
factor of safety in this plan is a universal approval: select it for a specific scenario and support it
with data. Conduct a static test on a restrained specimen, without an operating actuator.


























M5 • 31 Jan 2027 - 24 Feb 2027 • 75 hours                                                                           2 / 15
СтраницаPage 68 · Sketches and parameters: build an
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Sketches and parameters: build an
adjustable link

What to study in CAD
Study the sketch plane, origin, construction geometry and constraints: coincidence, horizontal and
vertical alignment, parallelism, perpendicularity, tangency, symmetry and dimensions. Identify the
degrees of freedom that remain. A fully constrained sketch should express design intent; fixing
every point indiscriminately conceals relationships and makes changes difficult.
Separate driving dimensions from reference dimensions. Use the names L_link, wall, shaft_d,
bearing_d, bolt_pitch and cable_clearance. Store units and comments. Practise extrusion
(extrude/pad), revolution (revolve), pattern, hole and fillet operations on features of the intended
part. Build the main volumes and holes first, then secondary fillets, so the cause of errors is easier
to locate when the shape changes.

Task 1. Parametric link
Inputs: the distance between axes, the envelope of the future mount and the selected printing
process. Sketch a link with two joint centres, a symmetrical outline and parametric thickness.
Extrude the body, add holes and one lightening cavity. Create three length variants by changing
only the parameter, rather than stretching faces manually.
Save the model in its native CAD format and a table of variants. Check that centre distances match
the specification, the sketch is fully constrained and geometry rebuilds without errors after a length
change. Edge case: the minimum length makes holes intersect the cavity. Provide a way to detect
this error in the model or checklist, and explicitly state the permitted parameter range.

Task 2. Bracket and a revolved part
Model a U-shaped bracket and a spacer bushing. Use a revolved profile for the bushing and a
pattern for repeated fastener holes. Identify mating surfaces, where a flat seat is needed under a
screw head, and which tool must reach the fastener. Do not make a wall thin simply because CAD
can construct it.
Save both parts in native CAD format, a bracket section view and the results of checking the main
dimensions. Change wall thickness and shaft diameter, then verify that symmetry is retained.
Deliberate error: a sketch references a face that disappears after a fillet change. Move the
reference to a stable datum plane or axis and explain why the revised model tolerates edits better.
































M5 • 31 Jan 2027 - 24 Feb 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          3 / 15
СтраницаPage 69 · Three joints, assembly and maintenance
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Three joints, assembly and maintenance

A component differs from a body
Understand the difference between a part, a component, an instance and an assembly. Two
identical bushings in an assembly should reference one model unless one needs a separate
revision. Define a fixed base and three revolute joints. Each joint has an axis, a zero position, a
positive angular direction and geometric motion limits.
Do not infer mechanical feasibility from a single chosen configuration. Collisions can appear during
combined rotations, and the motor housing and screw heads occupy space. Add simple envelopes
for the tool, cable and connector as separate reference components; include them in access
checks, but exclude them from the printed part's mass.

Task 3. Passive 3-DOF leg
Assemble the base bracket, three joint units and links. Name the joints J1/J2/J3 and label their local
axes and initial angles. Check each joint's motion separately, then combinations of extreme
positions with intermediate points. Initially, geometry determines the learning model's ranges; the
real actuator's limits must be reconciled later.
Save the assembly, a configuration table and screenshots of intersections before and after
correction. Check for exactly three intended degrees of freedom, a fixed base and no unintended
motion in rigid groups. A discrete set of poses does not prove there are no collisions between them;
state the checking increment and investigate suspicious intervals in greater detail.

Task 4. Cable routing and replacement of one joint
Route a provisional cable from the base to the distal joint, allowing extra length for motion,
securing it and providing connector access. Check extreme poses: the cable must not become taut,
enter a joint gap or rub against a sharp edge. Take the minimum bend radius from the actual cable;
for an envelope sketch, mark it as an assumption requiring confirmation.
Describe disassembly in the reverse order of assembly: which screw is removed first, and whether
the shaft can be withdrawn and the bushing replaced without dismantling the whole link. Save five
maintenance steps and an exploded view. Edge case: the screw head is accessible, but a hex key
cannot be inserted along its axis. Add the tool envelope and modify the mounting. For the future
hand, this exercise will recur within the smaller space of a finger.



































M5 • 31 Jan 2027 - 24 Feb 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          4 / 15
СтраницаPage 70 · Fits, datums, fasteners and tolerance stacks
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Fits, datums, fasteners and tolerance stacks

Basic machine elements
Study the functions of screws, nuts, washers, threaded inserts in plastic, bearings, bushings, shafts
and couplings. Separate their functions: a screw clamps, a shaft defines rotation, and a bearing
transfers load while allowing specified motion. The thread of an ordinary screw is generally
unsuitable as a precision rotational bearing surface. Select fits to suit the assembly method and
actual part tolerances.
A datum is a surface or axis from which important dimensions are specified. GD&T fundamentals
explain why axis position and surface perpendicularity differ from a single linear tolerance. Choose
one clear set of datums A/B/C, identify the controlled axis and explain how to measure it. Studying
the complete geometric tolerancing standard is outside the month's scope.

Task 5. Specimen for checking holes and inserts
Build a small specimen containing a series of fit holes with sizes close to the nominal size of the
selected shaft or insert. Choose the increment relative to the expected accuracy of the printer and
measuring tool; for example, 0.1 mm may serve as an exercise increment, rather than a promised
FDM accuracy. Print the specimen in two orientations with the same material and profile.
Measure the holes using an available method, then check the fit of the actual mating part. For
small internal diameters, assess the limitations of calliper measurements and use a known shaft as
a functional gauge. Save nominal/measured/fit_result. Edge cases: a hole becomes oval because of
layer direction, an insert splits the wall, or a part fits only after undocumented reworking. Record
any machining or finishing separately.

Task 6. Axial clearance and drawing
Build a tolerance stack for the assembly: bracket width, two walls, bushings, the rotating link and
washers. Calculate minimum and maximum axial clearance for unfavourable tolerance
combinations. Do not add standard deviations as though they were guaranteed dimensional limits:
the probabilistic estimate in M03 and a worst-case tolerance check answer different questions.
Prepare a drawing of the critical link with views, a section, datums, hole dimensions, material, print
orientation and revision. Acceptance check: another person understands what to manufacture and
measure. Deliberate error: the dimension chain permits negative clearance and binding after
tightening. Correct the spacer bushing or geometry; simply loosening the screw without a
controlled fastening arrangement is not a solution.
































M5 • 31 Jan 2027 - 24 Feb 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          5 / 15
СтраницаPage 71 · Statics and strength: how loads are
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Statics and strength: how loads are
transferred

Essential mechanics
Obtain a free body by mentally separating a part and replacing constraints with reactions. In a
static case, the sums of forces and moments are zero. Show how the load passes from the foot
through links, shafts and the bracket to the body. Stress is internal force per unit area, and strain is
relative dimensional change; modulus E relates them in a simple linear elastic model.
Study tension, compression, shear, bending and deflection. For an ideal cantilever beam with end
force F, M=F·L, σ_max=M·c/I and δ=F·L³/(3EI). Here c is the distance to the outermost fibre, and I is
the second moment of area of the section, not a mass moment of inertia. These equations apply for
small deflections, the stated supports and an appropriate material model.
In a simple case, factor of safety n is the ratio of a selected material limit to calculated stress. First
state the failure mode and the source of the limiting value. For printed plastic, parameters must
correspond to layer direction, temperature and loading conditions; an unknown value cannot be
replaced by an arbitrarily generous safety factor.

Task 7. An unfavourable leg pose
Choose an assumed future body mass and a load-distribution scenario, marking them as design
assumptions. Do not automatically divide the weight by the total number of legs: some supports
may carry no load. For three different poses, calculate the force lever arm about each joint and the
base-mount reaction. Include the links' own weight if it is already known from the model or
weighing.
Save three free-body diagrams, a force and torque table and the selected design load case. Check
force and moment balance, dimensions and sensitivity to a load change. This provides a static
reference; foot-strike impact and dynamic accelerations need a separate model. Reflect their
uncertainty in the selected scenario and safety factor, rather than concealing it behind a claim of
reliability.

Task 8. Two link versions
Simplify the critical part of the link to a beam with a known cross-section. Compare versions A and
B: change section height or add a rib while retaining a clear load path. Calculate expected
deflection, stress and mass; for a rectangle, I=b·h³/12, so the orientation of its height relative to
bending matters.
Prepare a calculation note and two CAD model variants. Verify the prediction: doubling the force
doubles deflection in a linear model, while changing height has a nonlinear effect. Edge case: a thin
wall beside a hole is not represented by the beam idealisation. Mark this region for local FEA and
inspection of the tested specimen. A material's catalogue strength is not yet the allowable strength
of the printed assembly.




















M5 • 31 Jan 2027 - 24 Feb 2027 • 75 hours                                                                           6 / 15
СтраницаPage 72 · FEA: formulation, mesh and independent
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

FEA: formulation, mesh and independent
verification

Avoiding unjustified confidence
FEA divides geometry into finite elements and approximately solves the equations of the chosen
model. Before running it, record the material, constitutive law, loads and restraints. Fully clamping
a large surface is usually stiffer than a real bolted or bushed connection; compare one restraint
arrangement with a physically plausible alternative.
For the first exercise, use one simple part and a linear elastic model. Confirm the units of E, loads
and dimensions. An isotropic approximation of FDM is a limited model suitable for comparing
trends; it does not automatically describe interlayer failure or TPU nonlinearity. Do not reach a final
conclusion about a plastic part's failure solely from a coloured equivalent-stress map.

Task 9. A beam, then the actual link
First perform FEA on the same cantilever as in task 8, with the same L, section, E, force and
support. Compare deflection at a selected point with the hand calculation. If the discrepancy is
large, check units, boundary conditions and geometry before complicating the model. Then apply
the approach to the actual link and name the metrics in advance: point deflection, support reaction
and stress away from an artificial singularity.
Build three mesh refinement levels while retaining the same problem formulation. For each, record
element count, mesh size, solution time and metrics. An exercise target is a change of less than 5%
in the selected deflection between the final two meshes; this is a convergence criterion for this
experiment, not a universal accuracy or permission to operate.

What to save
Save the original analysis model, material parameters, a list of loaded and restrained surfaces,
mesh characteristics and the comparison with the hand calculation. Show the exaggerated
deformed shape with its scale labelled; without a label, a viewer may mistake visual magnification
for actual deflection.
Edge cases: an unrestrained rigid body, incorrect force units, a load applied to a single vertex and
excessive local stress at an ideal sharp edge. A stress maximum that grows without converging
needs investigation. Do not simply refine the mesh and declare the latest peak a reliable part
stress. For M05, recognising the limitation and checking overall deflection and support reactions is
sufficient.






























M5 • 31 Jan 2027 - 24 Feb 2027 • 75 hours                                                                           7 / 15
СтраницаPage 73 · Printing, materials and testing the passive
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Printing, materials and testing the passive
leg

PLA, PETG and TPU according to part function
Compare materials in terms of stiffness, temperature response, creep, impact behaviour, layer
adhesion and ease of processing. PLA is useful for initial dimensional prototypes; PETG is often
used for tougher parts; TPU suits a flexible foot or pad. These are directions for selection, not
guaranteed properties of a particular spool. Consult the manufacturer's data and test your own
specimens.
FDM orientation affects interlayer bonding, holes, overhangs and the quality of bearing surfaces.
Record layer direction relative to expected tension and bending. Infill density is only one
parameter: wall thickness, perimeter count, top and bottom layers, and load transfer may have a
stronger influence. Do not compare two materials while simultaneously changing the entire
geometry and profile.

Task 10. Specimens and a static check
Prepare two identical beam specimens in different orientations. Measure actual dimensions and
mass. Place a specimen in a simple fixture, apply a small known force using a weight or force
gauge, and measure deflection at one point. Choose the load range from the preliminary
calculation and the fixture's and instrument's capabilities; increase load in steps recorded in
advance.
At each level, save load, deflection, hold time and residual deformation after unloading. The fixture
must retain the part and weight, and the possible drop area must be clear. Stop testing if the
fixture shifts, cracking is heard, a crack appears or deflection becomes unexpectedly large.
Destroying the finished leg is not required to pass: a measured range and a description of any first
signs of damage or unacceptable deformation are sufficient.

From a test specimen to an assembled leg
Choose orientation and profile from the specimen tests, print the critical links and assemble the
passive leg. For the static experiment, use a fixture to lock the joints in one calculated pose; do not
rely on the resistance of an unpowered motor. Apply a known, limited foot load and measure total
deflection, play before loading and recovery after unloading.
Compare the direction and order of magnitude of deflection with the hand calculation and FEA,
explaining the contribution of joints and mountings. Prepare CAD revision B to address one
observed defect: a fit, access, a rib or cable clearance. Save photographs, the raw measurement
table, a force-deflection plot, observations and the decision on the next revision. A successful static
test does not establish walking fatigue life or impact strength.

























M5 • 31 Jan 2027 - 24 Feb 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          8 / 15
СтраницаPage 74 · Work sequence: hours 1-40
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Work sequence: hours 1-40

Block A: a model that can be changed
Hours 1-2. Choose CAD, create the project structure and a three-axis diagram. Hours 3-4. Study
geometric and dimensional constraints and fully constrain a link sketch. Hours 5-6. Study
parameters, expressions and units. Hours 7-8. Practise extrusion, revolution, patterns, holes and
fillets (extrude/revolve/pattern/hole/fillet) on your own parts. Hours 9-10. Study components,
instances, assemblies and revolute joints.
Hours 11-20 - practice. 2 h: task 1 and three link lengths. 2 h: bracket and bushing. 2 h: 3-DOF
assembly. 2 h: extreme poses and intersections. 2 h: cable, tool and saving revision A. Prepare a
short dimensional-specimen print at the end if helpful, so it does not delay the next practical
session.
Checkpoint at hour 20: change one link's length and wall thickness. The assembly must rebuild, the
axes must remain connected, and the unconfirmed motor envelope must retain its provisional
status. If rebuilding fails, correct model dependencies first: adding decorative parts only increases
the work needed for revision.

Block B: manufacture and maintenance
Hours 21-22. Study fasteners, inserts and the functions of connections. Hours 23-24. Study
shafts, bearings, bushings, couplings and fit requirements. Hours 25-26. Cover datums and
tolerance stacks. Hours 27-28. Study how to prepare a clear drawing and the basics of geometric
tolerances. Hours 29-30. Check cables, tool access and the repair sequence.
Hours 31-40 - practice. 2 h: fit specimens and print preparation. 2 h: measurement and
functional trial fitting. 2 h: axial tolerance stack and clearance correction. 2 h: drawings and
exploded view. 2 h: BOM, assembly sequence and revision control. If specimen printing takes
longer, prepare drawings while it runs; do not change fit criteria after seeing the result.
In the BOM, include part_id, revision, quantity, material or product type, dimensional source and
method of obtaining the part. Separate printed parts, standard fasteners and provisional
components. Totals by item must match the assembly. For every important item, make clear
whether it can be manufactured now or requires selection of the actual actuator.







































M5 • 31 Jan 2027 - 24 Feb 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          9 / 15
СтраницаPage 75 · Work sequence: hours 41-75
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Work sequence: hours 41-75

Block C: calculate before loading
Hours 41-42. Draw free bodies of the links and their reactions. Hours 43-44. Calculate moments
for three leg poses. Hours 45-46. Study stress, strain, shear and modulus E. Hours 47-48. Study
a cantilever beam and the influence of cross-section. Hours 49-50. Describe uncertainties in load
and material properties and justify the design safety factor.
Hours 51-60 - practice. 2 h: leg design load case. 2 h: simplified beam and unit checks. 2 h:
versions A and B, comparing mass and deflection. 2 h: prototype test fixture and measurement
plan. 2 h: preparation for printing critical parts and the calculation package. State the limits of
available fixtures before choosing loads.
At hour 60, explain where the most heavily loaded region lies and why. If the answer rests only on
a sense that a region looks thin, return to force lever arms and the load path. If geometry is too
complex for a hand calculation, choose a clear idealisation and explicitly identify what it omits.

Block D: compare calculation, simulation and measurement
Hours 61-62. Cover FEA boundary conditions, units and material selection. Hours 63-64. Study
mesh, convergence and limitations of local peaks. Hour 65. Compare PLA, PETG and TPU, layer
orientation and the static verification plan.
Hours 66-75 - practice. 2 h: FEA of a simple beam and a hand-calculation comparison. 2 h: actual
link and three meshes. 2 h: measured specimens, fits and joint locking. 2 h: static experiment on
one assembled leg, table and photographs. 2 h: revision B, final drawings, BOM and presentation.
Prepare final parts and specimens before these sessions.
If the available FEA environment requires lengthy setup, retain a minimal analysis of one simple
part in an available solver and do not move to a full assembly contact model. Measuring one leg
and making a justified comparison with a simple model is more useful than an unfinished complex
simulation. The three meshes serve the chosen metric, rather than a target number of analyses.
Final independent check: double the assumed load or rotate a rectangular section by 90°. Predict
the change in deflection and the most critical region before running the analysis. Then verify the
result by hand and with FEA; increase the physical load only if the new range is justified and stays
within the prepared test limits.

СтраницаPage 76 · Acceptance checks: model, documentation
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Acceptance checks: model, documentation
and observations

Six required checks of errors and limitations
1. Rebuilding. Changing length or thickness does not break the main geometry. 2. Collision. An
extreme combined pose has been checked with fasteners and tools included. 3. Fit. An
unfavourable tolerance stack does not conceal binding; retain an unsuitable specimen with the
recorded observation.
4. FEA units and supports. Incorrect scale or an unrestrained body is detected through
independent verification. 5. Mesh. A growing local peak is not automatically accepted as a reliable
physical result; the selected deflection has been checked for convergence. 6. Physical specimen.
Residual deformation, play or a crack is recorded and influences the next revision, rather than
disappearing from the report.

What to prepare
Save the leg assembly in native CAD format, a STEP export and print files with units and revision;
critical-part drawings; an exploded view; BOM; parameter table; force, moment and beam
calculations; FEA file and settings; mesh table; print profiles; specimens and actual measurements.
Photographs must make it possible to identify the physical part by its part_id and layer direction.
Check that all driving sketches are constrained, the assembly has three intended degrees of
freedom, the assembly and maintenance sequence is known, and calculation assumptions are not
presented as properties of the finished robot. For every deflection or load value, identify its source:
hand calculation, simulation or experiment. Compare trends and scale under identical conditions
and explain discrepancies.

Self-check questions and handover
How does a geometric constraint differ from a dimension? Why is a part instance preferable to a
copied independent body? Where are the datums for the critical hole? What happens to clearance
during tightening? Why does support on a threaded surface fail to provide precise rotation? How
does the foot load reach the body? Why does section height enter I to the third power?
What does a factor of safety mean when printed strength is unknown? Why does isotropic FEA not
establish interlayer strength? How do you distinguish a singularity from a real stress concentration?
What did the specimen reveal that CAD did not? Which conclusions cannot be carried over from a
static test to walking?
Pass mounting dimensions, envelopes, cable route, mass, maintenance constraints and the test
fixture to M06-M07. Once the actual actuator is selected, its mounting must be checked and its
loads recalculated. For the future hand, retain the parametric bushing, bracket and fit-checking
method; the complete hand and tactile elements will appear in the relevant module and a separate
optional block.

СтраницаPage 77 · Assigned reading: a focused reading route
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Assigned reading: a focused reading route

Read only the specified sections before the corresponding experiment. Most literature is in English;
keep explanations, the glossary and the report in English for this edition. Reading and preparation
are included in the existing 75 hours; you do not need to work through entire books.

Core reading
1. David Roylance, Mechanics of Materials, open MIT modules. Introduction to Elastic
Response; Stresses in Beams; Beam Displacements. For tasks 7-8, derive the relationship between
load, stress and deflection. Then read selected parts of Finite Element Analysis for task 9: a mesh
approximates a model, so comparison with the beam is compulsory.
2. Alexander Slocum, FUNdaMENTALS of Design. Chapters 4, 8-10: Linkages; Structures;
Structural Conn. & Interfaces; Bearings. For tasks 3-5, study only diagrams relevant to your joint,
load transfer and part connections. Record which motions the support allows and which reactions it
transmits.
3. Yorik van Havre, A FreeCAD Manual. Modeling for product design; Preparing models for 3D
printing; Creating FEM analyses. For tasks 1 and 9 and specimen printing, study the parametric
model, mesh export and analysis setup. This is an introductory book; check current commands
against the help for your version. If using Fusion, read only the general principles of models and
meshes.

Three references for the chosen tools
CAD commands. FreeCAD: Sketcher: Constraints, PartDesign: Body, Tools, TechDraw: Views,
Dimensions. Alternative: Fusion Parameters and Joints, Limits.
FEA. FreeCAD FEM: Workflow; SimScale Static: materials, boundary conditions, mesh as an
alternative reference. In task 9, record the actual restraints and check mesh refinement.
Print material. Prusa Filament Material Guide: PLA, PETG, FLEX. This compares materials; it is not
a ready-made profile for your printer. Establish temperature and operating settings from filament
manufacturer data and specimen test results.
Reading deliverables. Prepare one load-transfer sketch, one beam calculation, a table of fit
dimensions and a justification of print orientation. Connect these results to the decisions in your
CAD revision.

СтраницаPage 78 · Glossary: terms and definitions
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Glossary: terms and definitions

Parametric model. Geometry defined by dimensions, relationships and a history of operations;
changing a driving parameter rebuilds dependent features.
Sketch constraint. A geometric or dimensional condition that reduces the independent motions
of sketch elements, such as coincident points or parallel lines.
Degree of freedom. An independent coordinate needed to specify an admissible mechanism
configuration; the number is determined by joints and imposed constraints.
Tolerance. The permitted variation in a specified dimension or geometric parameter, selected
according to function and manufacturing method.
Fit. The nature of a connection between mating parts, determined by the combination of their
limiting dimensions; a fit may be clearance, interference or transition.
Backlash. Free relative motion when the load direction reverses; it arises from clearances and
affects motion transmission accuracy.
Tolerance stack. The relationship between several dimensions that jointly determine a final
clearance or position; each deviation's contribution depends on assembly geometry.
Load path. The sequence of components and connections through which a load passes from its
application point to the structure's supports.
Stress. Internal force per unit cross-sectional area, measured in pascals. Normal and shear
components are distinguished.
Strain. Relative change in material geometry; for uniaxial tension, ε=ΔL/L, a dimensionless
quantity.
Young's modulus. The coefficient relating normal stress and strain in the linear elastic region,
measured in pascals.
Stiffness. The ratio of load to the corresponding displacement in a linear model; it depends on
material, shape and support conditions.
Strength. A material's or part's ability to sustain load without failure through the mechanism
considered; it differs from resistance to elastic deflection.
Second moment of area. A geometric integral describing the distribution of area about an axis;
measured in m⁴, it influences flexural rigidity E·I.
Factor of safety. The ratio of a selected limiting value to an operating value for a specified failure
mechanism; it cannot correct an incorrect load model.
Anisotropy. The dependence of material properties on direction; a printed part's strength
between layers may differ from its strength along them.
Finite element analysis (FEA). Numerical analysis of a model divided into finite elements; the
result depends on material, loads, constraints, mesh and problem formulation.
Mesh convergence. Stabilisation of a selected result as the mesh is progressively refined; it does
not establish the correctness of the analysis's physical assumptions.
















M5 • 31 Jan 2027 - 24 Feb 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          13 / 15
СтраницаPage 79 · Equipment, installation and readiness checks
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Equipment, installation and readiness checks

Complete preparation within the first study blocks in place of a repeated general overview. The
total remains 75 hours; waiting for delivery is excluded. The statuses below identify actions for you
to take, rather than purchases or installations already completed.

USE EXISTING EQUIPMENT
MacBook Pro M4, your existing 3D printer with a profile for its exact model, hand tools and
a measurement log. There is no need to buy another printer. M05 ends with a passive leg and
specimens; the future actuator envelope may still be explicitly provisional.

BUY BEFORE MEASUREMENT AND PRINTING
1 pair of 150 mm callipers with external and internal jaws, a depth gauge and specified
measurement error appropriate to the part tolerances. Digital display resolution is not accuracy.
Check zero and repeatability on one specimen before inspecting fits.
Material: if supplies are unavailable, 1 spool of PLA for specimens and geometry; PETG if selected;
a small amount of TPU only for a flexible part or pad. Filament diameter and settings must suit the
printer; calculate the required mass with the slicer, allowing a reserve for repeat specimens.
Fasteners and supports: one set for one passive leg and specimens, according to the released
BOM: screws, nuts, washers, threaded inserts, shafts, bushings or bearings. Specify exact
diameters and quantities from your CAD model, ensuring that tools can reach the fasteners. Do not
order final actuators or a set of parts for the entire robot here.

INSTALL NOW - ONE CAD ENVIRONMENT
macOS ARM: FreeCAD, official macOS arm64 release or Fusion if already familiar. FreeCAD
requires Sketcher, PartDesign, assembly, TechDraw and FEM; analysis needs CalculiX and Gmsh.
Check whether these are included, configure their FEM paths and add missing components
following the instructions for your version. FEM Workflow describes the workflow; included
components depend on the chosen version's installer.
Install or update only the appropriate slicer and profile for the printer's exact model, following its
manufacturer's instructions. If choosing Fusion, check access to static FEA beforehand; if
unavailable, use a separate simple beam in FreeCAD FEM instead of buying an unnecessary
package. Save the CAD, solver and slicer versions and the profile in the project.

INSTALLATION AND READINESS CHECKS
1. Fully constrain a rectangular sketch, extrude it and change a dimension. 2. Export STEP and STL,
reopen them and check scale. 3. Create a PDF drawing with a dimension. 4. Analyse a static beam
with a known force and compare deflection with the hand formula. 5. Check dimensions and print
paths in the slicer, then manufacture one specimen; measure it before printing the whole leg.
Act on the checks: if the specimen does not achieve the required fit or sustain load across the
layers, change the print profile or CAD model and produce another specimen. Order subsequent
parts from the verified model revision; this result does not automatically call for a different printer
or a bulk parts order.

СтраницаPage 80 · Motion fundamentals: leg constraints and
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M05  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Motion fundamentals: leg constraints and
equilibrium

Required, within the 75 hours. Use 1 h from hours 41-42 and 2 h of the hours 51-60 practical
work on the leg design load case. Use the existing task 3 assembly and task 7 diagrams. No new
equipment or motor experiment is required. Before starting, check yourself: identify the three joint
axes and convert mass 0.20 kg into weight 1.962 N at g=9.81 m/s².

Freedom of motion requires correctly specified constraints
An open chain of three independent revolute joints with a fixed base has three degrees of freedom.
Its configuration is q=(q₁,q₂,q₃). Constraining a part sketch does not immobilise the assembly. If
joints are locked by a fixture in a static test, additional constraints and their reactions are
introduced. This is a different mechanical problem from a free leg; friction in an unpowered
actuator is no substitute for a specified constraint.

Free-body model of one link
For an illustrative special case of task 7, use one horizontal rigid link with L=0.12 m, m=0.20 kg
and its centre of mass at L/2. The fixed coordinate frame originates at the left joint; x points right, y
up, and positive moments are anticlockwise. Friction and acceleration are absent. The environment
applies an upward force f_ext=(0;2) N at the right end; weight acts downward. These are exercise
values, not a test load for a printed specimen.
Mentally isolate the link. Replace the base with reactions R_x,R_y and the fixture's holding torque
τ_hold. The environmental force produces moment +L·2=+0.240 N·m; weight produces moment
−(L/2)mg=−0.11772 N·m. The sum of moments without the fixture is positive, so the free link will
not remain horizontal.
Equilibrium requires τ_hold+0.240−0.11772=0, giving τ_hold=−0.12228 N·m. Force balance gives
R_x=0 and R_y+2−1.962=0: R_y=−0.038 N. Here a negative reaction is admissible for a bilateral
attachment to the rig; unilateral floor contact cannot realise every calculated force.

Why the Jacobian also appears in statics
For this link at q=0, J=(0,L)ᵀ. Work done by the external force during a small rotation is
f_extᵀδp=f_extᵀJδq, so the corresponding generalised torque is Jᵀf_ext=+0.240 N·m. Holding torque
balances it together with the moment of weight. In M05 this is a fixture reaction; in an
actuated-joint model, an actuator may fulfil this role. Here f_ext is the environment's force on the
robot; its sign cannot change while its definition remains the same.

Two deliverables for CAD and the test fixture
1. Mark on the assembly which motions each joint permits and which the fixture prevents. Save
two diagrams: the free 3-DOF leg and the restrained test pose. For task 7, identify the physical
component that transmits each holding torque.
2. Repeat force and moment balance for the three poses already selected, expressing lever arms
and forces in one coordinate frame. Check the moment using both r×f and Jᵀf for a simple link.
Save a reaction table with units and a load-transfer sketch. A geometrically admissible pose does
not establish the structure's ability to sustain load; deflection, strength and dynamics require
separate checks.
Assigned reading: Lynch, Park, Modern Robotics: §2.2, Degrees of Freedom of a Robot; §5.2,
Statics of Open Chains. Compare the book's sign for force acting on the environment with the f_ext
convention used here.

Why a robot needs a separate controller

M6 • 25 Feb 2027 - 22 Mar 2027 • 75 hours

Outcome of the month
Create an ESP32-S3 controller that polls an IMU and encoder, transmits consistent measurement
snapshots, limits the control signal and enters a predefined, tested state on a fault. This forms the
basis of the electronics for a leg or finger: the computer may delay a message, while the local
controller must determine whether measurements are fresh and operation may continue. Deliver
firmware, a wiring diagram, bus traces, cycle-timing measurements and a record of injected faults.
Completing the module requires demonstrated controller operation on a physical test rig.

What to bring from previous months
Use the M1 telemetry format and error handling, circuit and measurement fundamentals from the
electrical modules, and the M5 leg CAD model for sensor placement and cable routing. Entry check:
explain voltage relative to common ground, an input versus a power output, the purpose of a
pull-up and encoder-angle units. Find the power circuit and pins reserved for USB, memory and
boot configuration in your exact board's documentation. If this is still difficult, include the review in
the first 2 hours, before connecting external circuits.
The minimum physical setup depends on available components: ESP32-S3, one compatible IMU, an
angle source or encoder, a button, a protected low-power output indicator and measuring
equipment. Check exact models first; select components according to their specifications.
Temporarily replace a missing sensor with a packet generator that keeps the same interface. This
demonstrates program logic, but the hardware item remains open in the final report until measured
on a real device.

Scope and connection to robots
M6 does not require moving a loaded leg or assembling the entire robot. Test the enable output on
a low-power load; the motor rig and its limits belong to M7. The same mechanisms will detect
missing finger feedback in a hand, or interrupted angle and IMU updates on a walking platform.
Software inhibition of a command and independent removal of energy are separate checks. A
stopping circuit must account for the fact that removing power from a real vertical axis can cause it
to fall; here, test its electrical logic on the rig.
Preparing verification evidence for G1 is part of this work. The G1 integration review itself has a
separate 35 hours in the overall plan and is excluded from these 75 hours. Take all hardware limits
from the selected components' documentation and the load calculation; the exercise frequencies
below define a measurement scenario, rather than a safe operating regime for the future robot.

Organising 75 hours and the test rig

Four work blocks
Block A, hours 1-20: 10 hours of GPIO, PWM, ADC, timer and memory theory; 10 hours of wiring,
signal measurement and interrupt practice. Block B, 21-40: 10 hours of protocols and 10 hours of
IMU, encoder and robust communication work. Block C, 41-60: 10 hours of task scheduling and 10
hours of cycle-time variation (jitter) measurement, queue checks and watchdog testing. Block D,
61-75: 5 hours of fault analysis and 10 hours of integration tests. This gives exactly 35 hours of
study and analysis plus 40 hours of practice.
Split each 10 hours of theory into five 2-hour sessions: 35 minutes reading the relevant section, 35
minutes drawing or calculating, 40 minutes on a small verification example and 10 minutes of
notes. Schedule ten-hour practical blocks on Sundays; divide them into stages with breaks and
count the 10 hours as active work. Split the final 5 analysis hours into 2+2+1. Calendar boundaries
may overlap adjacent modules; retain rest days, holidays and G1 from the overall plan. Complete
numbered steps during available study hours without counting any hours twice.

Deliverable structure
Create firmware/ for ESP-IDF, host/ for the Python decoder, config/ for pin assignments and limits,
tests/ for frames and state transitions, evidence/ for traces, and plots/ for graphs. In README, state
board model, revision, SDK version, build and flashing commands, external power wiring and each
sensor type. Keep raw measurements separate from processed plots, so errors can be traced to the
device or script. For every run, record run_id, firmware hash, configuration, start time and workload
type.

Change one thing at a time
In each hardware experiment, change one parameter: bus frequency, polling period, queue depth
or logging load. Before starting, record the expected effect and termination condition. Afterwards,
record actual frame count, errors and missed deadlines. If a trace is unclear, return to the last
reproducible configuration. Do not change wiring, firmware and communication speed
simultaneously and then claim to have identified the cause. Use separate commits for the working
baseline and deliberate fault injection.
Take the first wiring photograph with ground, power, data lines and enable output labelled. In the
log, distinguish “physically measured”, “verified by a software test” and “awaiting hardware
verification”. This allows work to continue while components are delayed, followed by the
remaining hardware checks.

СтраницаPage 83 · GPIO, PWM and ADC: signals in a real robot
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

GPIO, PWM and ADC: signals in a real robot

What to study
Study GPIO modes: input, output, open drain, pull-up/pull-down and active level. For PWM, relate
frequency, period and duty cycle: duty=high-level time/period. For ADC, distinguish raw code, pin
voltage and the physical quantity measured by the sensor. Resolution alone does not guarantee
accuracy: know the permissible input range, calibrate the channel and assess noise. Read the
board pin table and GPIO restrictions in the ESP-IDF GPIO reference; check PWM parameters in the
ESP-IDF LEDC reference. A motor or coil is not an ordinary GPIO load.

Task 1. Button-controlled motion enable
The aim is to verify operator enable for a local joint controller. Initial conditions: a low-power
indicator replaces the actuator, and the active-level circuit is explicitly known. 1. Create an
input/state/output table. 2. Configure a safe electrical state before application startup. 3.
Implement time-based debouncing while retaining raw events for analysis. 4. Perform 30 presses
and releases, including short presses and holds. Save the diagram, log and state-machine test.
Check for one confirmed action per press and no accidental enable at startup. Fault: a
disconnected button wire must not be interpreted as a new start command.

Task 2. Check the control pulse
The aim is to check whether the software command matches the physical signal. Use only a
protected test output. 1. Select frequency and resolution within peripheral limits. 2. Apply several
duty-cycle values within the API's permitted range. 3. Capture at least 100 periods per mode with
an analyser or oscilloscope. 4. Calculate mean, minimum and maximum period and duty deviation.
Save the trace and a table of commands and measured values. Separately test zero command and
an invalid parameter; the driver must report failure rather than silently retaining the previous
active output.

Task 3. Analogue diagnostic channel
This task prepares for supply-voltage or current measurement, initially using a known permissible
test signal. Record the channel transfer function and units. Collect a series with constant input,
calculate mean and standard deviation, then change the signal to at least three points across the
range and compare with independent measurements. Save conversion coefficients, calibration
residuals and a saturation flag. For a signal outside the measurable range, the program marks data
invalid rather than substituting a plausible value. Never apply an ADC voltage outside your exact
board's limits.

Experiment references: GPIO, PWM. Use the configuration and API error sections for your pinned ESP-IDF
version.

СтраницаPage 84 · Timers, memory and interrupt handlers
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Timers, memory and interrupt handlers

Essential theory for reliable firmware
Distinguish a hardware timer, the system tick and elapsed-time measurement. Schedule periodic
polling from its expected time, otherwise execution duration is added to every period. Learn which
operations are permitted in an ISR, how to pass an event to a task, and why logging or waiting for a
lock in a handler increases latency. Check the available ESP-IDF APIs in the documentation for the
chosen version. A pointer to a local array cannot be used after that array's lifetime ends; volatile
provides neither atomicity nor synchronisation between cores and tasks.

Task 4. Timestamp an encoder event
The aim is to associate joint angle with measurement time, rather than USB packet reception time.
Begin with a pulse generator or available encoder. 1. Define a sequence with a known edge count.
2. In the ISR, save only the minimum: a count or timestamp and a task notification. 3. Process and
transmit data outside the ISR. 4. Compare received events with the original trace. Deliver an
interval plot, lost-event count and an explanation of counter overflow. Increase frequency until an
error is detected, within the electrical rig's capabilities; the resulting limit applies to this
configuration.

Task 5. Who owns the measurement snapshot?
The aim is to prevent memory overwrites from making angle and IMU readings refer to different
times. Create a Snapshot structure with seq, sample time, measurement fields and validity bits. 1.
First reproduce the error in a computer test: the producer changes a shared buffer and the
consumer reads it later. 2. Pass the snapshot by value through a queue, or use buffers with explicit
ownership. 3. Populate fields with related check values and verify that slowing the consumer does
not produce mixed snapshots. Save the integrity test and data-lifetime description. Define
queue-overflow behaviour in advance and add a loss counter.

Stack, heap and limited resources
Fix queue sizes and estimate memory per snapshot. Measure the minimum remaining task stack
with the SDK's available tools after the highest-load test, rather than just after startup. Check
memory-allocation failure and driver reinitialisation paths. Do not add dynamic allocation to a
frequent loop without a reason; begin with bounded structures. State units and clock type for every
timeout. Test timer-counter overflow using artificial values in a computer test rather than waiting
for it on the board. The report must distinguish the largest measured latency from a proven
real-time guarantee.

Experiment references: timer, encoder. Use the configuration and API error sections for your pinned ESP-IDF
version.

СтраницаPage 85 · Buses and packets: IMU, encoder and
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Buses and packets: IMU, encoder and
computer

Interfaces to study
UART: baud rate, character format, message boundaries, complete and partial frames. I2C:
address, register operations, ACK/NACK, pull-ups and timeout. SPI: CS, CPOL/CPHA, bit order and
register reads. Study CAN and RS-485 in terms of transceiver role, topology and termination; do not
confuse CAN arbitration with shared-channel management in RS-485. Implementing all five
physical buses within the month is unnecessary: primary computer communication and one real
sensor interface are required; reinforce the others by interpreting traces and drawing a small
circuit.

Task 6. Identify the sensor from its trace
The aim is to confirm that data comes from the intended IMU and is decoded correctly. Inputs: the
installed sensor's datasheet, identification register and measurement format. 1. Check power and
logic levels. 2. Read the identifier and range settings. 3. Capture a transaction with the analyser
and manually label address, direction, data and acknowledgement. 4. Convert bytes to a number,
accounting for signedness and byte order. Save an annotated trace and a calculation converting
the raw value to physical units. Fault: an incorrect address or broken line must produce a timeout
and missing-data status, rather than an endless wait.

Task 7. A telemetry frame that can resynchronise
Design a bounded-length frame: start marker or boundary encoding, version, length, seq,
timestamp, payload and checksum. Choose a CRC algorithm from a documented implementation
and state its parameters; a simple sum has different error-detection properties. 1. Write encoding
and decoding code on the computer. 2. Feed the stream one byte at a time and in random chunks.
3. Add a missing byte, junk before a frame, incorrect length and an altered checksum. 4. Connect
the same decoder to the board. Acceptance: no damaged frame in the fixed test set is accepted,
and the next intact frame is recovered without restarting.

Throughput and units
Estimate traffic before flashing firmware: frame bytes × frames per second plus the chosen
transport's overhead. Compare the calculation with the actual trace and retain capacity for
diagnostics. For each field, state SI unit, sign, range and invalid flag; do not mix rad/s and deg/s.
For the encoder, separately state counts per revolution, accounting for decoding mode and
gearbox. An open computer connection does not make the last value fresh: assess measurement
freshness from sample time and sequence number.

Experiment references: UART, I2C, SPI. Use the configuration and API error sections for your pinned ESP-IDF
version.

СтраницаPage 86 · FreeRTOS: measuring timing behaviour
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

FreeRTOS: measuring timing behaviour

Separate responsibilities
Divide the work into four functions: sensor reading, state and enable checks, telemetry
transmission and service diagnostics. Assign priorities according to the consequences of delay,
rather than code size. First achieve predictable execution with a small number of tasks; introduce
core pinning only after measurement. Read the differences in ESP-IDF FreeRTOS and its
critical-section rules in ESP-IDF FreeRTOS: Critical Sections. A queue transfers data, a mutex
protects a shared resource, and a notification signals an event; choose the mechanism to suit
communication and synchronisation requirements.

Task 8. Measure period, latency and deadline
Choose an exercise period T, for example 10 ms for the first low-power rig, then justify it using
sensor frequency and permitted communication time. The planned start of cycle k is t0+kT. Record
actual start s_k and finish e_k: start jitter=s_k-(t0+kT), execution time=e_k-s_k. A deadline is
missed if completion occurs after the selected deadline. 1. Capture a baseline run. 2. Repeat with
intensive logging and a slowed receiver. 3. Compare p50, p95, p99, maximum and missed-deadline
count over equal numbers of cycles. Save raw timestamps, configuration and plots. An average
must not hide a rare, large outlier.

Task 9. Queue overflow without losing control
The aim is to keep updating joint state while USB communication is slow. Create a fixed-length
queue and two modes: full data recording for a rig experiment, or retaining only the latest state for
monitoring. Each mode needs its own explicitly described loss policy. Slow the consumer enough to
guarantee the queue fills. Check maximum occupancy, dropped_count, seq ordering and time to
detect stale data. Firmware must not wait indefinitely for queue space in a task responsible for
inhibiting the output. Save the observed limit together with test duration.

Task 10. Test the watchdog
Study the interrupt watchdog and task watchdog in ESP-IDF Watchdogs. On the low-power rig,
deliberately block a selected task in a separate test build and record the reset cause. Measure the
enable output using an independent channel before reset and after boot. Acceptance: restarting
must not restore active enable from a saved command; a new explicit start procedure is required
after successful checks. Watchdog servicing must reflect the health of critical functions, rather than
run unconditionally from an unrelated timer. Separately stop the computer process: this is a
communication failure, not necessarily a failure of the MCU itself.

СтраницаPage 87 · Integrated rig and fault state machine
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Integrated rig and fault state machine

controller-io v1 specification
Rig inputs: IMU, encoder angle or count, operator command and electrical-limit sensors where
available. Outputs: telemetry snapshot, diagnostic events and test-channel enable. Initial mode
BOOT validates configuration and moves to DISARMED. Only an explicit start command with all
conditions satisfied enters ARMED. Loss of valid measurements, violation of a monitored limit or
E-stop enters FAULT. Removing the cause does not by itself enter ARMED. Recovery proceeds
through a confirmed fault reset and DISARMED.

Task 11. Transition table and its code checks
Inputs are the lists of events, states and physical outputs. 1. For every state/event pair, specify the
next state, reason code and channel enable. 2. Implement a pure transition function that can be
tested on the computer. 3. Issue commands out of order: start during a fault, repeated reset,
connection restored without confirmation. 4. Compare actual telemetry with the table. Save the
table, tests and logs for at least five event sequences. Check that no path leads from BOOT or
FAULT to ARMED without the required conditions and a new operator action.

Task 12. Independent stop
Draw the energy path from source to test load separately from the software command path.
Identify a component capable of stopping the energy supply independently of the normal MCU
loop; select it from the load and circuit documentation. First test its function on a low-power
equivalent. Then hold the program in a deliberate test hang and activate the physical stop. Deliver
the circuit, output measurement and recovery procedure. Measure time from the physical event to
cessation of the test signal and compare it with the rig requirement set in advance. This test does
not assign an industrial safety rating to a homemade system.

Configuration and reset during supply loss
Store configuration with a schema version and range validation. Do not save ARMED as a state that
restores automatically. For NVS, study initialisation, writing and errors in ESP-IDF NVS. Test a
corrupt or unknown format on a data copy: loading invalid limits must inhibit enable. Test power
reset by controllably disconnecting an appropriate source with a low-power load, rather than by
short-circuiting it. After power returns, the log shows the restart cause, configuration is checked
again and motion enable remains absent. Actual power-stage tolerance of voltage dips is tested
later with the specific M7 actuator.

СтраницаPage 88 · Test matrix and verification criteria
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Test matrix and verification criteria

Input-data failures
Test F1: disconnect the IMU. Record the last valid snapshot time, timeout and removal of enable.
Choose the freshness threshold from the expected update period and the rig's acceptable delay.
Test F2: corrupt frame and false length. The decoder rejects the packet without reading beyond the
buffer, increments a counter and recovers the next valid frame. Test F3: a stuck encoder value
while packet sequence numbers continue. Demonstrate the difference between fresh data and a
physically plausible measurement; without a motion model, a constant value alone does not prove
a fault.

Execution and recovery failures
Test F4: the telemetry receiver stops reading. Logging drops data according to the selected policy
while freshness checks and channel shutdown continue; measure response latency. Test F5: the
monitored task is blocked. The watchdog triggers in the test build, the reset cause is included in
the report, and the controller remains DISARMED after boot. Test F6: E-stop while the MCU is hung.
The independent circuit switches off the test output; releasing the button does not restart it. For
F5/F6, capture the physical output, because “FAULT” in the console does not prove the signal has
stopped.

Configuration and timing boundaries
Test F7: configuration contains a negative period, unknown version or nonnumeric coefficient. Each
cause has clear diagnostics; reject the entire configuration or apply it using predefined
atomic-update rules. Test F8: power restart while ARMED with a low-power load. A new enable is
required after startup. Test F9: artificial counter overflow and two frames with the same seq.
Statistical counters must not report negative age, and duplicates must not conceal missing new
measurements. Test F10: ADC measurement reaches the range boundary; the program reports
saturation rather than inferring an exact current value.

How to record each result
For every scenario, record circuit and firmware versions, initial state, fault-injection method,
expected transition, measured times, filenames and outcome: pass, fail or “not physically verified”.
Repeat critical transitions several times and retain their variability; one successful reset does not
characterise reliability. For each timing metric, state its start, end and measurement clock. Do not
subtract PC and MCU timestamps without synchronisation or an offset estimate. If an instrument is
unavailable, the computer test remains useful, but leave the physical-latency item open.

СтраницаPage 89 · Work sequence: hours 1-40
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Work sequence: hours 1-40

Hours 1-10: read and design
1-2: describe rig components and parameters; check pin assignments, levels and unused pins.
Draw the power path and initial output state. 3-4: study GPIO and PWM signals, calculate period
and duty cycle, and select measurable modes. 5-6: cover ADC and unit conversion; tabulate raw
and converted values. 7-8: study timers and ISR; draw an event-timestamp-task-packet timing
diagram. 9-10: understand snapshot memory and queues; write a shared-buffer overwrite scenario.
Finish the block with an interface design and a list of expected measurements.

Hours 11-20: first practical block
11-12: assemble and test the button with protected indicator; save photographs and the task 1
state table. 13-14: perform task 2 PWM measurements, including invalid configuration. 15-16:
collect task 3 analogue series and plot calibration. 17-18: measure task 4 edges and move
processing out of the ISR. 19-20: correct snapshot ownership in task 5, add a bounded queue and
save the working baseline. Allocate the final 15 minutes of every two-hour step to documenting
results; those minutes are included in the stated time.

Hours 21-30: data and protocols
21-22: study UART and frame boundaries; estimate required throughput. 23-24: study I2C and the
specific IMU's registers; manually decode an example transaction. 25-26: study SPI and compare
clocking modes with the sensor datasheet; do not connect a new sensor before checking levels.
27-28: create a comparative diagram of UART, I2C, SPI, CAN and RS-485: lines, addressing,
shared-medium access, transceiver and termination. 29-30: design framing, CRC and
resynchronisation rules; prepare a fixed set of damaged messages and expected responses.

Hours 31-40: the complete sensor path
31-32: read IMU identification and measurements; verify axes and sign. 33-34: capture and
annotate task 6 traces; compare raw values and SI conversions. 35-36: implement task 7 frame
reception with partial reads. 37-38: inject corruption, disconnect and reconnect the sensor; remove
indefinite waits. 39-40: perform an extended run in the chosen mode and compare frame count
and traffic volume with calculations. Save the second baseline as baseline-2 and describe its
limitations. If new hardware is unavailable, use a test-data generator and label these steps as
software work, rather than a completed physical sensor path.

СтраницаPage 90 · Work sequence: hours 41-75
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Work sequence: hours 41-75

Hours 41-50: timing, resources and faults
41-42: read the FreeRTOS task model and ESP-IDF differences; draw dependencies and selected
priorities. 43-44: allocate available time within a cycle and define task 8 metrics; choose frequency
from the sensor and available communication. 45-46: compare queues, notifications and mutexes
for your data; examine slow logging. 47-48: study watchdogs and reset causes; define testable
boot behaviour. 49-50: study configuration storage and separate recovery after power loss into
distinct states. Do not spend these hours optimising code before obtaining measurements.

Hours 51-60: measurement practical
51-52: implement periodic scheduling and timestamp recording. 53-54: perform the task 8 baseline
run and repeat under load; produce distribution plots. 55-56: overflow the queue in task 9 and
compare the selected policies. 57-58: inject the task 10 hang in a separate build and observe the
physical output during reset. 59-60: check restart, memory and configuration; fix one identified
cause of deadline misses and repeat only the affected experiment. Finish the block by stating
measured limits, test durations and what remains unproven.

Hours 61-65: five hours of analysis
61-62: analyse rig hazards. For each, identify the energy source, failure event, possible
consequence, preventive measure and an observable check of that measure's operation. 63-64:
complete the task 11 state-machine table and task 12 independent-path diagram; verify that
hardware and software stops do not depend on the same hung task. 65: prepare the acceptance
sequence, initial states and record forms. This 2+2+1 split retains the overall 35/40 balance and
adds no hours to the programme.

Hours 66-75: final rig block
66-67: integrate the state machine, measurement-freshness checks and configuration validation.
68-69: perform F1-F3 and F7; compare messages with the transition table. 70-71: perform F4-F5
and check latency under load. 72-73: independently verify F6/F8 on a low-power load and test
recovery; check completeness of timestamps and raw traces. 74-75: reproduce the project from a
clean build, make a short demonstration video and assemble the G1 package. Explicitly state any
hardware check not completed. You may omit a second transport prototype, an extended PC
interface and extra plots; the fault design, primary sensor path and prevention of automatic restart
are compulsory.

Acceptance, self-check and handover to M7

Completion conditions
First: firmware builds from the instructions and starts without active output enable. Second: one
real IMU and angle-measurement source have documented formats, units and timestamps;
temporary substitutes are explicitly marked. Third: physical traces of the primary communication
path and damaged-frame checks are available. Fourth: cycle period, jitter, execution time and
missed deadlines have been measured under a described workload. Fifth: watchdog, lost
communication and E-stop do not cause automatic restart after recovery. Sixth: the independent
stopping path has been verified from the physical output, and the limits configuration cites the
source of every value.
Set numerical requirements for frequency, timeouts and time to remove the test signal before the
experiment, based on the rig's purpose. Place requirement, measurement, instrument, conditions
and conclusion side by side in the final table. Where evidence is missing, “not completed” is more
useful than an average without its source. Before G1, prepare the revision-labelled circuit,
photographs, repository, tests, raw measurements, plots, failed-case log and list of unverified
hardware assumptions.

Questions for oral review
1. Why does volatile not resolve a race between ISR and task? 2. How does measurement age differ
from packet age? 3. Where should a timeout occur if the IMU does not respond? 4. Why does CRC
not establish the physical plausibility of an angle? 5. What happens to the output while the
bootloader runs? 6. Why must watchdog servicing depend on critical tasks? 7. How can p99 look
good despite a dangerous single outlier? 8. What exactly does the physical stop switch off during a
program hang? 9. Which data may be restored from NVS? 10. Why does power restoration not
mean permission to resume motion?
Answer each question using your own circuit, test or trace. If your answer uses only library
terminology, create a physical example: a missing finger-angle measurement, a stale leg command
or USB overloaded by logging. Connecting a cause to its observable effect is this month's central
skill.

What the next module needs
Pass the working controller, measurement and command interfaces, timeout list, reset log, fault
state machine and independent-stop circuit to M7. Adding a real actuator requires new current,
thermal and mechanical limits; low-power rig values do not transfer automatically. The completed
interface will support actuator-latency measurement and reproducible identification experiments.
Save release controller-io-v1 and the list of required hardware checks separately from subsequent
control changes.

Assigned reading: a focused reading route

Read only the specified sections before the corresponding experiment. Most literature is in English;
keep explanations, the glossary and the report in English for this edition. Reading and preparation
are included in the existing 75 hours; you do not need to work through entire books.

Core reading and limits on transfer
1. Jonathan W. Valvano, Embedded Systems: Introduction to ARM Cortex-M
Microcontrollers. Chapters 4, 6, 9-11: input/output, pointers and data structures, interrupts and
real time, analogue interfaces, communication. For tasks 1-7, read the principles; do not apply
Cortex-M register descriptions to ESP32-S3 or buy a TI development board for the book.
2. Richard Barry / FreeRTOS, Mastering the FreeRTOS Real Time Kernel. Current online
book: chapters 4, 5, 7: Task Management, Queue Management, Interrupt Management. Tasks 8-9
need task states, queues and deferred ISR event processing. Older PDFs use different numbering;
follow these chapter titles.
3. Edward A. Lee, Sanjit A. Seshia, Introduction to Embedded Systems, 2nd ed. (2017).
Chapter 3 Discrete Dynamics; chapter 11 Multitasking. Read selectively on finite-state machines
and concurrent tasks. For task 10, draw the fault-machine transitions; for the queue, explain the
race and data ownership. Full formal verification of the controller is outside this module.

Documentation instead of API guesses
ESP-IDF FreeRTOS. Tasks, SMP Scheduler, Critical Sections. After the book, compare the specific
ESP-IDF implementation: stack-size units, cores and locks. Select the reference version matching
the project's pinned version.
Failure and recovery. Watchdogs: IWDT, TWDT, JTAG and NVS: Read, Write and Erase; Error
Handling. For task 10, check hangs, restarts and corrupted configuration; ARMED must not restore
automatically.
Buses and peripherals. Links for GPIO, LEDC, timer, UART, I2C, SPI and PCNT appear on the
relevant practical pages. Add your IMU's datasheet: registers, units, byte order and access
conditions.
Reading deliverables. Prepare a pin diagram, a task-period table, a buffer-ownership diagram
and a fault state machine. Every document should explain an actual trace or reproducible failure.

СтраницаPage 93 · Glossary: terms and definitions
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Glossary: terms and definitions

Microcontroller (MCU). A chip containing processor, memory and peripherals for direct device
control; ESP32-S3 uses Xtensa cores.
GPIO. A programmable general-purpose digital pin; the controller and board circuit determine its
mode, permissible voltage and functions.
Interrupt. An event that invokes a handler outside normal task execution; service latency
depends on priorities and blocking.
ISR. An interrupt service routine with bounded execution time and restricted permitted operations;
it usually delegates lengthy processing to a task.
Timer. A hardware or software mechanism for measuring time; a hardware counter and software
handler have different sources of delay.
Jitter. Variation in start times or operation duration relative to a selected reference; measured in
units of time, such as microseconds.
Deadline. The time by which a computation or action must finish; a miss is defined by system
requirements, rather than average performance.
RTOS task. An independent execution context with a stack and state; the scheduler selects a
ready task according to priorities.
Queue. A bounded buffer for passing messages between contexts; overflow and waiting require an
explicitly selected policy.
Data race. Unsynchronised concurrent access to shared memory involving a write; the result may
depend on execution order.
Critical section. Code accessing shared state protected by a coordinated synchronisation
mechanism; its duration affects system latency.
DMA. Transfer between peripherals and memory without per-item processor copying; buffer
ownership and transfer completion must be coordinated.
UART. An asynchronous serial interface with agreed baud rate and character format; the protocol
specifies message boundaries separately.
I2C. An addressed synchronous bus with SDA data and SCL clock lines; its electrical
implementation requires checks of pull-ups, capacitance and levels.
SPI. A synchronous serial interface with clock and device selection; mode, bit order and
transaction boundaries must match the sensor.
CRC. A check code for detecting specified transmission errors; it provides neither sender
authenticity nor protection against intentional substitution.
Data age. Time from acquisition of a physical measurement to its use, including transmission,
queues and processing.
Watchdog. A mechanism detecting the absence of expected evidence of operation; a controller
restart does not guarantee a safe power-stage state.
Finite-state machine. A model with a finite set of states and defined event-driven transitions,
useful for enabling operation and handling faults.
NVS. Nonvolatile value storage with an access API; configuration needs a version and validity
checks after loading.

Equipment, installation and readiness checks

Complete preparation within the first study blocks in place of a repeated general overview. The
total remains 75 hours; waiting for delivery is excluded. The statuses below identify actions for you
to take, rather than purchases or installations already completed.

USE EXISTING EQUIPMENT AND BUY BEFORE THE PRACTICAL
Reuse the Mac M4, multimeter, supply, breadboard, wiring and M04 low-power load. Buy: 2
boards ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 of one verified revision: the first is the controller, the second a pulse
generator and packet-exchange device. Check Flash, PSRAM, circuit and pins reserved for USB and
boot configuration.
1 IMU breakout module: access to raw three-axis accelerometer and gyroscope data,
documented registers, I2C and/or SPI, an accessible interrupt line, and supply and logic levels
compatible with 3.3 V. Check driver support for ESP32-S3, the chosen interface and ESP-IDF
version. If you already have such a sensor, do not buy another. A sensor providing only processed
angles does not replace access to raw channels.
1 logic analyser: at least 8 digital channels, inputs suitable for the chosen levels, UART/I2C/SPI
decoders and a sample rate with margin for the bus being studied. An example is Saleae Logic 8;
check Apple Silicon software before ordering. 1 USB set: two data cables with connectors
matching the boards, an adapter or hub if needed, probes with common ground and connectors.

INSTALL NOW - macOS ARM
Start with PlatformIO IDE for VS Code: build, upload and monitor a simple project. Then use
ESP-IDF, official Get Started for target esp32s3 with compatible CMake, Ninja and compiler tools.
Pin versions; the PlatformIO espressif32 platform version and ESP-IDF framework version are
different fields and their compatibility requires a separate check.
Add KiCad for macOS for the wiring diagram and electrical checks, and software for your exact
analyser, for example Logic 2 for Saleae. A sigrok-compatible instrument may need PulseView;
check ARM and USB support before purchase. Logic 2 does not support arbitrary analysers. Use
Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 in UTM only after separately checking USB; the main build and measurement
route is native Mac.

INSTALLATION CHECK
On both boards, perform build→flash→monitor, hardware reset and firmware-version reading. Then
test UART loopback or communication between boards, measure PWM, perform one I2C or SPI
transaction with the IMU and export the trace. Verify raw-count units and monotonic time. Open the
circuit in KiCad and run ERC; save environment versions and the pin-assignment diagram.
Optional, for later: STM32 only for a separate comparison; the motor with encoder is purchased
in M07. In M06 an existing encoder can be the angle source, and the second board can generate
quadrature pulses. The generator tests the interface; required real sensor measurements remain
separate acceptance items.

СтраницаPage 95 · Motion fundamentals: angle, velocity and
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M06  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Motion fundamentals: angle, velocity and
time

Required: connect measurements with motion
The leg controller receives counts, but motion is described by angle q(t) and its change over time.
Before the experiment, explain: 90°=π/2 rad; positive rotation is defined by the oriented joint axis,
and an identical angle in two packets does not prove a stop. In M6, use the available sensor or a
generator on the second ESP32-S3, without a new motor.

Measurement model and worked example
Let c_k be an unwrapped counter without overflow, C the counts per revolution of the measured
shaft after the selected decoding, and t_k the sample time in seconds from one MCU clock. Relative
angle q_k=2π(c_k-c_0)/C, in rad. If the encoder is on the motor, converting to link angle separately
requires a known gear ratio and sign. There is no reduction here.
Exercise data: C=4000, c=(100;104;110), t=(0;0.010;0.025) s. This gives
q=(0;0.006283;0.015708) rad. Interval velocity v_k=(q_k-q_{k-1})/(t_k-t_{k-1}) is 0.628319 rad/s
in both intervals. Dividing the second increment by the nominal 0.010 s gives a false 0.942478
rad/s: interval variation creates the appearance of acceleration.
Finite-difference velocity is the interval average, rather than the exact instantaneous derivative.
One count corresponds to 0.001571 rad; over short windows, quantisation is visible in velocity.
Smoothing reduces noise but introduces delay. USB reception time is no substitute for physical
sampling time: a late, intact packet may contain a stale angle.

One end-to-end experiment for tasks 4, 5 and 8
First reproduce the table on the computer. Then transmit a known A/B sequence from the second
board and compare received edges with the logic analyser. Save counts, sample_time,
receive_time, seq, q and interval v. Plot velocity calculated from actual and nominal intervals.
Adding a constant to every c must not change relative angles.
Repeat with delayed consumer reads and identical timestamps on two frames. Reject a zero or
negative interval before dividing; a stale snapshot does not become fresh because of a new packet.
For example, at constant v=0.628319 rad/s, age 0.05 s means an angle change of 0.031416 rad.
This indicates the error scale, rather than specifying a robot timeout.
Included in the 75 hours: 1 hour from 7-8 for the time model; 1 hour from 17-18 for task 4; 1
hour from 53-54 for task 8 plots. Use their existing traces and report. The generator validates the
signal path; the real angle sensor requires a separate check.
Read selectively: Lee/Seshia, Introduction to Embedded Systems, ch. 3 Discrete Dynamics for
state and samples; ESP-IDF PCNT: Introduction, Channel Actions for A/B counting semantics. Check
the API against the pinned version.
