СтраницаPage 128 · Newton and Euler: forces, torques and inertia
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Newton and Euler: forces, torques and inertia

How to draw a force and torque diagram
For translation of the centre of mass, the sum of external forces equals m·a_COM. For planar
rotation of a rigid link about a fixed axis, sum torques about that axis and use the moment of
inertia about the same axis. In general spatial motion, the rotational equation includes I·ω̇ and the
gyroscopic term ω×(Iω), expressed in a consistent basis. Do not automatically apply the planar
relation τ=Iα to an arbitrary rotating system. The centre of mass is the point whose motion
describes the translational part of the body’s motion; the mass distribution relative to the axes
determines its inertia.

Task 1. Physical parameters of a link
The inputs are the M5 CAD link and available mass measurements. 1. Separate geometry from
material and list the contributions of fasteners and the actuator. 2. Determine mass, COM position
in the local coordinate frame and inertia about the COM. 3. Transfer the inertia to the joint axis
using the parallel-axis theorem; in the planar case, I_joint=I_COM+m·d². 4. Compare with a rod or
point-mass approximation. Deliverable: a parameter table with units and sources. Check: shifting
the axis away from the COM increases inertia by a non-negative amount. Edge case: an incorrect
CAD scale changes inertia more strongly than it changes a linear dimension.

Task 2. Forces and torques on a leg or finger link
Draw one link showing its weight, joint reaction force, actuator torque and an external force at its
endpoint. 1. Choose the point about which you calculate torques. 2. Write down lever arms and
signs. 3. Calculate the holding torque in several known configurations. 4. Check the external-force
torque using τ=JᵀF from M8; calculate the gravitational contribution separately. Deliverable: three
labelled drawings and a torque table. Check: if a force’s line of action passes through the axis, its
torque about that axis is zero. Error to avoid: a link’s mass cannot be added as a force without
multiplying by g.

Energy and units
A single link’s kinetic energy is the sum of 0.5m·v_COM² and 0.5ωᵀI_COMω. Potential energy in a
uniform gravitational field depends on COM height. For two links, add their energies; obtain COM
velocities from the geometry and Jacobians in M8. Prepare a table: length m, mass kg, time s, force
N, torque N·m, energy J, inertia kg·m². Check the dimensions of every term before running a
numerical calculation. Using I for both inertia and electric current in different files is acceptable
only when the context is clear; separate names such as inertia and current are preferable.






























M9 • 03 Jun 2027 - 06 Jul 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          3 / 15
СтраницаPage 129 · One link: its equation and an energy test
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

One link: its equation and an energy test

Task 3. A single-joint pendulum
For clarity, measure θ from the downward vertical. With moment of inertia J about the axis, mass m
and distance c to the COM, a simple model is J·θ̈+b·θ̇+m·g·c·sin(θ)=τ. A convenient zero for
potential energy is the lowest point: V=m·g·c·(1-cosθ). If you use an angle q measured from the
horizontal axis, the gravitational term changes; do not switch conventions without transforming the
coordinates. 1. Derive the gravitational torque from a drawing. 2. Write the state [θ,ω] and its
derivative [ω,α]. 3. Solve the equation for α, then integrate. 4. Compare the initial acceleration
direction with a hand calculation.
Deliverable: angle, velocity and energy plots, plus a configuration that reproduces the calculation.
Check without friction or torque: total energy should be conserved within numerical error, which
you investigate by reducing the step size or tolerances. For a small angle, compare the period with
2π·sqrt(J/(m·g·c)) for positive parameters. Edge cases: the lowest point with zero initial velocity
remains an equilibrium; reject negative mass or zero inertia as an invalid model.

Task 4. Work and dissipation
First disable gravity and apply a constant torque to a link with known inertia J: acceleration should
be τ/J. Then restore gravity and apply a bounded torque pulse. Numerically integrate power P=τ·ω
and compare work with the energy change. Add viscous friction b·ω with b≥0: the dissipated power
b·ω² is non-negative. Save the balance E(t)-E(0)-actuator_work+losses, as well as the q plot. Check:
with zero actuator torque and positive damping, mechanical energy must not systematically
increase. Negative b is a separate artificial test that the validator must reject in a passive model.

The numerical method is part of the experiment
Compare fixed-step integration with the adaptive solve_ivp solver. Record duration, step size,
relative and absolute tolerances, and termination status. Run an experiment with successive
step-size reductions while keeping physical parameters unchanged. Assess both the trajectory and
the energy-balance residual. Similar position plots do not yet establish convergence of force or
acceleration. High velocities and stiff contact will change the integrator requirements; preserve this
basic model without contact for subsequent comparisons.







































M9 • 03 Jun 2027 - 06 Jul 2027 • 75 hours                                                                           4 / 15
СтраницаPage 130 · Lagrange’s equations and the structure of
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Lagrange’s equations and the structure of
two-link dynamics

What to derive
The generalised coordinates q=[q1,q2] uniquely specify the 2R configuration. Measure q1 from the
horizontal x-axis and q2 relative to the first link; use the x-y plane with y upward. Construct the
centre-of-mass positions, differentiate them with respect to time, and calculate kinetic energy K
and potential energy V. The Lagrangian is L=K-V. For each q_i, write d/dt(∂L/∂q̇_i)-∂L/∂q_i=τ_i,
adding external forces and losses separately. A symbolic algebra system can help with derivatives,
but you must be able to explain every energy expression and the choice of signs.

Task 5. Mass matrix and gravity
Use l1,l2 for lengths, c1,c2 for distances from the corresponding joints to the COMs, m1,m2 for
masses, and I1,I2 for planar inertias about the COMs. Extract the structure M(q)·q̈+h(q,q̇)+g(q)=τ
from the equations. For checking: M22=I2+m2·c2², M12=M21=I2+m2·(c2²+l1·c2·cosq2),
M11=I1+I2+m1·c1²+m2·(l1²+c2²+2l1·c2·cosq2). Here h combines the velocity-dependent terms;
an individual matrix C is not unique, so check the vector h first.
1. Obtain M and g from your own derivation. 2. Compare M against an independent implementation
or the structure given above. 3. Check symmetry and positive definiteness in admissible
configurations. 4. Compare gravitational torque with the numerical derivative of V with respect to
q. Deliverable: a computational notebook with the derivation, a numerical function and tests. For
the chosen coordinates, g2=m2·g·c2·cos(q1+q2), while g1 additionally contains
g·(m1·c1+m2·l1)·cosq1. Edge case: all h terms must vanish when q̇=0.

Task 6. Forward and inverse dynamics
The inverse problem takes q,q̇,q̈ and returns the required τ; the forward problem takes q,q̇,τ and
solves a linear system for q̈. 1. Choose several states. 2. Calculate τ using inverse dynamics. 3.
Feed it into forward dynamics and compare the reconstructed acceleration. 4. Repeat with
endpoint forces added through JᵀF in a consistent basis. Save the acceleration reconstruction errors
after the inverse-then-forward calculation. Use solve(M,rhs), not an explicit matrix inverse. This test
does not replace an independent physical check: both functions may contain the same model error.





































M9 • 03 Jun 2027 - 06 Jul 2027 • 75 hours                                                                        5 / 15
СтраницаPage 131 · 2R simulation and checks of physical
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

2R simulation and checks of physical
behaviour

Task 7. Two links without contact
Inputs: validated M,h,g, the M8 geometry, and physically admissible masses and inertias. 1. Run
free motion from a non-zero initial configuration without friction. 2. Plot angles, velocities, the
endpoint path and total energy. 3. Repeat with half the step size or tighter tolerances. 4. Add
damping and bounded torque, checking the work balance. Deliverable: four comparable runs and a
numerical-convergence report. Edge case: with horizontal links and no holding torque, acceleration
must not be zero merely because the initial velocities are zero.

Checking velocity-dependent terms
For the 2R model described above, define a=m2·l1·c2·sin(q2). Then h1=-a·(2q̇1q̇2+q̇2²), h2=a·q̇1².
Compare this with your own derivation and check reversal of velocity direction. Do not remove h
simply because calculations agree with an experiment at low velocity: the error will change as
velocities change. However, a slow-motion model may deliberately neglect some dynamics if this is
an explicit approximation and its error has been checked. Record the velocity range in which the
approximation remains useful.

Application to a leg and hand
Use the 2R model as a planar section of a leg or as two phalanges. For the leg, add the masses of
the relevant parts and actuators mounted on the links; for the finger, specify a different length
scale and fingertip load. Compare gravitational torque and inertial effects for the same normalised
motion. Do not transfer planar-model equations to a complete spatial leg without a new derivation:
the first axis, COM offsets and inertia tensors change the equations. It is sufficient to specify the
interface through which a multibody library will later connect.

An independent numerical reference
Build the same simple mechanism in one tool, such as Drake, MuJoCo or Featherstone’s reference
library. First disable contact and default actuators, and align gravity, masses, COMs, inertias and
initial coordinates. Compare acceleration in one pose before comparing a long trajectory; then
compare energies and a short motion. Disagreement may result from built-in damping, limit stops
or a different coordinate frame. In the comparison report, list the effects that are enabled and
disabled. You need not install several heavyweight simulators for one plot: one independent
reference is enough.






























M9 • 03 Jun 2027 - 06 Jul 2027 • 75 hours                                                                         6 / 15
СтраницаPage 132 · Contact, friction and body support
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Contact, friction and body support

Task 8. Unilateral normal contact
A horizontal surface can exert an upward force on a foot, but cannot attract it towards the floor.
Begin with a vertical mass and a spring-damper model of penetration δ≥0. An illustrative model
force N=max(0,k·δ+c·δ̇) acts only during contact; δ̇ is positive when penetration increases. 1.
Check free fall before touchdown. 2. Add contact and measure maximum penetration. 3. Check the
force sign and absence of tension during lift-off. 4. Compare several k,c values and integrator step
sizes. Deliverable: height, force, energy and the region of numerical stability. These parameters do
not automatically represent the properties of a real foot.

Task 9. Sticking and sliding
In a simple Coulomb description, static tangential force is bounded by |F_t|≤μ_sN; during sliding it
opposes velocity, with a magnitude determined by μ_kN. 1. Place a body on a horizontal plane. 2.
Gradually increase the prescribed horizontal force. 3. Show the transition from sticking to sliding. 4.
Repeat with a different normal load. Deliverable: plots of tangential force, velocity and contact
mode. Check: tangential friction must not systematically add mechanical energy. Edge case N=0:
the contact friction force also vanishes. Smoothing near zero velocity changes the model and must
be explicitly identified.

Impact and discrete time
Compare elastic and inelastic impact with a continuous compliant model. The coefficient of
restitution describes the ratio of normal velocities after and before impact under specified
conditions; it is not a universal material coefficient for every velocity. Do not combine a rigid
impulsive impact with the same energy loss in a damper without checking for double counting. For
the first implementation, explain the two approaches and implement one, then investigate
sensitivity. Force, penetration and energy matter in contact; smooth animation can hide
non-physical high-frequency oscillations.

Task 10. Support polygon
Take known contact points on a horizontal plane and the projection of the body COM. Construct the
convex hull of active contacts and the signed distance from the projection to its boundary: positive
inside and negative outside. Repeat after removing one support and shifting the COM. Deliverable:
support diagrams and the static margin in metres. Check: a point on an edge has zero margin; two
contacts do not form a polygon with non-zero area. This is a quasi-static geometric check under
stated force and friction assumptions, not proof of the dynamic stability of a walking robot.






























M9 • 03 Jun 2027 - 06 Jul 2027 • 75 hours                                                                           7 / 15
СтраницаPage 133 · Validating the M7 model and assessing its
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Validating the M7 model and assessing its
accuracy

Task 11. A joint with real actuator parameters
First establish what M7 identified: mechanics under a known torque, or the response of a servo with
an internal controller to a position command. 1. Import parameters with units, signs and operating
ranges. 2. Check gearing and inertia: do not count the load twice. 3. Replay the measured input in
simulation with the same initial state. 4. Compare q(t) and the available velocities and currents on
a common time axis. Deliverable: overlaid plots, a residual and an explanation of the most
prominent discrepancy. Do not connect a position-command response model as an ideal torque
source: these are different physical interfaces.
If torque is not directly known, validate the available command-to-angle model and state
separately which mechanical properties remain unconfirmed. Current telemetry can support an
explanation of saturation, but does not become an accurate torque measurement without a
coefficient and a definition of the current type. Add heating, friction, backlash and delay from M7
only where their meaning is consistent with the new equation. For each effect, first show a
comparison against the model without it; otherwise you cannot determine what improved the
result.

Task 12. An independent recording and sensitivity
Before fitting parameters, set aside recordings of separate runs for independent validation. 1. Fit
the model on the first group. 2. Freeze the parameters. 3. Predict a new run with a different
admissible command waveform or load. 4. Calculate angle RMSE, maximum residual and
characteristic-time error. Then vary one parameter at a time within its justified uncertainty range
and compare the effects. Deliverable: a sensitivity table and independent-validation plots. If no
new real data are available, perform a software test, but leave physical validation open.

Assessing model errors
Prepare a table of error source, observed effect, required accuracy and refinement method. For
example: COM affects gravitational torque; J affects acceleration; delay shifts the response; friction
affects low velocities; contact k affects penetration and peak force. Allocate time to the parameters
that most strongly affect the result of interest. State numerical integration error and measurement
noise separately. The aim is the smallest model adequate for the chosen experiment, rather than
the largest number of parameters. The report must identify admissible operating conditions and
specific examples where the model ceases to be reliable.

СтраницаPage 134 · Step by step: hours 1-40
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Step by step: hours 1-40

Hours 1-10: physical terminology and diagrams
1-2: check units, gravity and the coordinate frame, and assemble the parameter table from M5-M8.
3-4: study mass, COM and inertia, and transfer inertia to a joint axis for a simple body. 5-6: draw
force and torque diagrams for a link and leg, and calculate static torques. 7-8: work through kinetic
and potential energy and the work done by torque. 9-10: derive the pendulum equation for the
chosen angle and define states and initial conditions. These ten hours do not require a complex
simulation: their outputs are checkable equations and physically expected relationships.

Hours 11-20: one link as a test system
11-12: finish the parameter table for task 1 and check the provenance of CAD mass and inertia.
13-14: complete the drawings and calculations for task 2 and compare against JᵀF. 15-16:
implement the pendulum in task 3 and plot q,ω,E. 17-18: complete the energy balance in task 4
with torque and friction. 19-20: investigate the integrator step size and compare small oscillations
against the analytical period. Freeze baseline-one-link with its inputs, method and achieved
accuracy. If energy grows without a source, fix the model before moving to the second link.

Hours 21-30: the two-link system
21-22: write the 2R centre-of-mass coordinates and their velocities using the M8 geometry. 23-24:
construct K,V,L and derive Lagrange’s equations. 25-26: extract the mass matrix,
velocity-dependent terms and gravity. 27-28: study the meaning of forward and inverse dynamics
and work through adding an external force. 29-30: prepare checks of M symmetry, positive energy,
the derivative of V and limiting cases. If using a symbolic tool, preserve the original energy
expressions and the meanings of variables, as well as the final long formula.

Hours 31-40: validated 2R dynamics
31-32: implement M,h,g for task 5 and compare with your own derivation. 33-34: check the
inverse-then-forward dynamics calculation in task 6 using fixed and random admissible states.
35-36: run the contact-free simulation in task 7 and its energy checks. 37-38: add bounded torque
and friction, and repeat the convergence check. 39-40: compare instantaneous acceleration and a
short trajectory with one independent library. If installation is taking too long, use an available
reference implementation; do not reduce unit and energy checks to accommodate a simulator
interface.

































M9 • 03 Jun 2027 - 06 Jul 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          9 / 15
СтраницаPage 135 · Step by step: hours 41-75
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Step by step: hours 41-75

Hours 41-50: contact physics
41-42: study unilateral normal force, penetration, and the difference between rigid and compliant
contact. 43-44: work through the friction cone and the transition from sticking to sliding, and draw
admissible forces. 45-46: study impact, the coefficient of restitution and energy losses. 47-48:
assess the effects of contact stiffness, damping and integration step separately; prepare a
parameter grid for comparison. 49-50: study the support polygon and static margin, and record
their conditions of applicability. Relate every concept to an observable force, velocity or energy.

Hours 51-60: contact experiments
51-52: implement the vertical contact in task 8; check the absence of force before touchdown and
at lift-off. 53-54: vary k,c and the numerical step, recording penetration and energy. 55-56:
complete the sticking-to-sliding transition in task 9 and check the sign of frictional power. 57-58:
construct several support configurations for task 10, remove a contact and move the COM. 59-60:
add simple endpoint contact to the 2R mechanism or leg in the chosen simulator and explain how it
differs from a geometric check. If time is limited, retain point contact, while preserving the
unilaterality and sensitivity checks.

Hours 61-65: model validation plan
61-62: revisit M7 identification and align the input type, delay, gearing and load inertia with the M9
model. 63-64: select separate measured runs and metrics, estimate errors and list parameters for
sensitivity analysis. 65: finalise the table of validity regions and the final report format. These 5
hours are split into 2+2+1 without adding time to the original programme. Do not revise the
quality criterion after seeing validation results in a way that makes every outcome a success.

Hours 66-75: compare calculation with experiment
66-67: complete the transfer in task 11 and reproduce the measured input and initial conditions.
68-69: compare trajectories, fix unit, timing and interface errors, then freeze the parameters.
70-71: perform the independent validation in task 12 and calculate errors using the predefined
metrics. 72-73: conduct sensitivity analysis and separate numerical problems from physical
disagreement. 74-75: assemble supporting results, limitations, a reproducible run and a brief
analysis of one failed model. If time is short, reduce contact-geometry complexity and additional
tools; the identified joint, 2R or leg dynamics, energy checks and independent model validation
remain mandatory.
































M9 • 03 Jun 2027 - 06 Jul 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          10 / 15
СтраницаPage 136 · Acceptance checks: detecting physical errors
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Acceptance checks: detecting physical errors

Test scenarios
F1: no gravity, friction or external torque. Rest is maintained; with an initial velocity, the
corresponding energy balance holds. F2: one link under constant torque without gravity.
Acceleration agrees with τ/J. F3: positive viscous friction without actuation. Energy decreases
within integration error. F4: geometry is scaled incorrectly. The unit table and comparison against
the analytical period reveal the error; visual similarity of the trajectory alone is insufficient to
accept the simulation. F5: the mass matrix is asymmetric or not positive definite for a physical
configuration. The test rejects the model before integration.
F6: contact without penetration and during lift-off. No attractive normal force occurs. F7: tangential
sliding. Frictional work does not create energy; contact force vanishes when N=0. F8: integration
step size is reduced without changing physical parameters. The result must show convergence of
the metrics of interest; otherwise conclusions about mechanics are premature. F9: the COM moves
outside the horizontal static support polygon. The margin changes sign; the test does not
automatically conclude that dynamic falling occurs. F10: parameters are fitted to one run, but do
not reproduce a new one. Narrow the validity region or improve the model and repeat independent
validation.

Evidence that the module is complete
Provide dimensional and energy tests; checks of M,h,g; input parameters with provenance; a
two-link or leg simulation; contact sensitivity analysis; transfer of the M7 identification results; and
comparison of a measured trend with calculation. The measured trend may be delay, characteristic
time, load dependence or decay; choose the metric in advance. The report must explicitly identify
conditions under which the model fails. Without a physical recording, the corresponding item
remains open even if every mathematical test passes.

Questions and handover to the next module
Explain why moment of inertia depends on the axis; where velocity-dependent terms come from;
how to check the gravity sign; why to solve a system with M rather than calculate its inverse; why
excessively stiff contact complicates integration; how the friction cone differs from the static
support-polygon rule; why a servo model with an internal controller cannot be treated as an ideal
torque actuator; and how to distinguish noise, numerical error and incorrect physics. Pass on
parameters, original measurements, dynamics functions and accuracy limitations. When designing
the controller next month, account for model validity limits and actuator saturation; calling a
simulation function alone is insufficient.





























M9 • 03 Jun 2027 - 06 Jul 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          11 / 15
СтраницаPage 137 · Assigned reading: a focused reading route
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Assigned reading: a focused reading route

Books and lecture notes may be in English; keep the plan, definitions and your own explanations in
English. Read only the specified sections within the existing 75 hours.

Core reading and one reference route
1. Core: K. Lynch, F. Park, Modern Robotics, Chapter 8. §8.1.3 - the mass matrix; §8.3 -
Newton-Euler; §8.5 - forward dynamics. Tasks 1-7 require force diagrams, the meaning of M(q) and
an independent check of the forward and inverse problems.
2. Core: R. Tedrake, Underactuated Robotics. The Simple Pendulum: Equations of Motion;
Multi-Body Dynamics: Lagrangian Dynamics and Manipulator Equations; Planning and Control
through Contact: physical models of contact and friction. Read for tasks 3-10, without trajectory
optimisation.
3. Reference: R. Featherstone, Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms. Chapters Modelling Rigid Body
Systems and Inverse Dynamics: establish the definitions of inertia and external force used, and the
directions of recursive calculations. The relevant example is sufficient for checking task 6; the
complete set of algorithms is not yet required.

Documentation for specific practical work
SciPy solve_ivp - method, rtol and atol parameters, the events mechanism and the success flag for
tasks 3-7. Featherstone spatial_v2 - mcI, HandC, ID and FDab as reference implementations of
dynamics.
MuJoCo Computation - Contact and Numerical Integration if comparing simulators; installing
MuJoCo is not required for your own numerical experiment.

After reading
After the derivation, check units, the gravity sign and the energy balance. Compare two integration
step sizes, then change one physical parameter. For tasks 11-12, return to the actuator model and
validation data from M7. The presence of contact alone does not imply the absence of sliding.

СтраницаPage 138 · Key terms and definitions
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Key terms and definitions

Rigid body. An idealisation in which the distances between any two points of a body remain
constant during motion and loading.
Centre of mass. The point whose position is the average position of all body elements, weighted
by their masses.
Inertia tensor. A matrix describing mass distribution about a selected point; it determines the
rotational contribution to kinetic energy and has units kg·m².
Free-body diagram. A diagram of an isolated body showing all external forces and torques,
including reactions from removed constraints.
Generalised coordinates. Independent configuration parameters sufficient to describe the
system’s position under its geometric constraints.
Lagrangian. The difference between kinetic and potential energy, used in Lagrange’s equations to
obtain system dynamics.
Mass matrix. The configuration-dependent matrix M(q), which determines kinetic energy and
relates generalised accelerations to forces.
Velocity-dependent terms. The part of the dynamics arising from coordinate motion, including
Coriolis and centrifugal effects; the representation of matrix C is not unique.
Gravity vector. Generalised torques or forces corresponding to the potential-energy gradient
under the chosen equation-of-motion convention.
Forward dynamics. Calculation of accelerations from current coordinates, velocities, applied
forces and the chosen constraint model.
Inverse dynamics. Calculation of required generalised forces from specified coordinates,
velocities and accelerations with known external inputs.
Dissipation. Irreversible conversion of mechanical energy into other forms, such as heat, through
friction or damping.
Unilateral contact. A constraint that permits bodies to separate and contact to be compressed,
but does not permit an attractive normal force between surfaces.
Normal force. The component of contact force along the surface normal; in a model without
adhesion it points away from the surface.
Friction cone. The set of admissible contact forces in the Coulomb model: tangential force
magnitude is bounded by μ times the normal force.
Sticking. A contact mode with zero relative tangential velocity, possible while the required force
remains within the friction limit.
Impulse. The time integral of force, which changes momentum; it approximates a short impact
without detailed calculation of peak force.
Support polygon. The convex hull of support points on a plane; the centre-of-mass projection
provides only a quasi-static criterion.
Check the relationships: M(q)q̈+c(q,q̇)+g(q)=τ+Jᵀf. All forces must have consistent signs, bases
and points of application.

Preparation for dynamics experiments

NEW PURCHASES: NONE REQUIRED
Use the existing MacBook Pro M4, CAD link models from M5, IMU and controller from M6, and the
secured actuator and current and temperature measurement equipment from M7. Investigate 2R
dynamics and contact numerically. The 3D printer is needed only if the fixtures change; choose a
printing profile for the exact printer model.

PREPARE BEFORE HOURS 1-20
Create a parameter table for each link: mass in kg, centre-of-mass position in m, inertia in kg·m²,
coordinate frame and value source. Distinguish inertia about the centre of mass from inertia about
the joint axis. Mark estimated parameters and their uncertainty ranges.
Before repeating a physical experiment, check mounting, stopping, the M7 limits, angle direction
and consistency of measurement timestamps. Use loads and levers from the existing fixtures;
increase the load only within the previously justified operating range.

INSTALL NOW
No new packages are mandatory. On macOS ARM, use the Python, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib and
pytest installations from M8; use SymPy if you already selected it for your own symbolic derivation.
SciPy solve_ivp integrates your own equation system on the CPU.

OPTIONAL: INDEPENDENT COMPARISON
An external engine is needed only for the chosen independent comparison. This month, you can
compare equations and values with the author’s spatial_v2 library without installing
MATLAB/Simulink. MuJoCo and other engines are not new mandatory purchases or prerequisites for
completing M9.

CHECK THE ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL MODEL
Reproduce pendulum motion: without friction, check energy drift as the step size decreases; with
friction, check that energy decreases. For 2R, check symmetry and positive definiteness of M, and
consistency between forward and inverse dynamics. In the contact model, check the absence of
attraction to the surface and the distinction between sticking and sliding.
Save versions, integrator configuration, initial conditions, an energy plot and an independent
validation recording. A successful simulation confirms only the model properties tested; physical
robot readiness requires its own experiments. Preparation is included in the existing 75 hours.

СтраницаPage 140 · Motion fundamentals: why torque is needed
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M09  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Motion fundamentals: why torque is needed

Required: derive the equation of motion in two ways
The kinematics in M8 relates angles to endpoint position. Dynamics determines which torque
produces a chosen acceleration and what happens with a limited actuator. Before deriving the
equations, clarify the distinction between mass m in kg, moment of inertia I in kg·m² and torque τ
in N·m. A geometrically admissible leg or finger trajectory may demand unavailable torque.

One joint: geometry, energy and equation
Example pendulum: a point mass m=0.5 kg at the end of a massless rod l=0.2 m; the pivot is fixed.
In the x-y plane, y points upward and q is measured from the downward vertical towards +x. Then
p=(l sinq;-l cosq), v=q̇ in rad/s, I=ml²=0.02 kg·m². There is no friction or contact; positive τ_act
increases q.
Newton and Euler: the torque of weight about the pivot is -mgl sinq, so Iq̈=τ_act-mgl sinq.
Lagrange: K=Iv²/2, U=mgl(1-cosq), L=K-U. Substitution into d/dt(∂L/∂v)-∂L/∂q=τ_act gives the same
equation, Iq̈+mgl sinq=τ_act. These are two descriptions of the same mechanics; their agreement
helps check the signs.
At q=π/6, an acceleration q̈=1 rad/s² requires, by inverse dynamics,
τ_act=0.02·1+0.5·9.81·0.2·0.5=0.5105 N·m. Of this, 0.4905 N·m compensates for weight and
0.0200 N·m accelerates the mass. Forward dynamics calculates q̈=(τ_act-mgl sinq)/I. With τ_act=0
at this position, q̈=-24.525 rad/s²: the link accelerates towards the downward vertical, even when
starting from rest.

From a pendulum to two links
For a fixed-base chain of revolute joints: M(q)v̇+h(q,v)+g(q)=τ_act+Jᵀf_ext. Here v=q̇; M relates
accelerations to torques, h contains velocity effects, and g contains gravitational torques; f_ext is
the force exerted by the environment on the endpoint, expressed in the same basis as the
positional Jacobian J. Geometry determines centre-of-mass velocities, from which energy and M are
calculated. At rest, τ_act=g-Jᵀf_ext; motion adds inertial and velocity-dependent terms.
An actuator with a position interface does not become a source of known torque: use the validated
M7 model. A moving body, distributed contacts and spatial tensors require a more detailed model;
this module requires a clear pendulum calculation and the specified 2R dynamics.

Check torque, acceleration and energy calculations
In tasks 3-6, save both derivations and the numerical example. Independently estimate dU/dq
using a central difference: at q=π/6, expect 0.4905 N·m. Apply 0.5105 N·m to forward dynamics
and recover 1 rad/s². Then, without actuation or friction, compare energy E=K+U at two integrator
step sizes; reducing the step should reduce numerical drift. Agreement between inverse and
forward dynamics does not rule out an error shared by both functions.
Included in the 75 hours: 1 hour from 9-10 for the two derivations; 1 hour from 15-16 for the
pendulum; 1 hour from 33-34 for the forward and inverse dynamics check. This is a required
reference example within the existing tasks. Calculations run on the CPU; no additional equipment,
software or hours are required.
References: Tedrake, The Simple Pendulum: equation of motion and the Undamped Pendulum
section; Lynch/Park, Modern Robotics, §8.1.1 and §8.1.4: Lagrange, Newton and Euler methods.

СтраницаPage 141 · Feedback: achieving stable motion
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Feedback: achieving stable motion

M10 • 07 Jul 2027 - 08 Aug 2027 • 75 hours

What you will learn this month
By the end of the month, you will be able to explain why a joint reaches its target angle, why
increasing gain produces oscillations, and how IMU delay affects platform stability. The deliverable
is a benchmark for comparing joint and body-tilt control methods. Prepare a model, a digital
controller, measured transient and frequency responses, a description of limitations and fault-test
results. For a future walking robot, this provides the basis for maintaining body attitude; for a hand,
it supports precise finger motion without accumulating error when pressing against an object.

Inputs and scope
Use the geometry, actuator, limits and measurements from M5-M9. Encoder and IMU reading,
timestamping, and command and state logging must work before you start. Review torque, angular
velocity, inertia, derivatives and integrals. Be able to read a step-response plot and distinguish
measurement time from delivery time. If any of these elements is not ready, use the first two hours
to diagnose it and reduce optional plots.
Begin with one axis. Full balancing of a multi-legged robot, gait planning and optimal force
distribution are not required here. For tilt, use a platform model with limited rotation or a secured
test rig from earlier stages. An IMU alone does not provide a plant to control: explicitly identify
which actuator action changes roll or pitch. If this mechanism is unavailable, test tilt control in a
model, physically measure only the joint and IMU, and leave physical tilt validation open.

What counts as a result
Show the continuous model, its discrete implementation and real data separately in the report.
Give units for every coefficient and a source for every limit. The minimum final demonstration
includes a joint-reference step, rejection of a repeatable disturbance, operation near saturation, tilt
holding, artificial delay and loss of fresh data. Fix the criteria before the experiment, then report
actual values without adjusting the acceptance limits.
The purpose of the month is to make control choices, beyond learning a list of controllers. Choose
the control bandwidth, justify the loop frequency and show the conditions under which the solution
stops working. A good result includes one clearly explained failure mode and the reason for
excluding it from the operating region. This information will support the transition to state-space
methods and estimation in M11.

СтраницаPage 142 · Organising the 75 hours
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Organising the 75 hours

Four work blocks
Block A, hours 1-20: feedback and joint PID. Block B, 21-40: frequency responses and noise. Block
C, 41-60: digital implementation and loop timing. Block D, 61-75: body tilt and the final comparison
experiment. Each of the first three blocks contains 10 hours of theory and analysis and 10 hours of
practice; the fourth contains 5 hours of analysis and 10 hours of practice. Total: 35 + 40 = 75
hours. The work steps on pages 9-10 expand these same hours and require no additional time
allocation.
Divide each ten-hour theory block into five two-hour sessions: 20 minutes reviewing the previous
model, 45 minutes reading the relevant section, 40 minutes deriving a small example or examining
a log, and 15 minutes recording the conclusion. Also divide the ten-hour Sunday practical session
into five two-hour periods with breaks between them. Breaks are excluded from net study hours.
Allocate the final five hours of analysis as 2 + 2 + 1.

Start with the question, then choose the tool
The main computational environment is Python, NumPy, SciPy and python-control; implement the
control loop in C++ in the existing rig firmware. Begin each session with a testable question: how
does the input affect the output, which state cannot be measured, and which data reveal its
changes? Before running, write down the expected sign, scale or sequence of events. Compare the
prediction with the result and examine at least one discrepancy. A plot supports a conclusion only
when accompanied by an explanation of the observed relationship.
Maintain one repository with model, config, experiments, tests and reports directories. Every
experiment needs a unique identifier, code version, configuration, parameter source, initial state,
units and raw data. The analysis script reads a saved experiment and builds the report without
manually correcting measurements. The final joint-and-attitude-control benchmark project
combines comparisons of joint and body controllers; the individual exercises gradually form its test
suite.

Time accounting and reducing scope
Calendar boundaries may coincide with an adjacent module. Keep rest days, holiday intervals and
integration checks as specified in the overall calendar; place numbered steps in available time
without counting hours twice. Do not add hours to this module. Assess equipment and library
readiness at the outset rather than spending the practical session on an unplanned platform
change.
If you fall behind, reduce the number of sinusoidal test frequencies and gain-scheduling variants;
thoroughly check one body axis. Retain the joint model, a saturation experiment with anti-windup,
frequency-response measurement, firmware timing assessment and the fault test for stale IMU
data. You may investigate the second axis in a model if you state this in the report. Preserve the
comparison of joint and tilt control; physical validation remains unfinished until there are
experimental results from the rig.

СтраницаPage 143 · Feedback, modelling and PID tuning
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Feedback, modelling and PID tuning

Study the relationship between torque and position
Examine the forward path command → actuator → mechanics → angle and the measurement
feedback path. For the example joint, use J·q̈ + b·q̇ = τ: J in kg·m², b in N·m·s/rad, τ in N·m and q in
rad. Under torque control, the transfer function from τ to q is 1/(J·s² + b·s). If the actuator accepts
only position, identify the actuator together with its internal closed loop as a single plant; a position
command cannot replace torque in the model. Explain where the sensor, delay, saturation and
disturbance appear in the diagram.
Poles determine natural modes; zeros change response shape. Stable poles of a continuous linear
model have negative real parts; an integrator at zero needs separate reasoning, and simulation
does not replace analysis. Study negative feedback T = PC/(1 + PC), error e = r − y and PID:
proportional action responds to current error, integral action to accumulated error, and derivative
action to rate of change. In a practical implementation, take the derivative of the measurement
and filter it to reduce command kick when the reference changes.

Task 1. A joint model with three proportional-control responses
Inputs: estimated J and b or an explicitly labelled illustrative parameter set, a rest position and a
bounded reference step. 1) Build the continuous model. 2) Choose three P values producing slow,
acceptable and oscillatory responses. 3) Record angle, error and torque on the same time grid. 4)
Explain changes in poles and curve shape. Deliverable: a computational notebook and a table of
rise, peak and settling times. Check: the first motion has the correct sign relative to the command;
doubling inertia must change the response. Error to investigate: reversed feedback sign, tested
first in the model only.

Task 2. Integral action near the actuator limit
Add a constant external disturbance and the command limit from the rig specification. Compare P,
PI and PID, then PID with anti-windup: for example, stop integrating when the command is already
limited and the error demands more action in the same direction. Record the unsaturated
command, limited command and integral state separately. Return the reference from an
unreachable region to the admissible region and compare recovery times. Deliverable: a test and
three plots. Check: the command never exceeds the declared limit; after returning, the integral
must not hold the actuator in saturation beyond the expected recovery transient. Add feedforward
as a separate calculation compensating for a known load, retaining feedback for the remaining
error.

СтраницаPage 144 · Frequency domain: bandwidth, margins and
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Frequency domain: bandwidth, margins and
measurement

Study the meaning of a Bode plot
For sinusoidal excitation, frequency determines whether the joint can keep up with the command.
Study magnitude and phase, logarithmic scales, 20·log10 of the amplitude ratio, and the
conversion ω = 2πf. Closed-loop bandwidth and open-loop crossover frequency are different
quantities. Gain and phase margins are calculated from the loop transfer L = PC under the chosen
negative-feedback convention. A closed-loop response plot alone cannot establish a stability
margin without knowing the loop structure.
Interpret S = 1/(1 + L) and T = L/(1 + L) as descriptions of disturbance rejection and signal and
noise transmission at the chosen point in the diagram. State where the disturbance enters before
comparing curves. Higher gain improves regulation over some low frequencies, but can amplify
measurement noise and bring unwanted dynamics closer. A sensor filter changes phase as well as
noise; include its delay in the loop analysis.

Task 3. Model margins and frequency response
Take the model from task 1 and the working PID. 1) Construct L and T and calculate margins with
margin. 2) Check phase-argument units: phase data supplied to margin are in degrees, whereas
frequency_response returns radians. 3) Introduce a known delay and rebuild the response. 4)
Calculate step responses for the original and degraded cases. Deliverable: one sheet containing the
Bode plot, poles and transient response. Check: a conclusion of reduced stability must agree with
the time-domain experiment. If there is no crossover, explain the meaning of an infinite or
undefined margin without treating it as a guarantee.

Task 4. A sinusoidal experiment on the rig
At small amplitude, apply 5-8 frequencies within the admissible range. At each frequency, wait for
the transient to end, record at least several complete periods, and estimate amplitude and phase
by fitting a sinusoid. Compare the reference-to-angle frequency response with model T.
Deliverable: measured points with a range of variability and a configuration table. Check: repeat at
half amplitude; a strong change in the ratio indicates nonlinearity or insufficient signal-to-noise
ratio. Stop the experiment at the predefined limits if saturation, noticeable heating or excessive
travel occurs. If margins are unconfirmed, describe tolerance to delay and load changes using the
experimental series.
































M10 • 07 Jul 2027 - 08 Aug 2027 • 75 hours                                                                       4 / 15
СтраницаPage 145 · Digital control: discretisation and real time
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Digital control: discretisation and real time

Study system behaviour between samples
A digital controller reads a sensor at intervals Ts, calculates a command and holds it until the next
update. Study the zero-order hold, conversion from continuous to discrete systems, and the ZOH
and Tustin methods. A discrete linear model requires poles inside the unit circle for stability. Euler’s
method is useful for understanding, but an excessively large step creates numerical instability
itself. Compare cont2discrete with a manual update of a simple first-order model.
Describe the loop period, computation time, measurement delay and data age separately. Jitter is
variation in interval duration; quantisation is the finite resolution of a measurement or command.
“A frequency of 200 Hz” without the distribution of actual intervals does not characterise operation.
The Nyquist condition relates sampling frequency to recoverable signal bandwidth, but is not
sufficient for choosing a control frequency: phase margins, filters, computation and the actuator
need additional headroom, supported by modelling and experiment.

Task 5. One algorithm at several frequencies
Take one controller designed for the continuous model and discretise it for three Ts values selected
relative to the desired bandwidth. Use the same physical plant, duration and reference amplitude.
Introduce delays of 0, 1 and several samples. Deliverable: a Ts × delay experiment table, poles,
RMSE and maximum command. Check: Ts is stored in the configuration, and integral and derivative
actions scale with time. Deliberately retain old coefficients after changing Ts, show the error and
add a test that detects it. Do not claim that example values apply to every actuator.

Task 6. Measure the embedded loop
In the existing firmware, timestamp the start of reading, end of calculation and command
transmission using a monotonic clock; where possible, check the period with GPIO and a logic
analyser. Run a quiet mode, intensive logging and an artificial delay in one handler. Save
distributions of computation time, intervals and measurement age: median, p95, p99 and
maximum, together with sample counts. Check: logging does not perform a blocking write in the
critical section; a stale measurement does not become fresh through late delivery. Deliverable: a
timing-budget report. Explicitly state the sensor polling, controller and logging frequencies; mark a
repeated previous value rather than counting it as a new measurement.





































M10 • 07 Jul 2027 - 08 Aug 2027 • 75 hours                                                                         5 / 15
СтраницаPage 146 · Roll and pitch: controlling body tilt
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Roll and pitch: controlling body tilt

Study the two-loop structure
The outer tilt controller receives roll and pitch and generates a bounded reference for the
actuator’s inner loop. Check one axis first, then the other. The inner loop must track the outer-loop
reference within the chosen range; tuning two fast loops independently without analysing their
interaction can produce oscillations. Derive the relationship positive command change → tilt
change from the geometry and verify it with a small test input. For a stationary model, distinguish
tilt from linear acceleration, which distorts the accelerometer-based estimate.
Gain scheduling is specified in advance, for example as a function of position or load. It requires
checks of boundaries and transitions, rather than arbitrary increases in P for large error. Limit the
target angle, reference rate of change, inner-loop command and admissible IMU data age
separately. Recovery after a fault must be an explicit state; the return of packets need not
automatically resume motion.

Task 7. Holding a tilt angle
Initial conditions: a model or secured platform with a known axis, an IMU and a working inner
controller. 1) Check zero and axis directions. 2) Command a small roll with zero pitch. 3) Repeat for
pitch. 4) Introduce a repeatable disturbance pulse. 5) Compare controller-off and controller-on
results under the same input. Deliverable: curves for both axes and commands. Check: calculate
RMSE over the same window after the disturbance, peak error as the maximum absolute error, and
settling time from entry into and continued residence within a predefined band. For a reference
near zero, specify an absolute band in radians rather than a percentage of zero.

Task 8. Surface tilt, limits and recovery
Save two base orientations and two admissible loads; run every combination with fixed gains, then
with two gain sets selected by operating point. Introduce a transition between gain sets and an IMU
dropout. Deliverable: a table of stable and unconfirmed operating conditions, detection time and
state sequence. Check: output continuity when gains change and correct handling of the integral;
during a dropout, new motion commands stop within the time allocated for software fault
detection. The physical stopping method depends on the mechanics: zero torque does not always
hold a platform. Use the predefined behaviour of the secured rig and describe separately what a
standing robot would require.
For the hand, repeat only the reasoning: object contact obstructs the commanded finger motion,
the internal actuator reaches its limit and the integral accumulates error. Describe which
implemented limits help and why a position PID alone is insufficient to control contact force.

СтраницаPage 147 · Specification for the final benchmark
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Specification for the final benchmark

Defining a reproducible experiment
One scenario specifies the plant identifier, model version, initial angle, initial velocity, step or
sinusoidal reference, disturbance, limits, Ts, filter and duration. The output log must contain
measurement and control times, reference, measured joint angle or body tilt, estimated velocity,
error, P, I and D terms, commands before and after limiting, saturation and deadline-miss flags,
and state-machine state. Record the command in the units actually used and separate any
conversion to torque.
For the joint, compare at least P, PID and PID with anti-windup. For the body, compare disabled
stabilisation with the working outer loop, then one variant with increased delay. Every variant
receives the same reference sequence and initial state. Save the scenario and configurations
before comparison; do not choose different convenient segments for each algorithm. On the real
rig, repeat the key scenario at least three times to distinguish a trend from a single successful run.

Calculating and interpreting metrics
RMSE = sqrt(mean(e²)) has the units of the measured angle. Peak error = max(abs(e)); define
percentage overshoot relative to a non-zero step amplitude. Calculate settling time as the time
after which the signal remains inside the chosen band until the end of the window; if the window is
too short, record “did not settle during the experiment”. The saturation fraction is the number of
samples with a limited command divided by the number of commands. For uneven sampling, also
calculate the fraction of time, since counting rows can distort the result.
Plots: reference and output; error and settling band; command and limits; data age; model Bode
plot and measured points. Separate calibration and validation data: do not assess model suitability
solely on the experiment used to fit J, b and delay. Use one validation experiment with a different
admissible load or excitation frequency.

Deliverable-package requirements
A launch command from a clean working directory must build the baseline report and run the limit
checks. The README explains the plant, wiring and mounting for physical experiments,
parameters, limits and stopping sequence. Include a log of failed scenarios and the reasons for
excluding them. State the basis for every conclusion: analytical linear model, nonlinear model, rig
experiment or a hypothesis awaiting confirmation. This will allow M11 to compare LQR with the real
PID using the same criteria.
































M10 • 07 Jul 2027 - 08 Aug 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          7 / 15
СтраницаPage 148 · Tests that reveal controller errors
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Tests that reveal controller errors

Required fault scenarios
Scenario F1: reverse the encoder sign in the model. Expected: error grows rapidly and the software
monitor detects departure from the permitted region; do not run this experiment physically. Save a
short log up to stopping and demonstrate that the event is caused by the feedback sign, rather
than random noise. The corrected configuration must pass the same test.
Scenario F2: an unreachable step followed by a return. Expected: the command is limited, the
integral state is controlled, and recovery is faster than without anti-windup in the chosen test. Do
not claim universal superiority from one curve; compare the specific recovery time and peak after
the limit is removed.
Scenario F3: measurement delay and a stale packet. Separate transport delay from the loss of new
measurements. Expected: the monitor uses the age of the original measurement, while frequency
analysis and the time-domain model show degradation as delay increases. The last late packet
must not reset the freshness timer without checking its timestamp.
Scenario F4: encoder noise and coarse quantisation. Expected: their effect on the D term and
command is visible; a filter reduces some high-frequency noise, but its phase lag is represented in
the model. Compare spectra and command RMS at a stationary reference, keeping this result
separate from step-tracking accuracy.
Scenario F5: increased inertia or load. Choose a model change and a separate admissible rig load.
Expected: metric changes that can be related to the model; the operating region is limited to
measured cases. Do not mark untested masses and configurations as passed in the table.
Scenario F6: occasional long computations. Introduce one computation deadline miss every N
cycles and batched logging. Expected: the event is explicitly marked, data losses are counted, and
the response to lateness is checked. Compare p99 and the maximum; average duration must not
hide an occasional overrun.

Analysing a failed experiment
First reproduce the failure using the saved configuration. Check units, signs and the time scale,
then limiters, and only then gains. Change one factor per experiment. If the model is stable but the
rig oscillates, check backlash, the actuator’s internal controller, the IMU filter, communication delay
and frequency mismatches. Every unexplained effect becomes a separate task for additional
measurements; reducing P without understanding the cause is a temporary measure.

Hours 1-40: foundations and frequency
checks

Hours 1-20: joint and feedback
Theory 1-10: five 2-hour sessions. 1-2: examine the actuator interface and units; 3-4: derive the
model and poles; 5-6: study the step response; 7-8: work through PID, feedforward and saturation;
9-10: design the sign and anti-windup checks. In each session, perform a small calculation using
numbers from your configuration so that theory immediately reveals missing parameters.

Acceptance and handover to M11

Practical defence of the result
In 10-15 minutes, show the loop diagram, one stable and one rejected operating condition, a
frequency response and a fault recording. Explain how the model relates to the real actuator
interface. Then change only delay or inertia and predict the direction of the response change in
advance. A reviewer must be able to recalculate metrics from the raw recording and reach the
same conclusion about whether the criteria were met.
Required evidence of readiness: positive axis directions are checked; settings and units are fixed;
the declared operating region is bounded; saturation and loss of fresh data are tested; measured
timing costs are documented. Support stability with margins from a correct loop model or
experimental evidence over declared delays and loads. Do not describe the latter as a rigorous
proof of stability for every possible operating condition.

Self-check questions
1) How does a pole differ from a zero in the joint example? 2) Why can increasing P both speed up
and degrade the response? 3) What does the integral do when the physical command is already at
its limit? 4) Why does differentiating the measurement differ from differentiating the error at a
reference step? 5) Which transfer is used to calculate phase margin? 6) Why does the Nyquist
frequency not determine a sufficient control frequency?
7) How can you distinguish sensor noise from loop oscillations? 8) What does a filter change
besides noise amplitude? 9) How do you specify settling time for zero target tilt? 10) Why does
average loop time not replace p99 and the maximum? 11) How can an old packet mistakenly
appear fresh? 12) Why are zero torque and safe body holding not always equivalent? Support your
answers with your own plots, as well as definitions.

What to save and which claims remain unconfirmed
Pass the model, baseline PID, discretisation parameters, disturbance scenarios, noise and delay
configuration, and common metrics script to M11. They form the fixed basis for comparison with
LQR and an estimator. In a separate table, list unmodelled effects: backlash, dry friction,
torque-speed dependence, structural compliance and incorrect tilt estimation during acceleration.
If time is limited, retain one thoroughly tested body axis and a model demonstration of the second
axis with explicit status. Reduce frequency count and presentation work, but retain closed-loop
response measurement, saturation and fault scenarios. The module is complete only within the
checks actually performed; any deferred physical work must appear in the subsequent integration
plan.

Books and lecture notes may be in English; keep the plan, definitions and your own explanations in

Core reading and one reference route
1. Core: K. J. Åström, R. Murray, Feedback Systems, 2nd edition. Chapters Transfer Functions,

2. Core worked example: B. Messner, D. Tilbury and the CTMS team, Control Tutorials for
MATLAB and Simulink. The page Introduction: PID Controller Design, followed by DC Motor Speed:

Python.
3. Reference: J. Doyle, B. Francis, A. Tannenbaum, Feedback Control Theory. §3.1 Basic Feedback
Loop and §3.4 Performance; §4.1 Plant Uncertainty - the introductory formulation only. For tasks

Documentation for specific practical work
Python Control step_info - transient-response criteria; margin - phase units and loop margins.
Before plotting, check units: rad and deg, Hz and rad·s⁻¹.
SciPy cont2discrete - zoh, bilinear and euler for task 5. For the spectral analysis in F4, use the

After reading

СтраницаPage 153 · Key terms and definitions
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Key terms and definitions

Plant. A physical system or its model whose output changes under a control input and external
disturbances.
Control error. The difference between the reference and measured output, in the same units and
a consistent coordinate frame.
Proportional action (P). The part of the command equal to current error multiplied by a gain.
Integral action (I). The part of the command that depends on error accumulated over time; it
helps remove constant offset under admissible operating conditions.
Derivative action (D). The part of the command responding to the rate of change of error or
measurement; it usually requires measurement-noise filtering.
Feedforward. A command calculated from the reference and a model of the expected input,
without waiting for measured error to appear.
Transfer function. The ratio of the Laplace transforms of output and input for a linear
time-invariant system under zero initial conditions.
Pole. A singularity of a transfer function associated with a natural dynamic mode; internal stability
is checked with reference to the realisation.
Frequency response. The complex ratio of output and input amplitudes of a linear system under
steady-state sinusoidal excitation at a specified frequency.
Bode plot. Plots of frequency-response magnitude and phase against a logarithmic frequency
axis, with explicitly stated units.
Phase margin. The additional phase lag to the critical value at a selected unity-gain frequency of
the open loop.
Gain margin. The permissible gain multiplier before the critical condition at a selected open-loop
phase crossover.
Bandwidth. The frequency range over which a signal is reproduced acceptably; the boundary
criterion must be declared for the selected channel.
Overshoot. The amount by which the output exceeds the final step level; a relative measure is
normalised by the non-zero amplitude of that step.
Settling time. The time after which error remains within the declared band until observation ends
for the given scenario.
Sampling period. The interval Ts between scheduled digital-controller updates; actual intervals
are also measured using timestamps.
Zero-order hold. Keeping the last command constant until the next output update.
Jitter. Variation in actual execution times or update intervals relative to the chosen digital-loop
schedule.
Gain scheduling. A predefined choice of parameters based on operating point, with validated
transitions between modes.
Check the relationships: for unity negative feedback, L=PC, T=L/(1+L), S=1/(1+L). Frequency
ω=2πf.

СтраницаPage 155 · Motion fundamentals: holding and tracking
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M10  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Motion fundamentals: holding and tracking

Required: why a stable position is insufficient
Holding specifies a constant angle qd; tracking specifies qd(t), velocity and acceleration. A leg joint
must change angle on time during foot swing. Small error at the end of motion is insufficient: lag
along the path changes foot position. Before calculating, explain the negative-feedback sign and
the distinction between angle, angular velocity and torque.

Joint model and error equation
The base is fixed; positive q and τ are chosen along the same axis. q is in rad, and primes denote
time derivatives: q′ in rad/s, q″ in rad/s². The link moves without gravitational torque; J is inertia
about the joint in kg·m², and b is viscous resistance in N·m·s/rad. For now, assume no saturation,
delay or model error:
J q″ + b q′ = τ; e = qd − q. Choose τ = J qd″ + b qd′ + Kp e + Kd e′. The first two terms
provide acceleration and overcome resistance in advance; PD corrects deviation. Substituting q =
qd − e into the model gives J e″ + (b + Kd)e′ + Kp e = 0. This is error dynamics, not a separate
physical joint.
Let J = 0.02 kg·m², b = 0.04 N·m·s/rad, Kp = 2 N·m/rad and Kd = 0.36 N·m·s/rad. Then e″ + 20e′ +
100e = 0; both poles equal −10 s⁻¹. Error decays with critical damping in the ideal continuous
model. This conclusion alone does not confirm the stability of a digital actuator with limits.

Calculation at a selected instant
At the selected instant, qd = 0.30 rad and q = 0.20 rad; qd′ = q′ = 0.50 rad/s and qd″ = 1 rad/s².
Thus e = 0.10 rad and e′ = 0; feedforward is 0.02·1 + 0.04·0.50 = 0.04 N·m, feedback is 0.20 N·m,
and total τ = 0.24 N·m. The model gives q″ = (0.24 − 0.04·0.50)/0.02 = 11 rad/s² and e″ = −10
rad/s²: the joint accelerates, reducing its lag behind the reference.
If feedforward is removed and qd moves at a constant velocity of 0.50 rad/s for a long time,
steady-state e = b·qd′/Kp = 0.01 rad. The error creates the torque needed to overcome resistance.
For a stationary target in this model, e tends to zero. Holding and tracking therefore require
different test references.

Two experiments within the existing laboratory work
1. For a constant target, take e(0) = 0.10 rad and e′(0) = 0. Save an e plot and compare with e(t) =
0.10(1 + 10t)exp(−10t): at t = 0.40 s, expect 0.00916 rad. 2. For a linearly changing reference,
compare PD with and without feedforward; save qd, q, τ and the individual terms. Check: error
without feedforward approaches 0.01 rad; mark saturated segments separately.
Time: 1 theory hour from hours 7-8 (PID and feedforward), and 2 practice hours from 15-16
(integral and derivative actions, limits); this analysis and these plots belong to existing tasks 1-2,
within the 75 hours. The numbers apply to the model. Do not send torque τ to a position servo: its
internal loop is studied separately. Full multi-joint computed-torque control remains outside the
mandatory minimum.
Read selectively: Lynch, Park, Modern Robotics, §11.4, Part 1: PD and error dynamics; §11.4, Part 3:
model-based feedforward.

СтраницаPage 156 · Robot state: estimation and admissible
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Robot state: estimation and admissible
control

M11 • 08 Aug 2027 - 12 Sep 2027 • 75 hours

This month’s deliverable
You will connect three engineering questions: what is happening inside the mechanism, what can
be reconstructed from sensors, and which command is admissible to send. The deliverable
compares PID, LQR, estimation with KF and EKF, and a simple QP on a model with known
parameters, using identical disturbances and testing optimiser failure. For a leg, this prepares for
contact-force allocation; for a finger, it prepares for control using an estimated state with bounded
actuation.
Begin with the axis from M10. State x = [q, v] contains angle q in rad and angular velocity v in
rad/s; input u is torque in N·m; the encoder measures angle. In this model, velocity can be
reconstructed from a sequence of measurements even without a separate velocity sensor. In a
small separate experiment, estimate tilt from a gyroscope and accelerometer. Then solve a planar
force-allocation problem with two supports. These three parts share rules for time, units and
checks, but each needs its own mathematical model.

Prerequisites
Review matrix multiplication, derivatives, eigenvalues and the meaning of variance. Bring the
baseline PID, joint model, command limiter and fixed test scenarios from M10. Distinguish
measurements, simulation ground truth and estimates. Validate estimates against a reference: the
known state in simulation or readings from an independent reference system. The output of an
IMU-processing library is not, by itself, true orientation.

Limits on complexity
This month does not require a complete MPC, a general-purpose 3D-EKF or whole-robot balancing.
Required topics are state space, linearisation, controllability and observability, the linear Kalman
filter, a small tilt EKF, LQR and a convex quadratic programme (QP) with explicit constraints.
Mathematics should explain the experiment rather than block it for weeks. You will check each step
from model to solution and see the limitations of each approximation.
The final project contains code, equations, units, covariances, chosen objective weights, raw logs
and automated checks. All numerical thresholds in example models are experiment parameters.
For a physical actuator, limits come from its specifications, load and the previously validated rig.
“The optimiser found a solution” implies neither physical feasibility nor a correct model.

ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Organising the 75 hours

Four work blocks
Block A, hours 1-20: state space and observability. Block B, 21-40: KF, EKF and estimation quality.
Block C, 41-60: LQR and a comparison with PID under identical conditions. Block D, 61-75: force QP,
faults and integration. Each of the first three blocks contains 10 hours of theory and analysis and
10 hours of practice; the fourth contains 5 hours of analysis and 10 hours of practice. Total: 35 +
40 = 75 hours. The work steps on pages 9-10 expand these same hours and require no additional
time allocation.
Divide each ten-hour theory block into five two-hour sessions: 20 minutes reviewing the previous
model, 45 minutes reading the relevant section, 40 minutes deriving a small example or examining
a log, and 15 minutes recording the conclusion. Also divide the ten-hour Sunday practical session
into five two-hour periods with breaks between them. Breaks are excluded from net study hours.
Allocate the final five hours of analysis as 2 + 2 + 1.

Start with the question, then choose the tool
The main environment is Python, NumPy, SciPy and python-control; use FilterPy for cross-checking
and CVXPY and OSQP for a small convex problem. Begin each session with a testable question: how
does the input affect the output, which state cannot be measured, and which data reveal its
changes? Before running, write down the expected sign, scale or sequence of events. Compare the
prediction with the result and examine at least one discrepancy. A plot supports a conclusion only
when accompanied by an explanation of the observed relationship.
Maintain one repository with model, config, experiments, tests and reports directories. Every
experiment needs a unique identifier, code version, configuration, parameter source, initial state,
units and raw data. The analysis script reads a saved experiment and builds the report without
manually correcting measurements. The final state-estimation-and-control benchmark project
combines comparisons of estimation and control methods; individual exercises gradually form its
test suite.

Time accounting and reducing scope
Calendar boundaries may coincide with an adjacent module. Keep rest days, holiday intervals and
integration checks as specified in the overall calendar; place numbered steps in available time
without counting hours twice. Do not add hours to this module. Assess equipment and library
readiness at the outset rather than spending the practical session on an unplanned platform
change.
If you fall behind, reduce the number of LQR weight sets, support geometries and validation runs
with different random-number seeds after the minimum checks. Retain the axis model with a
two-dimensional state, an unobservable case, KF with a missing measurement, tilt EKF with an
outlier, an equal-conditions PID/LQR comparison and a two-support QP with infeasible and timeout
statuses. Full 3D orientation and MPC are unnecessary. The result must connect modelling,
estimation and constrained control; all declared results can be obtained in simulation with known
parameters.
