СтраницаPage 158 · State space and the operating point
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

State space and the operating point

Study the state and its evolution
Write ẋ = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du. For J·q̈ + b·q̇ = u, the matrices are A = [[0,1],[0,−b/J]], B =
[[0],[1/J]], C = [[1,0]], D = [[0]]. Dimensions: A 2×2, B 2×1, C 1×2, D 1×1. Rows have different
physical units; matching matrix shapes do not make q and v interchangeable. In discrete time, use
x[k+1] = Ad·x[k] + Bd·u[k], obtaining Ad and Bd for the declared Ts with a held command.
For a nonlinear model ẋ = f(x,u), choose an equilibrium f(x0,u0)=0 and work with deviations δx, δu.
Evaluate Jacobians A = ∂f/∂x and B = ∂f/∂u at that point. Check the meaning of gravity
compensation in u0 for a loaded axis: do not linearise around an accelerating state and then treat it
as stationary. Small-deviation equations apply only within a limited neighbourhood.

Task 1. A one-step transition
Inputs: the M10 model, two initial states and three constant torques within the model’s admissible
range. 1) Derive the matrices. 2) Obtain Ad and Bd. 3) Compare one step with numerical
integration on a fine grid. 4) Repeat for zero torque and non-zero velocity. Deliverable:
state_transition_tests and an error table. Check: q=v=u=0 remains the zero state; for positive
torque, the first velocity change has the correct sign. Error to test: omitting Ts from an update
creates a scaling error that the test must detect.

Task 2. Observability and controllability
Construct the controllability matrix [B, AB] and observability matrix [C; CA], and calculate rank and
singular values. For comparison, replace the angle sensor with a velocity-only sensor C=[0,1]. For a
free axis without positional stiffness, absolute angle is then unobservable. Specify two different
initial angles with the same velocity and show identical measurements. Deliverable: a short
demonstration using two trajectories, as well as rank(). Check sensitivity of numerical rank to unit
scaling; poor conditioning can hinder estimation even when rank is formally full.
Then linearise a model with gravity near a chosen q0 and compare it with the nonlinear model for
small and large deviations. State the region in which the linear prediction error is acceptable under
your predefined criterion.








































M11 • 08 Aug 2027 - 12 Sep 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          3 / 15
СтраницаPage 159 · KF and EKF: estimation with testable
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

KF and EKF: estimation with testable
uncertainty

Study filter prediction and update
Prediction calculates the next estimate and covariance from the model; the update refines them
using a new measurement. Q describes process-model uncertainty, R measurement uncertainty,
and P estimate uncertainty. These are covariances, not “confidence coefficients between zero and
one”. Their dimensions correspond to products of component units. If Ts changes, reconsider
discrete Q using the chosen noise model. Scalar angle variance has units rad²; angle-velocity
covariance has units rad²/s.
The measurement residual, or innovation, ν = z − h(x̂⁻) is the difference between a measurement
and its prediction; S is the predicted covariance of that difference. A smooth estimate can be wrong
even when its claimed uncertainty is small. Check error against simulation ground truth, changes in
P and innovation statistics. For NIS, calculate νᵀS⁻¹ν by solving a linear system without explicitly
inverting the matrix. Comparison with a χ² distribution is meaningful under correct Gaussian
assumptions and the appropriate measurement dimension. This is a diagnostic check with stated
conditions of applicability.

Task 3. Angle and velocity from a noisy encoder
Generate joint motion with a fixed seed, encoder noise and a small model error. Implement
prediction and update for x=[q,v]; compare with a library using identical data. Compare the
velocity estimate with a simple finite difference. Save true and estimated q and v, the diagonals of
P, the innovation and RMSE. Check: noisy data are not written to truth; when a measurement is
missing, perform prediction only and let the corresponding uncertainty grow. Then set R artificially
100 times smaller than the actual variance and explain the consequences using innovations and
estimation error.

Task 4. An EKF for one tilt axis
For one axis, choose state [θ,bg]: tilt in rad and gyroscope bias in rad/s. Prediction:
θ[k+1]=θ[k]+Ts·(ωm−bg), bg[k+1]=bg[k]. For a consistent axis, you may use accelerometer
model h=[g·sinθ,g·cosθ] in m/s²; explicit signs must match the coordinate-frame convention and
rest test. Derive H=[g·cosθ,0;−g·sinθ,0]. Check the Jacobian with finite differences. Introduce an
outlier and translational acceleration; innovation gating must mark rejected measurements and
preserve the prediction. Deliverable: an experiment with gyroscope drift, accelerometer correction
and temporary rejection of updates; yaw cannot be determined from gravity direction alone.






























M11 • 08 Aug 2027 - 12 Sep 2027 • 75 hours                                                                        4 / 15
СтраницаPage 160 · LQR and LQG: the cost of error and control
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

LQR and LQG: the cost of error and control
effort

Study the objective function
For the discrete axis, define the sum xᵀQx + uᵀRu and find feedback u = −Kx. Q is positive
semidefinite and R is positive definite; do not confuse this Q with the filter’s process covariance.
Name them Q_cost and Q_noise in code. To compare rad, rad/s and N·m meaningfully, normalise
components by selected characteristic scales q_ref, v_ref and u_ref. The weights then express the
relative cost of error and actuation, rather than depending accidentally on a conversion to degrees.
LQR does not impose saturation itself. On a real actuator, a limiter changes the closed-loop
dynamics, so test it separately. Tracking a non-zero reference requires deviations from an
equilibrium and the corresponding u0; simply inserting absolute x into −Kx drives it towards zero.
LQG combines a linear Kalman filter with LQR. The separation principle applies under specific linear
conditions; it provides no automatic stability guarantee for delays, saturation, nonlinearities or EKF.

Task 5. LQR on an axis with true state
Use Ad and Bd from task 1. 1) Specify two sets of normalised weights: prioritising accuracy and
prioritising small torque. 2) Calculate K and the poles of Ad−BdK. 3) Check stabilisation at zero and
a small step change of equilibrium. 4) Add the same limit on u. Deliverable: two responses and a
table of RMSE, peak command and the integral u²dt in N²·m²·s. Check: predicted poles are inside
the unit circle for the linear case; under saturation, support the conclusion with a separate
experiment. Failure case: weights designed for degrees are applied to radians without conversion.

Task 6. Comparing PID and LQR under identical conditions
Take the PID with frozen settings from M10. First compare it with LQR under equal access to true
state or measurements; state explicitly which controller receives velocity. Then connect KF and
repeat the noisy cases. Use the same plant, limits, Ts, initial conditions, disturbance and test seeds.
Deliverable: a table of accuracy, control effort, computation time and saturation fraction. Check:
tuning uses a separate scenario set; the final set is not used to fit weights. If LQR wins through
access to true velocity, describe this as an information advantage rather than an advantage of the
algorithm itself.
Separately compare an inaccurate model and estimation delay. Make the conclusion specific: which
controller is better for the chosen axis and conditions, where behaviour differs and which added
complexity is justified. LQR superiority is not a required outcome of the exercise.

СтраницаPage 161 · QP: allocating forces between two supports
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

QP: allocating forces between two supports

Variables, geometry and dimensions
Model: two point supports in the x-z plane, with coordinates relative to the body centre
r1=(−a,−h), r2=(a,−h), where a,h are in metres. The unknown vector is f=[fx1,fz1,fx2,fz2]ᵀ; all four
components are in newtons. Contact pushes upward: fzi ≥ 0. The prescribed force-and-moment
vector, or wrench, w=[Fx,Fz,My] has component units N, N and N·m. From r×f, obtain
My=−h·fx1+a·fz1−h·fx2−a·fz2. Thus A is 3×4 with third row [−h,a,−h,−a]; the first rows sum fx
and fz.
To avoid directly adding squared N and N·m values, define D=diag(1/Fref,1/Fref,1/Mref). Minimise
||D(Af−w)||² + λ||f/Fref||² with λ>0. Constraints: 0 ≤ fzi ≤ Fmax_i and −μfzi ≤ fxi ≤ μfzi; μ is
dimensionless. This is a planar friction cone with linear boundaries and a convex QP. Label
a,h,Fref,Mref,Fmax and μ as illustrative values or measurement-derived values. Contact forces do
not yet convert automatically into real actuator commands; that will later require Jacobians and
model validation.

Task 7. A feasible allocation
Take symmetric geometry and request Fx=0, Fz=mg, My=0. 1) Write A and the bounds. 2) Solve
the QP. 3) Check fz1=fz2 for symmetric limits. 4) Add a small My and explain the load transfer. 5)
Increase Fx until the friction boundary is reached. Deliverable: a computational notebook, forces at
each support, a normalised residual and active constraints. Check: independently recalculate Af,
every bound and the moment sign. Do not trust solver status alone: check residuals in physical
units with an explicit tolerance.

Task 8. An unreachable request and solver failure
The problem with the soft objective above usually has a feasible solution f=0, so separately add
the equality Af=w and require Fz>Fmax1+Fmax2 to create a deliberately infeasible request. Then
check premature termination at the iteration limit and an artificially late result. Record status,
residual, iteration count and time; compare cold and warm starts on the same request sequence.
Deliverable: p50, p95, p99, maximum and the fraction of unusable solutions. The fallback mode
uses only a previously validated action for the current constraints; a previous solution cannot be
repeated unconditionally after losing contact.

СтраницаPage 162 · A common experiment and component
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

A common experiment and component
compatibility

Three connected experiments
Part A - axis: model → sensor → KF → PID or LQR → limiter → model. Part B - tilt: gyroscope and
accelerometer → EKF → log of estimates, errors and rejected updates. Part C - force allocation:
requested wrench → QP → independent constraint check → admissible output or fallback mode.
Align units, timing and scenario format. QP forces cannot be inserted into the joint model without a
physically justified transformation; a full model of a balancing robot is not required this month.
The axis scenario contains J, b, Ts, noise, initial state, u limits, seed and reference trajectory. The
EKF scenario contains the θ trajectory, true gyroscope bias, noise intensities and intervals of
additional acceleration. The QP scenario contains support coordinates, μ, force limits, requests and
time limits. Label all synthetic parameters as synthetic; measured contains only physically
measured data.

Meaningful metrics
For the axis, calculate angle and velocity RMSE, peak command, the integral of squared torque and
saturation fraction. For state estimation, calculate RMSE against simulation ground truth,
innovation mean and temporal correlation, NIS and the fraction of rejected updates. For QP,
calculate the wrench residual in physical and normalised units, maximum bound violation, solution
time, iteration count, status and the number of transitions to fallback mode. Laptop timing applies
only to that machine and configuration and does not guarantee the same speed on a
microcontroller.
Use one set of seeds for parameter selection and a separate held-out set for final validation. Before
increasing the run count, try small limiting cases: zero state, zero load, symmetric supports and a
missing measurement. Save at least one case you cannot explain and make it an open task with a
minimal reproducing example.

Files and reproduction
The README describes mathematical models and applicability limits; config stores units and
normalising scales; tests checks transitions, Jacobians, matrix dimensions and constraints. reports
contains matching plots for all compared algorithms and a separate fault page. The reproduction
command must recalculate aggregates from saved logs; repeating a simulation with pinned
versions and seed must give statistically and numerically consistent results. Do not require bitwise
equality across different BLAS libraries, operating systems and solver versions without a separate
check.

СтраницаPage 163 · Six tests for incorrect solutions
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Six tests for incorrect solutions

Estimation and modelling
F1 - unobservable absolute angle. Two states differ only in q; the sensor sees v on a free axis.
Expected: identical measurements; the estimator must not confidently “recover” an unknown
offset without additional information. Deliverable: two trajectories and an explanation of which
sensor or constraint would change the situation.
F2 - missing encoder samples. Remove several consecutive measurements while retaining the true
motion. Expected: prediction continues, updates are skipped and uncertainty changes according to
the model. An incorrect variant repeats an old measurement as new and artificially reduces P;
include it as a negative test.
F3 - an IMU outlier and linear acceleration. Introduce one large outlier and a separate sustained
acceleration interval. Expected: gating flags the outlier; do not hide the sustained effect by
claiming that an accelerometer always measures gravity alone. Compare the number of rejected
updates and accumulated drift; separately record resumption of updates.

Control and optimisation
F4 - inaccurate model and LQR saturation. Increase J, add delay and constrain u to the same limit
as PID. Expected: measurable changes; the original model’s linear poles are not used as proof of
stability for the saturated system. The report shows where the chosen controller’s advantage
disappears.
F5 - an infeasible QP with hard equality constraints. Request a vertical force above the sum of the
limits with Af=w. Expected: an unusable status is handled before publishing a command; the log
contains a reason rather than an empty vector. Alongside it, show the soft problem with a non-zero
residual to distinguish an optimal approximation from exact fulfilment.
F6 - a late or non-finite solution. Substitute NaN for the output or delay it until the next step.
Expected: checks of finiteness, compatibility with current contacts and the computation deadline
reject the result. Also recheck the last admissible solution against new constraints; if a support has
disappeared, its old forces are no longer permitted.

Analysis and correction
For each test, save inputs, the expected event and the actual event. Check dimensions and
normalisation first, then the model, and only then Q, R or solver settings. Do not reduce R merely
because an estimate looks smoother, or weaken physical constraints to remove an infeasible
status. The corrected version must pass the same original scenario; any criterion change requires
an explanation and a new experiment identifier.

СтраницаPage 166 · Acceptance: explain and reproduce the
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Acceptance: explain and reproduce the
solution

What to demonstrate without prompting
Begin with the axis’s two-dimensional state and give every matrix dimension. Show an
unobservable case, then a successful KF and a poor covariance choice. Explain the EKF Jacobian
and demonstrate its comparison with finite differences. Next, show an identical test for PID and
LQR and a solved QP with a manual check of total force and moment. Finish with a forced solver
failure and the log of transition to fallback mode.
Readiness criteria: state-transition tests pass; every sensor has a measurement model and units;
covariance is not treated as an arbitrary confidence percentage; innovations and missing
measurements have been investigated; tuning is separate from validation; QP constraints are
checked independently; timeout, infeasible and non-finite results are handled. Justify how well
innovation statistics agree with the assumed noise model. A histogram’s appearance alone is
insufficient.

Self-check questions
1) Why can two different states produce the same measurement? 2) How does poor conditioning
differ from formal rank deficiency? 3) When is linearisation needed, and how do you check its
validity region? 4) Why can a filter not keep updating indefinitely with an old number after a packet
is lost? 5) How does Q_noise differ from Q_cost? 6) What are the units of R for an accelerometer?
7) Why does increasing the filter’s confidence not guarantee a smaller error? 8) Where is LQR
action limited? 9) What changes when an angle is converted to degrees without normalisation? 10)
Why can a QP with a soft residual penalty remain feasible for an infeasible request? 11) Why do
force and moment need different cost scales? 12) When can the last successful solution no longer
be used? Relate every answer to a saved negative test.

Handover to the next module
Prepare field-level definitions of StateEstimate, SensorSample, ControlRequest and ControlStatus:
timestamp, coordinate frame or axis, units, value, covariance or quality status, and scenario
identifier. Do not create ROS interfaces before M12, but record which component produces each
field and which state is considered stale. Separately list frequency, admissible age and diagnostic
requirements.
Numerical experiments do not close unfinished physical checks. As specified by the final project,
this month can be completed entirely on models with known parameters; transfer to real
equipment remains a separate, justified step. If reducing scope, retain one linear axis, one tilt EKF
and a two-support QP. Complex three-dimensional models and rewriting all algorithms in a third
language are optional.

СтраницаPage 168 · Key terms and definitions
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Key terms and definitions

State. A vector of variables sufficient to predict the model’s subsequent motion given known
future inputs.
Operating point. The state and input around which a system is studied; equilibrium additionally
requires an unchanging state.
Linearisation. A local approximation of nonlinear equations using first derivatives with respect to
state and input around a chosen operating point.
Controllability. The ability to move a linear model between arbitrary states in finite time using an
input admissible under the problem formulation.
Observability. The ability to determine a model’s initial state uniquely from its output history with
known inputs.
Covariance matrix. A matrix describing the joint variability of random errors; the diagonal
contains variances, and each element’s units are products of component units.
Process noise. A random input representing uncertainty in modelled state evolution; its
covariance is denoted Q_noise.
Measurement noise. The random component of sensor error in the observation equation; its
covariance R_noise refers to the measured quantities.
Innovation. The difference between a new measurement and the predicted measurement before
updating; it signals disagreement between data and prediction.
Kalman gain. The matrix mapping innovation to a state correction, determined by the
measurement model and estimated covariances.
Kalman filter (KF). Recursive state estimation for a linear model through prediction and update;
optimality requires stated noise assumptions.
Extended Kalman filter (EKF). An estimator for a nonlinear model using local Jacobians to
propagate covariance and update from measurements.
LQR. Feedback that minimises a quadratic cost of state and actuation for a linear model under
specified problem conditions.
LQG. The combination of LQR and Kalman estimation in a linear problem with Gaussian noise and a
quadratic criterion.
Quadratic programming (QP). Optimisation of a quadratic objective subject to linear equalities
and inequalities; convexity requires a positive semidefinite quadratic form.
Feasible solution. A variable vector satisfying every problem constraint within declared
numerical tolerances; optimality is checked separately.
Constraint residual. A quantitative measure of equality or inequality violation, calculated from
returned variables independently of the solver message.
Fallback control. A predefined admissible action when estimation or optimisation fails, consistent
with the system’s current limits.
Check the relationships: x[k+1]=Ad·x[k]+Bd·u[k]; with u=-Kx, the closed-loop matrix is Ad-BdK.
Command limiting changes the linear model.

СтраницаPage 170 · Motion fundamentals: state and support
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M11  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Motion fundamentals: state and support
forces

Required: what a sensor allows you to reconstruct
Joint state x = [q, v] stores angle and velocity for prediction. One angle measurement does not give
velocity; angle history and a known input allow it to be reconstructed. Before calculating, explain
why the same q with different v produces different leg motion, and draw the ground forces on the
body through two supports.

From measurement history to velocity
A fixed-base joint without friction or gravitational torque: q′ = v, Jv′ = u. q is in rad, v in rad/s, J in
kg·m² and u in N·m with the same positive direction as q. For constant u over interval Ts, the exact
model is q1 = q0 + Ts·v0 + Ts²u/(2J); v1 = v0 + Ts·u/J. Time, input and parameters must be
known.
Let J = 0.02 kg·m², Ts = 0.10 s and u = 0.04 N·m; the sensor reports q0 = 0.20 and q1 = 0.24 rad.
The acceleration contribution to angle is 0.01 rad. Therefore v0 = (0.24 − 0.20 − 0.01)/0.10 = 0.30
rad/s, and v1 = 0.50 rad/s. A simple angle difference would give the mean velocity 0.40 rad/s,
rather than v0 or v1.
When measuring q, the two observability rows are [1, 0] and [1, Ts]; they are independent for Ts ≠
0. When measuring only v, both rows are [0, 1]: an arbitrary constant shift in q is invisible. A
Kalman filter cannot create this missing information. With noise, reconstruction becomes
estimation with uncertainty, making R, Q and timestamps essential.

From desired motion to admissible forces
Model two point supports in a right-handed frame: x forward, z upward, moment My about +y.
From the centre of mass to the supports, r1 = (−a, 0, −h), r2 = (a, 0, −h). Contact forces f act
from the ground on the robot. If horizontal forces are zero, Fz = fz1 + fz2 and My = a(fz1 −
fz2). These are force and moment sums; QP seeks an admissible allocation.
For m = 2 kg, g = 9.81 m/s², a = 0.20 m, Fz = mg = 19.62 N and My = 0.40 N·m, obtain fz1 − fz2 =
2 N, hence fz1 = 10.81 N, fz2 = 8.81 N. At My = 0, both forces are 9.81 N. A non-zero resultant
moment specifies angular acceleration of the body; this is no longer static equilibrium. With a limit
of 12 N per support, a request Fz = 30 N is infeasible because the total cannot exceed 24 N.
Support forces are not yet joint commands. Their generalised external action is Jᵀf; the actuator
accounts for gravity and required dynamics, and opposes external action when holding. Check only
force allocation here.

Exercises and verifiable results
1. In task 2, compare initial q = 0.20 and 0.70 rad with the same v and input. Save two angle and
velocity histories: v measurements will agree, while q differs by 0.50 rad. 2. In task 7, compare the
manual forces with the solver and record sums and moment; then, in task 8, request 30 N with a
hard equality and check infeasible. For the soft problem, check the residual rather than expecting
the same status.
Time: 1 theory hour each from 7-8 (observability) and 61-62 (support forces); 1 practice hour each
from 15-16 (task 2) and 66-67 (task 7). These calculations belong to existing tasks within the 75
hours; floating-base dynamics comes later.
Read: Lall, EE363, Observability and state estimation, slides 3-11; Lynch, Park, Modern Robotics
§5.2: the relationship between forces and joint torques.

СтраницаPage 171 · ROS 2 as a testable robot software system
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

ROS 2 as a testable robot software system

M12 • 12 Sep 2027 - 14 Oct 2027 • 75 hours

This month’s deliverable
You will combine individual models, drivers and controllers into a reproducible multi-node system.
The final telemetry-and-control stack v1.0 includes custom interfaces where needed, specified QoS,
separated callbacks, coordinate transforms at the correct time, a software simulator of the
hardware with lifecycle management, diagnostics and replay of a recorded fault. This is the
software foundation for the legs and hand; one leg and one representative finger in separate
namespaces are sufficient for now.
Use this architecture: an IMU or joint data source publishes data; an estimator outputs state; a
controller produces a bounded request; the hardware layer executes authorised commands; a
monitor checks freshness and state; and a recorder saves the experiment. One component owns
each physical resource. Activate control after checking readiness; the presence of a topic, a
message publication channel, in the graph does not establish sensor or actuator readiness.

Environment and prerequisites
The main programme route uses ROS 2 Jazzy on Ubuntu 24.04. Packages support amd64 and
arm64; on an Apple Silicon MacBook, use an ARM64 Linux environment. State the virtualisation
method, network settings and device access. Test DDS participant discovery, USB passthrough to
the guest, graphics and tracing in a small experiment: their operation depends on the virtual
environment. If the graphical interface causes problems, first run the system from the console and
record data, then state graphics and physical-hardware limitations separately.
Previous months must provide stable telemetry fields, units, monotonic measurement timing,
controller and state-estimation models, and negative tests. Do not rewrite the mathematics when
moving to ROS. Extract validated calculations into a library and call it from a small node so the test
without ROS continues to work. Use C++ for execution-time measurement and the hardware layer,
and Python for scenarios and analysis; a third language is optional.

Completion criteria
The system builds and launches from its documentation; the graph and interface ownership are
clear; QoS and execution choices are justified by measurements. The simulator activates and
deactivates correctly, and a recorded failure can be replayed. Prepare material for the architectural
review and recording replay at checkpoint G2. Its integration hours are separate from these 75
hours. A simulator running in ROS does not close the separate HIL criteria involving real hardware.
State every unconfirmed property in the report.

Organising the 75 hours

Four work blocks
Block A, hours 1-20: graph, messages and launch. Block B, 21-40: DDS, QoS and callbacks. Block C,
41-60: TF2, URDF and hardware-component lifecycle. Block D, 61-75: diagnostics, recording and
replay. Each of the first three blocks contains 10 hours of theory and analysis and 10 hours of
practice; the fourth contains 5 hours of analysis and 10 hours of practice. Total: 35 + 40 = 75
hours. The work steps on pages 9-10 expand these same hours and require no additional time
allocation.
Divide each ten-hour theory block into five two-hour sessions: 20 minutes reviewing the previous
model, 45 minutes reading the relevant section, 40 minutes deriving a small example or examining
a log, and 15 minutes recording the conclusion. Also divide the ten-hour Sunday practical session
into five two-hour periods with breaks between them. Breaks are excluded from net study hours.
Allocate the final five hours of analysis as 2 + 2 + 1.

Start with the question, then choose the tool
The main environment is ROS 2 Jazzy on Ubuntu 24.04, colcon, rclcpp for C++ and rclpy for Python;
also use rosbag2, ros2_control, tf2 and one plotting tool. Begin each session with a testable
question: how does the input affect the output, which state cannot be observed, and which data
reveal its changes? Before running, write down the expected sign, scale or sequence of events.
Compare the prediction with the result and examine at least one discrepancy. Accompany every
plot with an explanation of the observed relationship.
Maintain one repository with model, config, experiments, tests and reports directories. Every
experiment needs a unique identifier, code version, configuration, parameter source, initial state,
units and raw data. The analysis script reads a saved experiment and builds the report without
manually correcting measurements. The final ROS 2 telemetry-and-control stack v1.0 project
combines telemetry and control; individual exercises gradually form its test suite.

Time accounting and reducing scope
Calendar boundaries may coincide with an adjacent module. Keep rest days, holiday intervals and
integration checks as specified in the overall calendar; place numbered steps in available time
without counting hours twice. Do not add hours to this module. Assess equipment and library
readiness at the outset rather than spending the practical session on an unplanned platform
change.
If you fall behind, reduce the dashboard to four plots and retain one hardware simulator and one
way of composing nodes in a process. Preserve the interface-ownership table, QoS experiment,
callback-delay measurements, TF at measurement time, lifecycle check and automated fault
replay. A second visualisation tool and porting nodes to Rust are optional. If tracing or a physical
driver is unavailable, name the specific untested criterion; architectural validation on a simulator
does not replace HIL.

ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Graph, interfaces and launch

Study how nodes interact
A topic suits an IMU or joint-state stream; a service suits a short configuration or state request; an
action suits a long-running motion with feedback and cancellation. A parameter stores a setting but
does not replace a reference stream on every cycle. Study nodes, topics, services, actions and
parameters, then launch, namespaces and composition of nodes within one process. Composition
changes data transfer and failure consequences; the number of logical components need not equal
the number of processes.
First use standard sensor_msgs/Imu and JointState messages wherever they express the intended
meaning accurately. A custom message is needed for fields missing from the interface description:
command identifier, failure reason, state version or associated quality flag. Study conversion of
.msg, .srv and .action to IDL, bounded arrays and strings, and serialisation. State units and
coordinate frames for every quantity, and the time source for timestamp. Version semantic
changes, as well as package names.

Task 1. Interfaces for one leg and finger
Inputs: definitions from M11, one leg with known joint names and one software finger simulator. 1)
Draw a graph containing source, estimator, controller and monitor. 2) Create a field-ownership
table. 3) Create an interface package and two minimal publishing and checking nodes. 4) Launch
/leg and /hand in separate namespaces. Deliverable: an interface document, messages and a
working example. Check: angles in rad, gyroscope angular velocity in rad/s and acceleration in
m/s²; map joints by name rather than arbitrary array position. Error to detect: graph inspection
reveals two publishers simultaneously setting the same reference configuration.

Task 2. Controlled launch and cancellation
Create a launch file for two rig instances, YAML parameters and an action for a small simulated
joint motion. Handle goal, feedback, result and cancel; after cancellation, the simulator must enter
the specified stopped state. Validate parameters before activation. Save one launch command and
a cancellation scenario. Check: package resources can be found from another working directory;
reject an invalid limit or unknown joint name with a clear reason. Endless respawn must not hide
errors, and restarting must not resume motion on its own.
Separately compare nodes in different processes with components in one container. At this stage,
measure correctness of names and data; assess performance gains from intra-process
communication through measurements in the next block.

СтраницаPage 174 · DDS, QoS and callback execution
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

DDS, QoS and callback execution

Study delivery versus freshness
RMW connects the ROS API to middleware; DDS discovery finds participants, and a domain
separates graphs on the chosen network. Record RMW_IMPLEMENTATION, ROS_DOMAIN_ID and
network conditions. QoS includes reliability, durability, history and depth, deadline, lifespan and
liveliness. Study compatibility between offered and requested profiles: incompatible nodes can
appear in the graph without exchanging messages. Reliable mode does not guarantee that a
command reaches the application fresh by its deadline.
For a sensor stream, freshness may take priority over complete delivery; motion commands need
an explicit sequence number, age and retry policy. A new subscriber must not accidentally replay
an old stored command because of transient_local. A deadline event reports a violation of expected
periodicity, but the application implements stopping. History depth N limits the message queue but
does not itself specify maximum delay. Check the combination of policy and actual behaviour of
the chosen RMW.

Task 3. QoS profiles and message loss
A source publishes N numbered measurement packets at a known frequency. Create three
compatible profile pairs and one deliberately incompatible pair; add a slow subscriber and a late
start. Record transmitted, received, duplicate and missing sequence numbers, message ages and
QoS events. Deliverable: a profile → observed behaviour table. Check: count missing packets by
seq within one source and session; do not treat a restart as a huge negative counter jump. Error
check: a bag recording made with incompatible recorder QoS cannot be considered complete.

Task 4. Callbacks that delay control
Implement a fast telemetry callback and deliberately slow processing or a service. Compare
SingleThreadedExecutor, MultiThreadedExecutor with one mutually exclusive group, and a version
with separate groups. In C++, measure callback start and end, queue waiting time and
publication-to-callback-start delay on a common time scale. Save p50, p95, p99 and maximum
distributions and a group diagram. Check: additional threads need not speed up callbacks in one
mutually exclusive group; a blocking request from a callback must not cause an unnoticed
deadlock.
Repeat the correct configuration with intra-process communication and state the message-transfer
method actually supported. Compare copy counts and latency only for the measured configuration:
do not treat zero-copy transfer as a property of every ROS2 exchange. Isolating computation helps,
but does not itself turn a general-purpose operating system into a hard real-time system.

ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

TF2, URDF/Xacro and the hardware lifecycle

Study coordinate transforms at the correct time
Describe the tree base_link → imu_link and base_link → hip → knee → foot; use separate names for
the finger. TF2 stores timestamped transforms and answers queries for a selected instant. The
latest available transform may differ from the transform at measurement time. Study static and
moving coordinate frames, buffering, timeouts, extrapolation and handling of a missing link. An
incorrect coordinate frame or timestamp can cause a spatial error that resembles a filter error.
In URDF/Xacro, distinguish visual, collision and inertial. Mass is in kg, centre of mass in metres and
inertia in kg·m²; check the tensor’s positivity and physical meaning. A detailed mesh may be used
for visual, with a simplified mesh for collision. The joint axis and limits must match the CAD model
and actuator. ros2_control provides hardware state and command interfaces; read and write
connect them to the device. A hardware component’s lifecycle and an ordinary node’s lifecycle are
related by the architecture but belong to different objects.

Task 5. Foot position at measurement time
Use the M5 geometry and a test joint trajectory. 1) Create a leg Xacro and a separate IMU
coordinate frame. 2) Publish joint states and tree transforms. 3) Transform a foot point into
base_link at the measurement time specified by timestamp. 4) Compare the result with a hand
calculation and kinematics from earlier months. Save the URDF, frame tree and coordinate test.
Check: a known zero configuration gives the expected values in metres; a late measurement
requests a historical transform. If a transform is missing or stale, produce a diagnosable failure
rather than a zero point.

Task 6. Hardware simulator: preventing premature commands
Create a minimal ros2_control hardware component with position state and command interfaces
for selected joints. Configure checks names and limits; activate enables commands after obtaining
an initial state; deactivate puts the simulator in the specified mode. Read returns synthetic
feedback; write applies limits and updates a counter. Save the package, controller manager
configuration and transition test. Check: no motion is executed before activation; a read or write
error triggers the expected state and event. The simulator validates interfaces and logic; check the
real driver, delays and physical stopping separately.

ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Diagnostics, tracing and fault replay

Study tools for observing the software
A log explains an individual event; a diagnostic status describes component state; a metric shows
behaviour over an interval; tracing reveals execution order and duration. Monitor IMU and
joint-data freshness, hardware-layer state, controller errors, missing-message counters, command
age and recording load. Every warning must contain a reason, timestamp and recovery condition. A
permanent “OK” line does not provide this information.
Rosbag2 records messages and their timing information. Save parameters, code versions,
random-number seeds, hardware events and external clocks separately. Reprocessing a recording
does not guarantee the same thread-scheduling order. For a reproducible experiment, fix the initial
state, use_sim_time, /clock source and input-order rules. Events sharing a timestamp may require a
custom seq or a deterministic handler in the test.

Task 7. Recording, dashboard and causal sequence
Record IMU data, joint states, estimates, commands, diagnostics and the required TF. Save
parameters and a version manifest. In PlotJuggler or Foxglove, create one dashboard: reference
and angle, IMU age, hardware-layer state and controller error. Then delay the source and trace
sensor data stale → monitor detects → command blocked. Deliverable: a bag recording, dashboard
configuration and a brief report. Check: the original measurement sequence number and every
transition are visible; the event does not disappear when switching plots. Compare source and
recording counters to assess bag completeness.

Task 8. Automated fault replay
Create a launch_testing test: start the system with the simulator, wait for readiness, replay a fixed
bag and verify the fault event. Add a timeout and terminate all processes. Separately enable
ros2_tracing for one callback-delay case if the Linux environment supports the chosen tracing
mechanism; state environment limitations. Check the exit code, result contents and system state
after the test. If a node fails to become ready or hangs during shutdown, the test must fail rather
than wait indefinitely.
Define the required repeatability: matching diagnostic events and values within tolerance, or an
identical sequence of processed messages. Do not call a recording deterministic merely because its
file is unchanged. State the controlled sources of nondeterminism and any remaining differences in
delays measured by physical clocks.

СтраницаPage 177 · Requirements for the ROS 2 v1.0 system
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Requirements for the ROS 2 v1.0 system

Packages and responsibilities
robot_interfaces contains only messages, services, actions and unit descriptions. robot_description
stores Xacro and meshes. robot_core contains calculations without ROS dependencies; robot_nodes
calls them from estimator, controller and monitor nodes. robot_hardware provides the hardware
simulator; robot_bringup stores launch and YAML; robot_tests stores integration scenarios;
experiments stores version manifests and recordings. Packages may be combined if these
responsibility boundaries and the absence of cyclic dependencies are preserved.
Choose one flow: mock_joint/imu → estimate → control_request → hardware. The monitor receives
independent freshness indicators and permits or prohibits activation. The command interface has
one owner; the diagnostic dashboard does not bypass it to write commands. For every graph edge,
record message type, units, QoS, frequency, time source and stale-data behaviour. Namespaces
allow a second hand instance to launch without changing source code.

Aligning time
Within a process, measure durations with a monotonic clock. A ROS message timestamp provides a
shared time reference and supports TF; across multiple machines, declare the synchronisation
method or restrict one-way latency measurement to one machine. Do not subtract clocks from
different devices and call the difference transport latency without estimating their offset.
Separately measure publication period, callback start, callback duration and data age when a
command is calculated.
Changes to system time or /clock must not silently change freshness monitoring. Choose virtual
time in advance for replay, and a defined stable time base for hardware freshness checks. When
replay pauses, controller behaviour must match the selected mode. Indefinitely repeating an old
physical command is unacceptable. Test replay on the simulator using a separate namespace and
configuration.

Reproducibility and documentation
One command builds the workspace, another starts the simulator and a third runs checks. State
dependencies, tested OS and architecture, terminal procedure and expected topics. The report
contains the graph, QoS table, lifecycle diagram, callback measurements, recorded failure and a
test link. Building from a clean directory checks paths to installed resources, rather than accidental
absolute paths from your computer.
Dashboard snapshots provide a quick overview, but the bag, manifest and calculated metrics
remain the primary evidence. The project rests on clear responsibilities: who produces data, who
makes decisions and who may operate the actuator.

СтраницаPage 178 · Six integration and fault tests
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Six integration and fault tests

Delivery and execution
F1 - incompatible QoS. Launch a publisher and subscriber with conflicting reliability or durability
requirements and demonstrate the missing expected exchange. Expected: a diagnostic
explanation rather than “the sensor is broken”. Then fix the profile and repeat the same
experiment with N packets, saving counters.
F2 - slow callback. Artificial processing takes longer than the source period. Expected: queue size
and data age grow, or messages are lost according to the profile; measure p99 and the maximum.
Explain how executor and callback-group choices affect the result. An average frequency close to
the target does not confirm data freshness.
F3 - source restart. The source resets seq and temporarily disappears. Expected: a new session_id
distinguishes restart from counter overflow or packet reordering; freshness monitoring detects the
pause; data returning does not automatically activate the device. Record recovery state as a
separate event.

Geometry, hardware layer and replay
F4 - TF from the future or past, and an incorrect coordinate frame. Supply one measurement packet
outside the available buffer and another with an unknown frame_id. Expected: the failure reason is
visible, and no command is generated from an unverified transform. In the corrected case, a known
foot point agrees with an independent calculation within the declared tolerance.
F5 - configure, read or write error. Supply an invalid joint limit, then simulate a hardware error in
the active simulator. Expected: premature activation is prohibited, the cause is diagnosed, and
controllers do not silently keep writing to an invalid interface. Fix the specific sequence of controller
and hardware-component actions according to the installed ros2_control version and the test.
F6 - an incomplete bag and a shutdown hang. Remove a required stream or stop one node before
the scenario ends. Expected: the replay test detects the missing event or data and ends at its
timeout; all processes terminate. A repeated run inherits neither old nodes nor an accidental /clock
from the previous test.

Confirming a correction
Each negative test has a corrected counterpart with identical initial conditions. Record the injected
error, observed event, detection delay, final state and path to the bag or trace. If the cause
remains unknown, leave the status open. Do not substitute increases to every timeout for a
correction: any new time limit must be justified by measurements and control requirements.
Virtual-machine special case: participant discovery may depend on network mode, while tracing
depends on the kernel and access to system mechanisms. Do not hide these environment
limitations under “everything checked”; still complete console and simulator checks, and prepare a
separate rerun plan for any unavailable hardware check.

ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Acceptance and preparation for a digital twin

Demonstrating the working stack
From a clean environment, build the packages, launch two namespaces and show IMU and joint
data flow and action cancellation. Enable a slow callback and explain what happens using metrics.
Finish by replaying a fault bag and checking that the automated test detected the expected event.
Show RViz, counters, hardware-layer state and the absence of processes left running.
Required acceptance checks: build and launch are reproducible; units and data ownership are
documented; QoS is compatible and tested; TF uses measurement time; the simulator handles a
fault correctly and enters the specified state. The recording contains required streams,
repeatability criteria are explicit, and automated tests terminate on both success and failure.
Starting a node alone does not confirm correct command execution.

Self-check
1) When should you use an action instead of a service? 2) Why do parameters not replace a
command stream? 3) How does incompatible QoS appear in the graph? 4) Why does reliable not
mean fresh? 5) How does deadline differ from application-level freshness monitoring? 6) Why do
multiple threads not rescue one mutually exclusive callback group?
7) How do you obtain a transform at measurement time? 8) Why should visual and collision differ?
9) Who owns the command interface? 10) What happens after a read or write error in your
particular stack? 11) Which data outside the bag are needed for repetition? 12) Why can the same
bag run with different delays? Support answers with configuration, a log or a test.

Handover to M13 and the G2 boundary
Pass on the leg Xacro, joint names, hardware interfaces, launch, QoS, bag template and fault
catalogue. This is the framework for a digital twin in Gazebo: the model will replace the hardware
simulator while preserving external interfaces and their requirements. Initial quadruped geometry
in M13 will extend one validated leg; a physical quadruped is not yet required.
Architectural and replay material is ready for G2, but the overall plan also includes a one-leg HIL
criterion developed in M13. This criterion remains open until an experiment with real hardware; a
software simulator does not satisfy it. Reaching the G2 calendar date does not justify assigning
PASS to every item.
If behind schedule, reduce the dashboard to four plots and retain one hardware simulator. Preserve
QoS and execution-time measurements, TF at measurement time and a reproducible failure. If
physical-interface validation or tracing is deferred, state the environment, command, expected file
and specific untested criterion.

СтраницаPage 183 · Terms and definitions
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Terms and definitions

Node. A logical ROS component with its own interfaces; several nodes may execute inside one
process.
ROS graph. The collection of nodes and their communication links discovered within a specified
domain and accessible network.
Topic. A named, typed message stream; publication generally does not acknowledge command
execution by a subscriber.
Service. A request-response interaction for a bounded operation; an action is more suitable for a
long motion with cancellation.
Action. A protocol for a long-running task with feedback, a result and a cancellation request that
the server must handle.
Parameter. A named node setting with a type and change rules; it does not replace a sequence of
control commands.
Namespace. A ROS-name prefix that separates subsystem instances; it does not itself provide
network isolation.
DDS and RMW. DDS implements data exchange; the RMW layer connects ROS to a specific
middleware implementation.
QoS. A set of message-delivery and storage policies; offered and requested profiles must be
compatible for communication.
Reliability. A best effort or reliable delivery policy; retransmission does not guarantee message
freshness by the control deadline.
Durability. A policy governing availability of previously published data to late subscribers;
transient local requires care for motion commands.
Deadline. The expected maximum interval between updates; a violation event reports a problem
and the application implements the response.
Executor. A mechanism that selects ready callbacks and executes them on available threads
according to group configuration.
Callback group. A group of callback functions governed by mutual exclusion or permission for
concurrent execution.
Deadlock. A state of mutual waiting for resources or events in which participants cannot continue
execution.
Timestamp. The numerical time of an event on a specified time scale; measurement time may
differ from message-receipt time.
TF2. A buffered tree of coordinate transforms that supports queries for relationships between
frames at a specified time.
Lifecycle. Explicit component configuration, activation, deactivation and error states, with
permitted transitions between them.
Hardware interface. A contract for reading a resource’s state and writing its command; control
authority must belong to a defined owner.
Replay. Resupplying recorded data with known timing and configuration; the original computation
order may not be reproduced.

What to buy and install this month

USE EXISTING EQUIPMENT
Use the MacBook Pro M4, UTM and Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 installed in M1, Git, CMake, C++ and
Python. A software simulator of the hardware is sufficient for M12; no new onboard computer,
motor or sensor is needed. Boards and measurement tools from M4-M7 will be needed later for HIL.

INSTALL NOW
In the Ubuntu guest, install ROS 2 Jazzy Desktop with RViz, colcon, rosdep, vcstool, ros2_control
and ros2_controllers, tf2, robot_state_publisher, Xacro and rosbag2. Start with the official Jazzy
installation guide. Record arm64 architecture, package versions, RMW and ROS_DOMAIN_ID; do not
mix distributions in one shell or workspace.
First run the ros2_control RRBot demo with simulated hardware. Keep the C++ or Python controller
library independent of ROS. For the interface package, keep IDL: Type system available; define
array sizes, strings and units before building.

AS NEEDED
For diagnostic tasks, use PlotJuggler or an existing graphical analyser. Install ros2_tracing if Linux
supports the chosen mechanism and permissions are available; otherwise save callback
measurements and state the tracing limitation. Add launch_testing to launch processes with a
timeout.

INSTALLATION CHECK
1) Build two minimal nodes with colcon, check talker and listener and discovery on the chosen
network. 2) Open RViz with the leg TF; test UTM graphics in practice. 3) Activate and deactivate the
hardware simulator without spontaneous startup. 4) Record and replay rosbag2 with timestamp
and seq, checking QoS compatibility. Test USB passthrough to the guest before M13 rather than
assuming every virtual machine supports it.
Preparation and these checks replace repeated setup and reading within the current 75 hours. An
installation page does not mean the software is already installed. Buying a licensed copy of the
book is optional if access is available; there are no hardware purchases this month.

СтраницаPage 185 · Motion fundamentals: the physical meaning
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M12  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Motion fundamentals: the physical meaning
of URDF

Required: four descriptions of one link
Which torques will the leg shown in RViz require? Kinematics specifies connections, axes and
transforms; visual specifies appearance; collision specifies collision and contact geometry; inertial
specifies mass, centre of mass and inertia. Before starting, transform one point between two
coordinate frames and explain the distinction between kg and kg·m².
robot_state_publisher computes TF from geometry and joint positions without integrating the
effects of forces. ros2_control defines command and state interfaces. The name effort does not
turn a position servo into a controllable torque source.

One bar: geometry and inertia from dimensions
Base B is fixed in a right-handed frame: x forward, z upward. The joint at the origin rotates about
+y. At q = 0, the link points along +x; positive q lowers its endpoint: p_tip in B = (L cos q, 0, −L
sin q). For L = 0.20 m, q = 0 gives (0.20; 0; 0) m and q = π/2 gives (0; 0; −0.20) m. Mass does not
enter this calculation.
A uniform bar has length L = 0.20 m along the link’s x-axis, width and height d = 0.02 m, and m =
0.30 kg. The link-frame origin is at the joint; its centre of mass in this frame is (0.10; 0; 0) m. Place
the inertia frame at the centre of mass with parallel axes:
Ixx = m(d² + d²)/12 = 0.000020 kg·m²;
Iyy = Izz = m(L² + d²)/12 = 0.001010 kg·m².
Off-diagonal elements vanish by symmetry. In inertial, specify this tensor about the COM and the
centre-of-mass origin; also offset the bar’s visual and collision by L/2.
Inertia about the joint axis is I_joint = Iyy + m(L/2)² = 0.004010 kg·m². The added term
accounts for circular COM motion. Substituting I_joint for Iyy while origin is at the COM counts the
axis transfer twice and distorts dynamics.
At q = 0, gravity (0; 0; −mg) N acts at x = 0.10 m. Its moment about +y is +mgL/2 = +0.2943
N·m; holding requires actuator torque −0.2943 N·m. At q = π/2, the force lever arm is zero. The
sign follows from r × f.
Doubling mass without changing shape doubles inertia and gravitational torque; TF at a given q is
unchanged. Changing visual changes appearance. Enlarging collision geometry changes contact
and clearances but does not establish link strength. The bar checks units; real masses and material
distributions come from measurements or CAD.

Two model checks within hours 41-60
1. Select a test link in the leg description; save its URDF and p_tip from manual FK and TF at q = 0
and π/2. The example tolerance is 10⁻⁶ m for this model. 2. Double the mass in a copy; use a script
to check doubled I and torque and unchanged FK. Save mass, COM, the six I elements and
coordinate frames; principal moments of inertia must be positive.
Time: 1 theory hour from 45-46 (URDF, masses, collision geometry), and 1 practice hour each from
51-52 (leg description) and 53-54 (task 5, TF). These check the existing model within the 75 hours.
Contact comes in M13; no real actuator commands are sent here.
Read: Lynch, Park, Modern Robotics §8.2, Part 1 - COM and inertia; ROS urdf_tutorial,
07-physics.urdf - visual, collision and inertial structure. Do not copy placeholder inertias from XML:
they are calculated here.

СтраницаPage 186 · A digital twin that can be checked against
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M13  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

A digital twin that can be checked against
measurements

M13 • 26 Oct 2027 - 21 Nov 2027 • 75 hours

Monthly outcome
Build a quadruped model in Gazebo, verify it against simple physical examples and connect the
controller in stages: first SIL, then PIL and single-leg HIL with a real processor and communication
channel. Deliver a digital twin with reports on fidelity, timing and HIL testing. The quadruped is an
intermediate architecture on the way to a six-legged robot: physical assembly is scheduled for
M22, and the transition to six legs for the conditional M23 stage.
A digital twin must reproduce a specific geometry and use parameters and measurements from the
actual system. Start with the leg CAD model, actuator specifications and M7-M10 logs. Identify the
sources of mass, inertia, damping, limits, delays and noise. An unmeasured parameter may be
assumed if it is explicitly labelled and given a range for sensitivity checks. A calculated curve must
never be presented as an experimental measurement.

Prerequisites
From M12, you need Xacro, joint names, hardware interfaces, launch files and diagnostics. From
earlier stages, you need controller firmware, the communication protocol, a secured single-leg or
joint test rig, and rules for limiting applied commands. Before HIL, understand every packet field
and the meaning of its timestamps. The model can be developed without an actuator; checking
hardware and actual delays requires a real test rig.
The main environment is ROS 2 Jazzy, Ubuntu 24.04 and Gazebo Harmonic with gz_ros2_control.
ARM64 installation is supported, but verify the particular plugins, graphics, GPU-processed sensors,
virtual networking and device access separately. Running a server without a GUI and rendering
depth images without a window are different modes: the latter still requires a working rendering
engine. Any replacement of missing depth data with ideal values must be explicitly declared.

What the evidence establishes
Check contact, noise and timing quantitatively. Successful simulation does not establish actual
strength, heating, surface friction or emergency stopping. HIL validates operation only within the
declared hardware and software configuration; the physical actuator and foot contact remain
separate experiments when represented by models. The G2 HIL criterion remains open until the
corresponding experiment in this module is completed, even though the checkpoint itself is
scheduled earlier.

СтраницаPage 187 · Organising the 75 hours
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M13  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Organising the 75 hours

Four work blocks
Block A, hours 1-20: SDF, physics and simple reference cases. Block B, 21-40: the quadruped,
sensors and tests without a graphical interface. Block C, 41-60: SIL and PIL, scenarios and timing
boundaries. Block D, 61-75: single-leg HIL and comparison with measurements. Each of the first
three blocks contains 10 hours of theory and analysis and 10 hours of practice; the fourth contains
5 hours of analysis and 10 hours of practice. Total: 35 + 40 = 75 hours. The work steps on pages
9-10 allocate these same hours; do not add them again.
Divide each ten-hour theory allocation into five two-hour sessions: 20 minutes to reconstruct the
previous model; 45 minutes to read the assigned section; 40 minutes to derive a small example or
analyse a log; and 15 minutes to record the conclusion. Divide each block's ten-hour Sunday
practical into five two-hour work periods with breaks between them. Breaks do not count towards
net study hours. Split the final five analysis hours as 2 + 2 + 1.

Start with a question, then choose the tool
The main tools are Gazebo Harmonic, ROS 2 Jazzy and gz_ros2_control; Python for scenarios and
analysis; and the existing microcontroller and physical communication channel for HIL. Begin each
session with a testable question: how should the input affect the output, which state is
unobservable, and what data can establish this? Before running the experiment, record the
expected sign, scale or event sequence. Afterwards, compare the prediction with the result and
investigate at least one discrepancy; producing a plot alone does not complete the task.
Maintain one repository with model, config, experiments, tests and reports directories. Every
experiment needs a unique identifier, code version, configuration, parameter sources, initial state,
units and raw data. The analysis script must read a saved experiment and generate its report
without manual corrections to measurements. The monthly deliverable is a Gazebo digital twin with
fidelity and HIL reports; every exercise adds to its verification suite.

Time accounting and reducing scope
Calendar boundaries may overlap with the neighbouring module. Rest, holiday periods and
integration checks remain as specified in the overall roadmap; place the numbered steps in
available study intervals without counting hours twice. No additional hours are assigned to this
module. Assess equipment and library readiness at the start, rather than spending the practical on
an unplanned platform change.
If you fall behind, reduce visual mesh detail and the number of worlds, and omit the second physics
platform. Retain analytical reference cases, contact verification, the four-leg structure, a sensor
reference scene and a dynamic single-leg experiment. Separate SIL, PIL and HIL results and a table
of discrepancies against measurements are mandatory. Do not add gait generation or RL yet. If the
target processor or physical rig is unavailable, leave that item open and describe its verification
procedure; another run on the host computer does not replace it.




















M13 • 26 Oct 2027 - 21 Nov 2027 • 75 hours                                                                          2 / 15
СтраницаPage 188 · Verify the physics model before adding the
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M13  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Verify the physics model before adding the
robot

Study: the world and the solver
Study SDF world/model/link/joint/sensor, the physics step, gravity, contact and friction coefficients.
Identify the selected physics engine and its available parameters; tag names do not guarantee
identical interpretation across engines. Mass, inertia and collision geometry determine dynamics,
while visual defines appearance. A detailed visual foot may differ from a simple contact geometry,
provided the contact model is explained.
Add joint limits, damping and an actuator model. Ideal torque control, ideal position control and an
actuator with an internal control loop and delay produce different results. First test a simple mass
and a pendulum: their simulations can be compared with analytical calculations. Choose the
physics step by considering convergence and computational cost. A smaller step will not correct an
erroneous mass, negative inertia or incorrect axis direction.

Task 1. Analytical reference cases
Create a freely falling body without contact and a small-angle pendulum. For free fall, compare
with z(t)=z0+v0t−gt²/2 before impact; for the small-angle pendulum, compare its period with
2π√(l/g), provided the model is a point mass on a massless link. Repeat with steps dt and dt/2.
Deliver error curves and a table showing how the metric changes when the step is reduced. Check
units of m, s and kg, identical initial conditions and a fixed duration. Error check: if pendulum
inertia does not match the chosen formula, correct the reference calculation before adjusting
solver settings.

Task 2. Foot contact and an inclined plane
Use a simple block with the mass and contact geometry of a foot. Place it on a horizontal surface,
then vary the inclination. Record penetration, sliding velocity, normal force and energy change.
Compare the onset of sliding with the teaching approximation tan(α)≈μ for the idealised model;
explain the effects of the solver, damping and contact shape. Deliver a scenario series with
tolerances chosen before the final comparison. Check that a block with zero friction cannot remain
stationary on an incline without another cause; any qualitative change when the step is reduced
needs an explanation.
The block deliverable is a set of simple cases with expected physical behaviour and at least one
reproducible contact-model failure. Only then add dozens of links and sensors.

СтраницаPage 189 · The quadruped model and sensors
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M13  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

The quadruped model and sensors

Study: repeatable geometry
Assemble a body and four instances of the verified leg using Xacro. Joint names and axes must
match M12; mirroring the left and right sides requires a separate sign check. Before exporting to
simulation, verify total mass, centre of mass, joint origin/axis, permitted travel, collision geometry
and transmission ratio. Connect command and state interfaces through gz_ros2_control following
the Jazzy/Harmonic conventions. Declaring a transmission does not by itself guarantee that the
plugin applies its reduction ratio.
Add an IMU, joint-state and foot-contact sensors, and a depth sensor. For each, specify its
coordinate frame, units, update rate, noise, delay and ground-truth source. The simulator publishes
ground truth on a separate stream for evaluation; the controller receives only permitted sensor
readings. Ground-truth leakage distorts the assessment of algorithm accuracy. Check IMU tilt using
the adopted gravity convention, and depth against a plane at a known distance.

Task 3. Turn one leg into four
1) Verify one leg in three known configurations. 2) Compare the link endpoint position with an
independent kinematic calculation. 3) Create the remaining instances with their mirroring
parameters. 4) Command the same intended movement on all legs and compare directions. Save
Xacro, SDF, launch files, a table of joints and interfaces, and a geometry test. Check the mass sum
against the parts list, physically meaningful inertias and that the body does not fall through the
floor. If a mirrored leg moves in the wrong direction, the test must identify the specific joint.

Task 4. Sensor reference scenes without a GUI
Create a world with a horizontal platform, a wall at a known distance and a fixed robot position and
orientation. Run the server without a GUI, wait for the streams and record IMU, contacts, joint
states and depth. Prepare an automatic test with a timeout and a report on frequencies, noise and
distance error. A disabled sensor, unavailable rendering engine or empty depth map must produce
an explicit error or be recorded as a limitation. Do not fill a missing stream with zeros. Compare
ground truth and readings at aligned timestamps; model delay separately from publication
frequency.
For the arm, transfer only the architectural principle: parameterised links, joint limits, correct
contact geometry and separate sensor-reading and ground-truth streams. A complete arm and
tactile models are outside this month's scope.
































M13 • 26 Oct 2027 - 21 Nov 2027 • 75 hours                                                                         4 / 15
СтраницаPage 190 · SIL and PIL: where each component runs
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M13  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

SIL and PIL: where each component runs

Study: experiment boundaries
In SIL, the controller runs on the host computer and controls a mechanical model in a closed loop.
In PIL, its code runs on the target processor and exchanges data with the model; this checks the
build, numerical types and calculations on the selected hardware. PIL can run step by step, slower
than real time. HIL in the next block also checks the physical communication channel and the
declared closed-loop timing requirements. Terminology varies between tools, so every report
diagram must show the actual distribution of components.
For each scenario, specify the random-number seed, versions, initial robot configuration and
controller state, world parameters, physics step, noise model, injected fault and expected result. A
fixed seed improves repeatability but does not guarantee bitwise equality for a multithreaded
physics engine across operating systems. Distinguish simulation time (sim time) from real elapsed
time (wall time). Real-time factor = sim time increment / wall time increment; this ratio does not
directly describe whether an individual packet arrives on time.

Task 5. SIL with the same controller
Use the M10/M11 controller library without copying its equations into a new node. 1) Run a fixed
single-leg trajectory. 2) Record error, commands, saturation and contact states. 3) Repeat three
times with the same seed. 4) Introduce sensor delay and additional friction. Deliver a scenario
catalogue and discrepancy report. Check that identical inputs produce results within the declared
numerical tolerance and that the fault scenario survives a restart. If callback order affects the
result, save seq and fix the data-input order in the test.

Task 6. PIL on the microcontroller
Build the computational core for a real target processor, such as the board from earlier modules.
The host sends a snapshot of the leg state; the processor calculates a command and returns
seq/status. In stepwise mode, the model continues only after the specified response. Save the
protocol, firmware hash and a target-versus-host comparison of commands for identical inputs.
Differences between float and double precision must remain within a tolerance justified in advance;
reject NaN and overflow. A damaged packet or missing seq must not result in data being accepted
as a new valid snapshot.
After comparing functionality, measure target computation time and round-trip time separately. Do
not subtract readings from unsynchronised clocks: measure the round trip on one side and local
computation with the processor timer. A PIL result does not yet establish timely control of a
physical actuator.





























M13 • 26 Oct 2027 - 21 Nov 2027 • 75 hours                                                                         5 / 15
СтраницаPage 191 · Single-leg HIL and comparison with real
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M13  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Single-leg HIL and comparison with real
mechanics

Study: HIL requires real hardware
The minimum HIL experiment in this programme uses a real controller with firmware and a physical
USB/UART/CAN channel. They exchange state and command data with the leg model in a closed
loop under timing requirements defined in advance. The controller acts on the model, whose
response returns to the controller. If all computation runs on a laptop, the experiment is SIL. If the
board merely receives and returns a packet without calculating control or affecting the model, the
experiment tests communication but does not yet demonstrate HIL control.
Declare the period, permitted data age, late-data handling and stopping method in advance.
Simulation on the host must meet the chosen timing mode; if performance is insufficient, record
failure of the timing criterion. A slow stepwise run is useful for PIL but does not satisfy timely HIL.
Choose the threshold from your loop's timing budget, rather than a universal number in an
instruction sheet.

Task 7. Close the hardware loop for one leg
Use the verified PIL protocol and connect the firmware to the leg model through a physical channel.
1) Run a small, safe trajectory with bounded commands. 2) Record sim time, host receive/send,
target compute duration and seq. 3) Introduce dropped packets, delay and a disconnected line. 4)
Check the watchdog, fallback mode and resumption through an explicitly defined state. Prepare an
HIL report, firmware, component diagram and fault log. Every cycle must correspond
unambiguously to a state snapshot; reject expired commands. The actuator and contact are
modelled here, so this experiment does not establish physical stopping of the leg.

Task 8. Connect the model to a physical test rig
On a secured real leg or joint, repeat one previously authorised small M10 test and compare
position, delay, settling time and available load information with the model. Use the same
command and consistent initial conditions. Estimate parameters from one set of recordings and
validate on another. Deliver a simulation-versus-measurement table and a list of discrepancies.
Check that you do not fit a single damping value to align every curve while concealing an incorrect
delay or internal actuator-loop model. If the physical rig is unavailable, prepare the procedure and
leave the corresponding validation open.
Use the command limits and mounting arrangements from the already verified mechanics. Do not
connect a real actuator to a virtual environment in a way that lets two controllers set the same
command simultaneously. Before the experiment, explicitly select model-only, HIL-controller or
physical-bench mode.

























M13 • 26 Oct 2027 - 21 Nov 2027 • 75 hours                                                                        6 / 15
СтраницаPage 192 · Digital-twin specification and scenario
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M13  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Digital-twin specification and scenario
catalogue

Project structure
Store geometry and interfaces in robot_description. The simulation directory contains SDF worlds,
physics and sensor settings, and the bridge; scenarios contains initial states, inputs and criteria;
firmware contains the target-processor build; hil_bridge contains the protocol and timeouts; fidelity
contains model and test-rig data; reports contains comparisons and limitations. Record the Git
revision, Jazzy/Harmonic versions, engine, operating system and architecture, physics step, seed
and actuator model in the common manifest.
The mandatory world catalogue contains an analytical reference case, foot contact, a stationary
quadruped with sensors and a single-leg test scene. A complete gait is not needed yet. The
quadruped model must have correct axes, limits and sensor streams, while the dynamic
experiment may use one leg with a fixed body. This reduces the number of simultaneously
unknown causes of discrepancy.

Accuracy requirements by subsystem
For geometry, compare lengths and coordinates in known configurations; for mass and inertia,
compare CAD data and available measurements; for the actuator, compare delay and transient
response; for contact, compare sliding and penetration. Check IMU noise, frequency and delay;
depth-sensor distance and pixel dropout; and communication losses, data age and missed
deadlines. Each table row must give the parameter source, criterion, result, limitations and next
physical experiment.
Do not assign one number such as "digital-twin accuracy 95%". Position error in millimetres and
timing error in milliseconds describe different properties. Set tolerances according to the question
the model will answer: interface testing, step-size selection, controller tuning or contact. A model
may be suitable for watchdog testing and unsuitable for predicting foot slip.

Automating a run
The launch script must open the world, wait for components to become ready, reset the state,
execute the scenario, record streams, check criteria and terminate every process. Account
separately for launch failure, missing clock or sensor, and timeout. Run tests without a GUI first;
check rendering availability separately for depth. Save a machine-readable pass/fail result and a
plot that makes its cause understandable.
Define the HIL boundary in every report: which signals are physical, which are generated, where
the control law runs and how time is measured. A photograph of the board and wiring helps
reproduction, but the evidence consists of commands, responses and the closed-loop model's
reaction to an active hardware controller.
