СтраницаPage 322 · Organising 75 hours and the workspace
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Organising 75 hours and the workspace

Four sequential blocks
Hours 1-20: 10 hours studying construction, power and commissioning procedures; 10 hours of
assembly, inspection and initial power-up. Deliverables: the unit record and power-verification
protocol. 21-40: 10 hours on calibration and communication; 10 hours measuring one actuator,
one leg and then the remaining legs. Deliverables: a machine-readable calibration file and actuator
mapping table.
41-60: 10 hours analysing HIL, contact, IMU and delays; 10 hours comparing the model with real
measurements and rerunning the controller. 61-75: 5 hours analysing standing and the test
programme; 10 hours practising standing, slow stepping, controlled stopping and preparing the
candidate. Total: 35 hours of theory and analysis and 40 of practice; protocol preparation and data
processing are included.

Arranging sessions
Organise each 10-hour analysis block into five 2-hour sessions: begin with a specific question, read
the relevant section, calculate or inspect a log, then decide what to do on the rig. Split the final 5
hours into 2 + 2 + 1. Each practice block comprises 10 study hours in the Sunday practical, with
breaks and alternating assembly, measurement and analysis. Do not operate actuators
continuously for 10 hours: use cooling time to process recordings.
The dates on the first page are the calendar window from the original plan. A boundary date may
belong to two modules; allocate available sessions without double-counting. Retain rest, holidays
and separate integration G blocks from the overall plan. The hour numbering below specifies
workload and order; it does not add evening sessions to the calendar.

Rig organisation
Separate the workspace into unpowered assembly, measurement and potential-motion areas.
Prepare a stable support that holds the body when actuators are disabled, and provide access to
the hardware E-stop. Before starting, specify the permitted motion and stopping condition. Do not
use your hands to hold the legs or body as the primary motion restraint.
Each attempt's log contains run_id, author, Git commit identifier, CAD revision, configuration hash,
initial conditions, expected behaviour and actual outcome. Record interventions separately:
retightening fasteners, replacing a cable or moving the battery. A condition changed during a trial
defines a new experiment. Record a missing measurement as no data, not zero current or zero
error.






























M22 • 03 Sep 2028 - 01 Oct 2028 • 75 hours                                                                         2 / 15
СтраницаPage 323 · Mechanics, mass and load distribution
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Mechanics, mass and load distribution

What to study
Identify the connections that transmit load from body to foot: frame, hip-actuator mounts, links,
shafts, bearings and threaded inserts. Read the insert and fastener manufacturers' guidance for
the material used, together with the test results for your printed parts. Check print orientation,
local cracks and deformation after tightening. No universal tightening torque applies to every
printed connection.
Review centre of mass: r_COM = Σ(m_i r_i) / Σm_i, with masses in kilograms, coordinates in metres
and all r_i expressed in one frame. CAD provides an initial estimate, but measure the mass of
cables, battery and actual actuators. For quasi-static standing, the centre-of-mass projection and
actual contacts help estimate support margin; they do not prove dynamic stability.

Task 1. Record the actual assembly
Inputs are CAD, the parts list, the assembled body and four legs with actuator power disconnected.
1) Assign leg names LF, RF, LR, RR and mark body axes. 2) Weigh assemblies and the complete
unit in one configuration. 3) Compare measured mass with the assembly sum and CAD. 4) Inspect
every loaded connection, insert and clearance throughout the admissible manual movement range,
where the actuator permits manual movement.
Save assembly_manifest.csv, photographs of connections and a discrepancy list. Check that every
loaded fastener and insert has an inspection status, and explain the difference between total and
summed masses considering scale resolution. Boundary case: a cable is trapped only with the leg
bent. Record the collision configuration, reroute the cable and repeat the complete inspection.

Task 2. Check centre of mass and deflection
Use supports or scales with suitable ranges and known contact coordinates. Measure reactions in a
repeatable static configuration and estimate horizontal centre-of-mass position from moment
balance. Repeat after moving the battery between two intended locations. Do not infer
centre-of-mass height from this horizontal-plane measurement; use a model estimate and state its
uncertainty.
Save mass_properties.md with calculations, battery positions and a frame-deflection estimate from
markers or a measuring instrument. Check that centre-of-mass shift agrees with battery movement
and the reaction sum agrees with weight. If a support carries no load, do not count it as a
confirmed contact. Reposition supports and repeat the measurement, then update model inertial
parameters only from established quantities.






























M22 • 03 Sep 2028 - 01 Oct 2028 • 75 hours                                                                        3 / 15
СтраницаPage 324 · Power, cable harnesses and independent
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Power, cable harnesses and independent
motion stopping

What to review before power-up
Trace the power circuit from the battery or supply through protection, switching and distribution to
each actuator. Identify computer and sensor power, common grounds, signal interfaces, cable
strain relief and connectors separately. For each branch, list wire specifications, connector ratings,
allowable conditions, protective device and its time-current characteristic. Comparing a single
current rating is insufficient.
Distinguish controller current limiting, wiring protection, BMS and emergency energy removal. They
serve different purposes and do not replace one another. If the circuit uses a contactor, check its
suitability for DC, voltage, load characteristics and coil-transient suppression against component
documentation. Develop a procedure for the selected circuit here; do not assign generic fuse
values.

Task 3. Wiring checks and staged power-up
Inputs are the de-energised assembly, circuit diagram and component instructions. 1) Check
continuity of intended connections, absence of unwanted connections between power rails, and
connector polarity. 2) Check harness restraint throughout the leg's permitted range. 3) Power the
low-power section and measure voltages. 4) Connect power branches using the approved
procedure, beginning with one supported actuator; do not enable motion yet.
Save powerup_checklist.csv and an oscilloscope trace or log of available voltage and current
measurements. Check that measured polarity and ranges match specifications; explain unexpected
consumption before the next stage. Boundary case: computer supply voltage sags when an
actuator is powered. Return to disconnected actuator power and check inrush current, DC-DC
conversion, ground and connections; increasing a software timeout does not repair a power fault.

Task 4. Demonstrate E-stop operation
Define the physically achievable state after an emergency stop: support by an independent
structure, removal of actuator energy and prevention of automatic reactivation. On a protected rig,
test the circuit with the programme running and with the control process stopped. Record the
button-press instant and an independent indication that force or torque application has ceased,
using a circuit or actuator measurement appropriate to the design.
Save estop_test.md with the circuit, measured response time and residual-motion description.
Derive the timing criterion from admissible displacement and mechanism characteristics. Releasing
the pressed button alone must not resume an earlier motion command: test recovery separately. If
torque removal makes the robot fall, test with support; improve how the safe state is achieved
instead of calling free fall a successful stop.























M22 • 03 Sep 2028 - 01 Oct 2028 • 75 hours                                                                       4 / 15
СтраницаPage 325 · Calibrating 12 actuators and reliable
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Calibrating 12 actuators and reliable
communication

The single-joint model
For each joint, record q = s · k · (n − n0), where q is angle in radians, n is the encoder count, n0 is
the calibration zero, s is +1 or −1, and k is radians per count including the transmission ratio. The
formula applies only to your encoder mode; count wraparound and multiple turns need separate
rules. Do not apply another actuator's conversion factor merely because its connector looks similar.
Separate the mechanism's physical limit from the software operating boundary. The latter must
account for calibration error, backlash, deformation, stopping distance and cable clearance. A limit
recorded in the model still requires verification in the command path. For current and temperature,
state measurement source, scale, offset and interpretation: built-in housing or board temperature
may differ from winding temperature.

Task 5. Identifiers, signs and zeros
Connect one actuator or one leg with support that constrains unexpected motion. 1) Read ID,
model and firmware and match them to the physical label. 2) In the permitted small region,
command a known increment and compare motion with the positive URDF axis. 3) Establish a
repeatable mechanical reference pose and calculate n0. 4) Repeat approaches to the reference
from both directions, then apply the procedure to the remaining joints.
Save calibration.yaml and a table of repeats. Check that all 12 IDs are unique, commands reach the
observed joint, and residual error and backlash measured in radians remain within a tolerance
justified in advance. Boundary cases are a mirrored leg and a swapped cable. The script must
detect disagreement with the hardware map; bus response order alone does not identify which
actuator to enable.

Task 6. Frequency, errors and bus utilisation
First calculate communication time from byte count, bit rate and framing for the actual interface;
add response and direction-switching delays. Then measure the real cycle for 1, 3 and 12 devices
with the same command frequency and telemetry content. For DYNAMIXEL, study Sync Read/Write
and Status Packet; for another bus, use its primary specification. Do not count a missing reply as
packet loss when the protocol specifies no reply to that command.
Save bus_budget.csv, the cycle-duration distribution and counters for timeouts, CRC errors and
retries. Calculate margin to the communication deadline using a measured adverse case and list
untested modes separately. In the driver simulator, suppress one reply: only that joint's data must
become stale, and an old sample must not be republished as new.
To calibrate current, compare the built-in channel with an independent measurement of the same
physical quantity in several permitted modes; record scale, offset and error. Check temperature
against a reference at a comparable location and in steady conditions. A board sensor cannot be
calibrated as a winding sensor by simple subtraction. If the register cannot be corrected, save the
verified conversion model and its limitations in the actuator record.
















M22 • 03 Sep 2028 - 01 Oct 2028 • 75 hours                                                                        5 / 15
СтраницаPage 326 · HIL and comparison with real measurements
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

HIL and comparison with real measurements

What HIL means here
HIL is a test in which part of the real computing or hardware chain operates with a simulated plant.
Draw the boundary: identify which process, controller, driver, bus and sensor are real and which
are replaced. If control hardware is absent, call processing a file on a laptop replay. Match interface
versions, units and timestamps; the HIL label alone does not make a test more accurate.
Tabulate discrepancies between model and robot: mass, link lengths, zeros, command delay,
filters, friction, backlash, stiffness and foot contact. For each, specify its expected effect and
measurement method. Correct geometry and signs first, then timing and dynamics. Simultaneously
tuning many coefficients hides the root cause and does not produce reproducible improvement.

Task 7. Time alignment and control verification
Take a low-amplitude target sequence already verified on the leg and one log of its physical
response. Record command-generation and transmission times, data-reception time and
measurement timestamp if available. Establish the relationship between clocks first; subtracting
timestamps from unsynchronised devices does not measure delay. Plot q_cmd, q_meas and
interface events together, estimate the shift, then replay the same input in the model.
Save fidelity_gaps.csv and a before-and-after report for one justified parameter correction. Check
that input, initial pose and frequency are identical; calculate RMSE on a common time grid and
label it in radians. Boundary case: several samples are lost. Mark the gap and do not present
interpolated values as complete measurements. Check controller changes by reprocessing the
recording dataset before restoring actuator power.

Task 8. IMU and foot contact
With the body secured, check physical axes against frame_id, then test known static tilts using an
external reference. Verify roll and pitch signs and IMU orientation relative to the body. Under
translational acceleration, do not treat tilt calculated from the accelerometer alone as ground truth.
For each foot, compare detected contact against observed touching and unloading, using the
chosen sensor or an indirect estimate with stated uncertainty.
Save imu_contact_validation.md: reference, reference uncertainty, orientation errors and a table of
correct and incorrect contact classifications. Control case: a leg touches the floor but slips; contact
exists, but there is no stationary support. Remove one contact from estimator input and check the
degradation flag. Accompany simulation friction tuning with a surface description; one fitted value
does not characterise all real terrain.
Retain the M19 classical algorithm and M20 force allocator; check QP failure and timeout. Before
operation, establish whether the actuator supports the required torque or current mode. Jᵀf is not a
ready-to-use position command: a position interface requires a justified inner and outer
control-loop design. Keep the M21 policy disabled during initial integration.





















M22 • 03 Sep 2028 - 01 Oct 2028 • 75 hours                                                                         6 / 15
СтраницаPage 327 · Integrated laboratory: standing and the first
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Integrated laboratory: standing and the first
step

Entry conditions and protocol
The assembly may enter this laboratory after tasks 1-8: known calibrations, verified independent
stopping, working diagnostics, and a recording and time-alignment procedure consistent with
measurements. Prepare a level area, foot and body markers, a backup support that carries no
weight during the qualifying stand, a way to observe displacement, and all measurable limits.
Record initial temperature, charge, voltage and battery configuration.
Before starting, specify operating boundaries: body-position region, joint limits, allowable data age,
current, temperature and trial-termination conditions. For every threshold, provide its calculation or
specification, unit and response. Criteria must use measurable quantities rather than descriptions
such as not very hot or a plot colour. Removing torque and controlled lowering are different
actions, selected according to the stopping cause and mechanism capability.

Task 9. Stand for at least 60 seconds
1) On the support, verify coordinated movement of all four legs to the permitted starting pose. 2)
Place feet on their marked locations and gradually transfer load to the robot using your procedure.
3) Run a short trial and inspect currents and contact. 4) Only then run a continuous qualifying
interval of at least 60 seconds. Record roll and pitch, body height and displacement where
measurable, joint errors, currents, temperatures and events.
Save stand_report.md, video showing the backup support and the raw log. Success means
independent standing throughout the interval without crossing declared boundaries or hiding
telemetry losses. Calculate mean and maximum absolute roll and pitch errors separately and state
units explicitly. If the backup support carries weight or an operator supports the body, the attempt
does not establish standing. Do not remove that moment from the evidence.

Task 10. Slow gait and stopping
After standing, perform a limited crawl sequence: transfer the load centre, lift one foot, move it and
confirm touchdown. Begin with one cycle, then attempt a short marked route. Compare initial and
final poses, completed steps and contact losses. A commanded stop must reach the previously
described state; an emergency cause uses the independent stopping path.
Save crawl_run and stop_run with video aligned to logs. Repeat a small, bounded change in tilt or
load under identical conditions, first on the rig; derive method and amplitude from allowable loads
instead of applying a hand strike. Check for recovery into the declared region within a measured
time, or a timely stop. One successful traversal is a demonstration, not proof of reliability.
Separately from the qualifying stand, command a small permitted sequence of body roll and pitch
changes, save target and measurement, and calculate error and settling time. Set amplitude from
available kinematics and loading. This tests command tracking as well as holding one pose; stop
the experiment on joint saturation according to the adopted criterion.


















M22 • 03 Sep 2028 - 01 Oct 2028 • 75 hours                                                                         7 / 15
СтраницаPage 328 · Failure tests and data validity
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Failure tests and data validity

Six required tests
T1 - incorrect ID or sign. Substitute a configuration in the test environment, then verify it by
reading hardware on the rig with actuator power disconnected. Activation must be refused with the
exact joint name. T2 - stale sample. Repeat the last value with its original timestamp in the driver
simulator. The controller must distinguish a missing new measurement from a stationary joint.
T3 - missing reply. Simulate one lost packet, then a sequence of losses; check counters and state
transitions without an automatic hidden reset. T4 - command beyond the limit. Supply an
inadmissible target only to the software path or HIL; verify rejection or documented clamping
before writing to the actuator. This test does not require contact with the mechanical stop.
T5 - emergency stop with a stalled programme. With the robot on a support, stop the control
process and check the independent path for ending force or torque application. T6 - inconsistent
contact. During replay, supply contact during swing or loss of expected support; the system must
report degradation and enter the intended state. Save the input, expected event and observed
sequence for every test.

Heat, current and physical repeats
Also test slowly rising temperature and current indication beyond the set threshold by substituting
telemetry in HIL. This establishes response logic; a separate circuit-specific rig test establishes the
protection's physical ability to remove energy. Do not create a short circuit or overheat a motor to
check a software flag. Load tests remain within the previously calculated range.
State which current is measured: supply current, branch current, phase current or the actuator's
internal estimate. Quantities with different definitions cannot be summed without a model. For
temperature, identify sensor location and sampling interval. Failure to record a peak with
infrequent sampling does not prove there was no peak. Telemetry losses make the relevant metric
incomplete.

Documenting verification
One test_matrix.csv row contains test ID, revision, evidence level, preconditions, stimulus,
expected result, measured result, PASS/FAIL/INCOMPLETE and log link. Run required scenarios first
in the simulator, then only those necessary and permissible on the rig. Do not reproduce physical
faults by dangerously destroying components.
Do not exclude a failed attempt from statistics without a reason defined before the trial. A startup
failure caused by your programme is a result, not bad data. An external-instrument error may
invalidate a trial, but retain the record. Fully analyse at least one real failure or deviation and its
correction: symptom, hypothesis, check, change and repeat.

























M22 • 03 Sep 2028 - 01 Oct 2028 • 75 hours                                                                          8 / 15

ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

The first 40 hours: detailed sequence

Hours 1-10: five 2-hour analysis sessions
1-2: reread the M22 objective, run the original algorithm in simulation or replay and inventory
earlier-module outputs. 3-4: trace load transmission in CAD and list questionable connections and
task 1 measurements. 5-6: calculate centre of mass and plan task 2 reaction measurements; state
method limitations. 7-8: annotate the power diagram, ratings and unknown data, and prepare
continuity testing. 9-10: describe the E-stop, support and restart prevention; rehearse without
motion.
Use the final 15 minutes of each session to record decisions. If a component rating is unknown,
name who will clarify it and the document required. An assumption must not become permission to
power up. Before the practical, prepare a short action sheet with power-up and stopping
sequences, available beside the rig.

Hours 11-20: the first practical
11-13: assembly, labels, inspection and weighing for task 1. 14-15: reaction measurements and
centre-of-mass estimation for task 2. 16-18: wiring, continuity checks and staged power for task 3.
19-20: independent-stop verification for task 4 and evidence recording. These intervals include
instrument setup and documenting results; repeats after finding a defect use time from the same
block.
If the E-stop fails verification, do not start the next motion stage. Use remaining time to repair the
circuit and make passive measurements. The month may end with a candidate that has not yet
passed; retain that status instead of recording an unsupported pass. Calendar pressure does not
relax the mandatory deliverable.

Hours 21-40: calibration and the bus
21-22: encoder conversion and zero definition. 23-24: mirrored legs, axis signs, operating limits
and uncertainty. 25-26: physical meaning of current and temperature readings for the selected
actuator. 27-28: calculate frame size and bus utilisation. 29-30: hardware-component lifecycle,
read-error handling and pre-activation checks. These are five 2-hour analysis sessions.
31-34: calibrate one leg and then the others; record zero-repeatability results. 35-37: compare
communication with 1, 3 and 12 devices and check timeouts in the simulator. 38-39:
parameterised hardware-map and limit tests. 40: inspect after first activation, freeze the
calibration version and prepare a log for model comparison. By the end of this block, physical
names and software indices must map unambiguously.






























M22 • 03 Sep 2028 - 01 Oct 2028 • 75 hours                                                                         9 / 15
СтраницаPage 330 · Hours 41-75: from HIL to a release candidate
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Hours 41-75: from HIL to a release candidate

Hours 41-50: transfer analysis
41-42: define the HIL boundary and tabulate timing in command and measurement paths. 43-44:
estimate delay and comparison limitations from task 7. 45-46: check measured masses, lengths
and contact parameters; choose one significant model correction. 47-48: review IMU conventions,
the tilt reference and contact-trust rules. 49-50: plan estimator and controller regression checks
using original and corrupted logs.
At this stage, read only the required primary-source sections on page 12. Reading must produce a
revised diagram, test or calculation. If dynamics material extends substantially beyond your control
stack, document the model limitation and retain the previously verified controller; this month
integrates material already studied.

Hours 51-60: the third practical
51-53: obtain a low-amplitude physical response from one leg and align it in time. 54-55: correct
one parameter, repeat the same input and record improvement or deterioration. 56-57: measure
the IMU in reference orientations and verify foot contact. 58-59: run T1-T6 in software or HIL and
verify recovery. 60: prepare the complete standing configuration and reinspect harnesses after
movement.
Do not spend the entire block seeking visually perfect simulation-hardware agreement. Establish
the magnitude of significant discrepancies and verify that the controller respects limits in their
presence. Record at least two explained discrepancies and one still unexplained, if present. An
incomplete model is a limitation that can be investigated experimentally.

Hours 61-75: completion
61-62: define standing and roll/pitch tracking criteria, stopping conditions and measurement
methods. 63-64: specify the slow gait, controlled stop and repeatable small disturbance. 65: review
readiness from documentation; state which result permits or blocks M23. These 5 hours are split
into 2 + 2 + 1.
66-68: preliminary and qualifying standing for task 9, with analysis between attempts. 69-71: a
slow gait cycle, short route and normal stop for task 10. 72-73: permissible disturbance repeats
and checks for new defects. 74-75: assemble the candidate package, verify plot reproduction and
complete the progression decision. If time is short, omit video editing, additional routes and
optional optimisation; calibrations, E-stop, standing and raw trial records remain mandatory.

СтраницаPage 331 · M22 acceptance and handoff to the
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

M22 acceptance and handoff to the
six-legged robot

What complete means
The release candidate contains source code and the exact assembly revision; a circuit with ratings
and selection rationale; mass and centre of mass with measurement descriptions; the 12-actuator
map; calibrations and operating limits; hardware-stop documentation; a consistent URDF; HIL,
replay, IMU and contact records; and evidence of independent standing for at least 60 seconds,
slow walking and controlled stopping. During the completed trials, currents, temperatures and
communication parameters remain within operating ranges specified in advance.
Turn the original criterion, no unbounded growth of current, temperature or bus errors, into an
observable check: every signal has a source, sampling interval, limit, response and test duration. A
short normal run does not authorise continuous operation of unknown duration. An unresolved
cause of control loss or an unreliable emergency stop blocks physical scaling.

Engineering self-check
Answer without running the programme: 1) Which joint moves when a chosen ID is addressed, and
why? 2) How was its zero measured, and what is the spread? 3) What happens after emergency
torque removal? 4) Which part of stopping is independent of the main computer? 5) How does a
measurement timestamp differ from recording time? 6) Why does supply current not equal torque
at each joint? 7) How do a new measurement from a stationary sensor and a stale sample differ? 8)
Which simulation-reality discrepancy constrains the next trial?
Practical defence: choose one failed run, open its raw log, reproduce the plot and identify the root
cause or explicitly state the hypothesis still untested. Show which change tests it. Then explain the
power-disconnection chain on the diagram and the axis direction using a physical label. A
screenshot of a successful simulation cannot replace this check.

The M23 package and the separate hand workstream
Create handoff_M23.md: verified quadruped capabilities, test boundaries, problematic parts,
maximum observed bus utilisation and a projection for 18 actuators. Attach the progression
decision PASS/HOLD. PASS means the scaling entry requirements are met; it does not establish
that battery, frame and bus are already suitable for six legs.
For the hand, pass on the calibration.yaml template, diagnostic scheme and method of linking
evidence to a physical unit. Do not copy numerical leg limits to fingers. The hand and
tactile-equipment work in OPT 120 hours remains a separate workstream begun after M17. M22
does not consume its time or present its results as results of this assembly. Completion of both
systems is checked at the end of the overall programme.

СтраницаPage 332 · Assigned reading: quadruped assembly and
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Assigned reading: quadruped assembly and
measurement

The references may be in English; the exercises and definitions are presented here in English. Read
only the named sections before the associated work, within the existing 75 hours.

Core reading
1. K. Lynch, F. Park - Modern Robotics. Sections 4.1.1 and 8.9: forward kinematics in the space
frame; actuation, gearing and friction. For the 12-joint map, connect physical zero and sign to the
model; for current tests, explain the effects of transmission and friction.
2. NASA - Systems Engineering Handbook. 5.2 Product Integration; 5.3 Product Verification;
5.4 Product Validation. Before HIL and floor trials, separate evidence of assembly, compliance with
requirements and suitability of the selected mode. Deliverable: the power-up sequence and entry
criteria for each rig.

Reference book: power problems
3. P. Horowitz, W. Hill - The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed. 9.4 Heat and power design; 9.6
Switching regulators and dc–dc converters. Read selected heating and power-conversion
calculations for task 4. The aim is to understand losses and limits of a ready-made DC-DC
converter; designing a mains supply is unnecessary.

Documents before specific checks
ros2_control, Jazzy. Hardware Components: interface types, lifecycle, errors. For the driver,
specify which states and errors permit command output; relate this to independent stopping.
ROS REP-103 / REP-145. Units, Axis Orientation, Rotation Representation; IMU: Data Reporting,
Common Parameters. For axis and IMU calibration, state the coordinate frame, units and meaning
of acceleration; perform static verification before standing.
The actual bus specification. For DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0: Status Packet, Sync Read/Write, Bulk
Read. For another actuator, use its specification. Calculate communication volume with 12 devices
and the cycle deadline; a similar connector does not establish compatibility.

Separately save specification pages for your actuators, battery, BMS, charger, DC-DC converter and protective
devices: voltage, current, temperature, mode and duration. A textbook example does not establish this
assembly's operating limits.

СтраницаPage 333 · Terms and definitions
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Terms and definitions

Commissioning. Connecting and verifying an assembled device in stages, progressing to the next
mode only after declared criteria are met.
Hardware revision. An identifier for the exact composition and implementation of an assembly:
parts, wiring, sensors and board versions to which measurements apply.
Actuator map. A table linking physical joints to bus addresses, directions, zeros, units and limits;
verified by real movement of every assembly.
Zero calibration. Determining the offset between a sensor reading and a selected geometric
zero, recording the method, conditions and repeatability spread.
Backlash. Relative movement within a transmission when load direction reverses, during which
input motion is not transmitted to the output.
Continuous torque. Torque admissible at specified speed, cooling and sustained thermal
conditions; it must not be equated with short-duration stalled-shaft torque.
Centre of mass. The mass-weighted position of the complete assembly; it changes as legs move
or the battery is repositioned.
Inertia tensor. A matrix describing mass distribution about a selected point and axes; it relates
angular motion to torques, with units kg·m².
Duty cycle. The fraction of time under active load within a declared cycle; together with peaks and
cooling, it affects actuator heating.
Power tree. A diagram of sources, converters, protective devices and loads showing current paths
and points where individual branches can be disconnected.
Voltage sag. A drop in voltage under load caused by source and wiring resistance or supply
limiting; it can reset electronics.
BMS. A system monitoring battery cells and providing specified protection; it does not replace a
compatible charger, fuses and emergency stop.
DC-DC. A DC voltage converter selected for input range, output voltage and current, losses,
cooling and response to transient loads.
E-stop. A specified independent means of ending hazardous motion; the structure may fall after
torque removal, so verify the final state.
Watchdog. Monitoring timely confirmation of correct operation; exceeding the timeout triggers a
predefined response independently of the normal command cycle.
Communication deadline. The latest time for obtaining required data and issuing a command;
exceeding it requires a response even without a packet error.
HIL. Testing in which real hardware interacts with a simulated part of the system; explicitly
document which channels are real.
Specific force. The ideal accelerometer reading associated with a − g in the sensor frame; it is
not directly equal to body acceleration in world coordinates.

Relationships: P = UI; conductor losses P = I²R. Check: disconnecting actuator power and reaching a safe final
state are different facts.

ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Quadruped purchases and setup

USE EXISTING EQUIPMENT
Use the tested 3-degree-of-freedom leg, its bus interface, MCU and IMU, RGB-D camera,
multimeter, CC/CV supply, analyser, tools and Mac M4. For the existing 3D printer, select a profile
for its exact model; replenish consumables and fasteners according to released CAD and BOM.

BUY BEFORE ASSEMBLY - AFTER LEG ACCEPTANCE
9 identical working actuators plus 2 separate spares: 3 + 9 = 12 installed. The family,
voltage, bus, thermal regime and continuous loading have already been verified on the leg. Add
parts for three legs, frame, harnesses and fasteners according to the BOM; the M7 bench DC motor
is not included in these 12.
1 onboard computer: Pi 5 with 8 GB or an Ubuntu-compatible x86 computer after measuring
CPU, RAM and USB loads. Reuse a suitable computer already purchased. The Pi needs 1 boot
medium, cooling and power according to Pi documentation; account for camera consumption
separately. The model name does not guarantee every driver will work.
1 power system: battery, compatible charger and BMS, hardware stop and power disconnection,
branch fuses, DC-DC converter, connectors and wiring. Select ratings after measuring operating
and peak currents, duration, voltage sag and heating; the bench supply limit is not the power
budget for 12 actuators. The number of protective devices matches the branch count.
1 support or backup frame with verified load capacity; 1 IR thermometer with a suitable range
and allowance for surface properties; spare harness components. If choosing contact-sensing feet,
provide 4 channels, one per foot, repeatable activation and calibration for robot mass; these
sensors do not establish absence of slip.

INSTALL AND VERIFY
Onboard, use Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 for Pi or 24.04 x86_64; ROS 2 Jazzy, existing ros2_control, bus
driver and diagnostics from the pinned working environment. Retain the existing environment on
the Mac and in UTM.
Check the build, software simulator and replay without motion; 12 unique IDs; units and sign of one
supported channel; heartbeat loss; current and temperature recording; and independent stopping.
Test USB, network and camera under load on the chosen computer. Do not enable torque
automatically when the OS starts.

For the model: URDF inertial/collision; for logs: Foxglove Plot; for the ID table: pytest parametrization.
Preparation and checks fit within the existing 75 hours, replacing repeated reading and setup. Delivery waiting
time does not count as study time.

СтраницаPage 335 · Motion fundamentals: loading before the
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M22  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Motion fundamentals: loading before the
first step

Required analysis: measured reactions, centre of mass and model limits

Kinematics shows where a foot can be placed. Forces and torques are needed to determine
whether the robot can withstand standing and acceleration. Begin with measurable statics: it
reveals errors in mass, centre-of-mass and load-transmission estimates before gait tuning. The
number of supports alone does not imply equal weight distribution.

Free-body diagram and equilibrium
The example body model assumes a horizontal surface, a stationary robot, gravity and vertical
reactions from two support groups. The x axis points forwards; the rear group is at x=-a, the front
at x=+a; z points upwards. F_r and F_f are ground forces on the robot in N, and x_c is
centre-of-mass position. Force and moment balance give F_r+F_f=mg; a(F_f-F_r)=mg·x_c.
Therefore, F_f=mg(a+x_c)/(2a), F_r=mg-F_f.
Example. m=4 kg, a=0.20 m, x_c=0.05 m, g=9.81 m/s²: F_f=24.525 N, F_r=14.715 N. Adding a
0.5 kg load at x=0.25 m gives total mass 4.5 kg and x_c=(4·0.05+0.5·0.25)/4.5=0.07222 m. The
new reactions are 30.043 N and 14.102 N. Rear loading decreases: the payload adds a moment as
well as weight.

Practice: verify the calculation on the assembled robot
1. Measure mass and grouped reactions in task 2 using existing fixtures and instruments. If an
instrument displays equivalent mass in kg, convert it to N using g. Recover
x_c=a(F_f-F_r)/(F_f+F_r), compare against CAD and include the mass of cables, battery and
mounts. Two sums cannot determine the force at each of four feet.
2. Relate load to the joint. For one adopted pose from M8, calculate J and the force in the same
coordinate frame; the force contribution is τ_ext=JᵀF_ext. During holding, the actuator must
compensate for it while accounting for link weight; compare with the M9 model. Convert current to
torque only through a calibrated transmission model. Do not send a calculated torque to a
position-controlled servo as an angle.

What counts as evidence
Save load_balance.csv: pose, payload, reactions, calculation, residuals, units and instrument
uncertainties. Check reaction sum, moment balance and direction of centre-of-mass displacement.
Set tolerance from scale resolution, repeatability and geometry; do not impose 1% without
justification. A negative calculated reaction means that support is infeasible, not that the foot is
attracted to the floor.

Within 75 hours: 1 hour of analysis in 5-6 and the practical in 14-15 (task 2), without a new motion mode.
This is a quasi-static check: accelerations, slopes and external disturbances require the full model. Read
Modern Robotics §5.2 - the relationship between external force and joint torques.

СтраницаPage 336 · Six legs: scale only what has been verified
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Six legs: scale only what has been verified

M23 • 01 Oct 2028 - 01 Nov 2028 • 75 hours

The completed robot
M23 aims to produce a six-legged robot v1.0 with 18 degrees of freedom, slow walking
and active body levelling: three actuators per leg. It must stand independently for at least 120
seconds, perform wave and ripple gaits under declared conditions, and diagnose loss of data,
contacts and individual components. The central question is what changes when moving from four
legs to six in mechanics, power, communication timing and support control.
18 DOF refers to the number of actuated joint coordinates, not the number of independent body
motions available on the ground. Additional legs provide more contact-allocation options, but
increase mass, energy consumption, wiring and possible faults. Simply appending six IDs to an
array does not validate previous calculations. Analysing the architectural change is a major
practical task.

Entry check before scaling
Open the M22 package: independent quadruped standing, slow gait, functioning independent stop,
calibrations, current and bus budgets, and analysis of significant failures. Record the entry decision
PASS/HOLD in writing. If E-stop, power, actuator identification or the control cycle remain
unverified, physical expansion stays on HOLD. In that case, complete M23 calculations and
simulation tasks while resolving hardware blockers.
The six additional actuators and parts for two legs are planned only after this check, as in the
original plan. Purchasing is not automatic: first verify compatibility, calculate the budget and obtain
the project owner's decision. Changing actuator family for the last two legs requires new
calibrations, a delay model and verification of joint operation.

The operating scope of the result
The ±10-15° range in the overall plan is a design target for body levelling and slope tests,
admissible only where the particular assembly's geometry, stability, traction and loads permit. Do
not adopt it as an operating range before calculation. Start with a smaller verified angle and
expand only when criteria are met. State surface angle and desired body angle separately: they
are different quantities.
The robotic hand develops along its own OPT workstream after M17; M23 leg verification does not
replace its limits or results. Shared logging and diagnostics benefit both systems. The final goal is a
walking robot and hand by programme completion, so pass six-legged-version limitations and
unfinished hand items to M24 and the separate G4 without adding hidden hours.



























M23 • 01 Oct 2028 - 01 Nov 2028 • 75 hours                                                                         1 / 15
СтраницаPage 337 · Work blocks, measurements and scope
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Work blocks, measurements and scope
management

The monthly plan: 35 hours of analysis + 40 hours of practice
1-20: 10 hours recalculating mechanics, power and communication; 10 hours assembling,
calibrating and testing 18 devices. 21-40: 10 hours on contact sequences and admissible
transitions; 10 hours implementing wave and ripple in simulation and on the prepared test area.
41-60: 10 hours on surface, contact and uncertainty estimation; 10 hours on active levelling,
bounded terrain and operation without a camera. 61-75: 5 hours analysing reliability and energy;
10 hours conducting a test series, maintenance and preparing v1.0.
Organise the first three analysis blocks as five 2-hour sessions each; the last is 2 + 2 + 1. Practice
comprises four Sunday blocks of 10 study hours. Alternate movement, cooling, inspection,
resetting initial conditions and analysis. Charging time alone is not study time; use that interval for
calculations and data processing.

One experiment, one question
For every run, record gait type, phase order, cycle duration, swing height, target body tilt, surface,
load, battery condition and temperatures. Begin by comparing two configurations differing in one
parameter. Simultaneously changing gait, surface and controller gain prevents you from identifying
why error changed.
The first-page dates repeat the overall plan's calendar window. Shared boundary dates do not
double hours; holidays and integration G blocks retain their place in the overall schedule.
Work-hour numbers specify task order and do not require extra evening work. Print parts and
arrange components in advance after entry-check authorisation, allowing for actual delivery time.

Reducing scope while preserving the objective
If behind schedule, postpone tripod first, then sideways motion on difficult terrain, then optional
depth-camera comparisons and additional surfaces. Retain wave and ripple, standing, independent
stopping, admissible-slope assessment, operation when the camera is unavailable and transparent
repeated-test results. Without hardware verification of wave and ripple, call the result a candidate,
not a completed six-legged robot v1.0.
Do not consume the hand reserve or G4's 35 hours on minor gait refinements without replanning
the programme. The main deliverable is a justified operating envelope. Python is useful for support
geometry and reports, C++ for the existing control loop. An additional log analyser may be written
in Rust; a third implementation is optional.




























M23 • 01 Oct 2028 - 01 Nov 2028 • 75 hours                                                                       2 / 15
СтраницаPage 338 · The six-legged frame and the 18-actuator
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

The six-legged frame and the 18-actuator
budget

What to study and recalculate
Examine the arrangement of six hip assemblies, fastener access, harness routing and
centre-of-mass changes. Check overlap between adjacent leg workspaces, load transmission from
the middle pair to the frame and whether one actuator can be removed without dismantling the
body. New legs use the existing naming conventions and units but have their own calibrations.
Estimate stiffness for the selected design load case and compare it with admissible foot-position
change.
Build the power budget for actual load combinations: standing, initiating swing, a low body posture
and stopping. Do not assign each leg exactly one sixth of the weight in every phase. List
specification limits and cooling conditions for branches, connectors, BMS and DC-DC converters.
Summed rated peaks represent only one conservative scenario; separately measure simultaneous
currents and their duration.

Task 1. Design review: 4 → 6
Inputs are the M22 candidate, six-legged-frame CAD and component specifications. 1) List changes
to parts, masses, axes, harnesses and power distribution. 2) Check fasteners, clearances and
service access for every new hip frame. 3) Calculate the new configuration's centre of mass and
predict support reactions. 4) After unpowered assembly, measure mass and verify geometry using
reference dimensions.
Save scaleup_design_review.md and an updated assembly_manifest. Check that every change
traces to a CAD revision and that software renaming does not conceal workspace collisions.
Boundary case: a middle foot collides with a front link during turning. Correct the trajectory or
geometry and save the forbidden region as a test before permitting physical motion.

Task 2. Power and communication after expansion
Calculate the 18-actuator communication cycle for your protocol and telemetry content, then
compare with M22 measurements for 12 devices. With the robot supported, add new branches in
stages, checking IDs, polarity, signs, zeros and idle current. Measure simultaneous communication
at the actual frequency, computer load and enabled diagnostics. Record supply and branch
currents separately where instruments permit.
Save power_bus_18.csv and plots of margin to the communication deadline. Acceptance: new
devices create no duplicate IDs, and voltage sag and delays remain within justified operating
ranges. Boundary case: two branches work separately but overload a shared DC-DC converter
together. Revisit calculation and measurement of the common circuit; reducing gait speed is not a
universal solution to an electrical problem.























M23 • 01 Oct 2028 - 01 Nov 2028 • 75 hours                                                                      3 / 15
СтраницаPage 339 · Wave, ripple and admissible contact
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Wave, ripple and admissible contact
transitions

Gait model and transition conditions
Describe each leg with the state machine STANCE → LIFT → SWING → TOUCHDOWN → STANCE. In
STANCE, the foot is an assumed support; in SWING it moves; TOUCHDOWN requires contact
confirmation. Transitions depend on more than time: check target reachability, state freshness and
remaining supports. Phase φ from 0 to 1 identifies position in the cycle, while duty factor is the
fraction of the cycle assigned to stance.
For slow motion, calculate the convex polygon of confirmed supports and the centre-of-mass
projection along gravity onto their plane. Support margin is the signed minimum distance from this
projection to the polygon boundaries. On a horizontal floor, this is the ordinary vertical projection;
retain the projection direction on a slope. Positive geometric margin alone does not check friction,
actuator torque or dynamics.

Task 3. A wave table and verifiable support margin
Inputs are the six-legged model, level floor, calibrated axes and initial standing pose. 1) Specify
sequential single-leg swing and a phase table for all six legs. 2) Before lift-off, recalculate
remaining supports and body-position feasibility. 3) Visualise contacts, polygon and margin in
metres. 4) Run a complete cycle, startup and stopping, first in simulation and then with a small
permitted step on the test area.
Save gait_wave.yaml, the phase diagram and a log of minimum margin. Check that no more than
one leg swings at a time, feasible support exists before lift-off and commands cannot skip
touchdown. Boundary case: the foot has not touched down but the timer requests the next lift.
Block the transition and emit an event; the state machine must not continue without contact
confirmation.

Task 4. Ripple, turning and sideways motion
Construct ripple with more overlap between swings, an explicit phase table and allowed
combinations. Do not rely on the gait name alone: ripple implementations use different
conventions. For every combination, check reachability, collisions and support. Then add turning
about body z and sideways translation separately; positive directions follow the frozen coordinate
frame.
Save gait_ripple.yaml, allowed-transition tests and three short scenarios: forwards, turning and
sideways. Check that an identical command has the same meaning for right and left legs and that
mode changes pass through an admissible state. Boundary case: switching wave → ripple during
swing. Permit it only after phase alignment or through a stop. If the assumed contact is physically
impossible, the test fails even when motion appears smooth.























M23 • 01 Oct 2028 - 01 Nov 2028 • 75 hours                                                                        4 / 15
СтраницаPage 340 · Six contacts, the surface plane and
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Six contacts, the surface plane and
uncertainty

What to study
Review transforming foot coordinates from leg frames to a common body or world frame. For an
approximately planar patch, estimate z = a·x + b·y + c from confirmed supports: matrix A contains
rows [x, y, 1], vector z contains foot heights in metres, and the solution minimises squared
residuals. The normal is proportional to (−a, −b, 1). Use weights for measurements with different
reliability, explaining their origin.
A plane model cannot represent arbitrary stairs or separate rocks without examining residuals.
Three nearly collinear points provide poor geometry even with a small computed error. Six
coordinates are not six independent measurements if all derive from one erroneous body
orientation. Contact, a stationary foot and estimator confidence are three different indicators.

Task 5. Estimate a plane from six supports
Generate synthetic data for a horizontal plane and two inclined planes with known parameters,
then add noise, one outlier and contact loss. 1) Transform every foot into one frame. 2) Select
confirmed supports. 3) Solve by least squares and check rank and conditioning. 4) Calculate
residuals and a validity flag. 5) Compare with an independent reference measurement of the
prepared area.
Save terrain_estimator_tests and plot_plane_error. Check that ideal data recover the specified
plane within numerical precision; with noise, compare error to the declared tolerance, not zero.
Boundary cases are two supports, nearly collinear contacts and one foot on a protrusion. Return
invalidity or a limited estimate in these cases; an arbitrary normal without a flag is unacceptable.

Task 6. Depth-based foothold selection and camera failure
Use a saved scene depth map and camera calibration from earlier modules. Construct a small
region of admissible footholds: reachable kinematics, clearance, known surface, height uncertainty
and image age. Compare selection against a method using only confirmed contacts. With the
camera disabled, the robot remains in a previously tested mode or stops; an IMU alone does not
authorise movement over unknown terrain.
Save foothold_candidates.json and two identical scenarios with and without the camera. Check that
unknown depth does not become zero height, a stale image is not treated as fresh, and the
selected foothold passes reachability checks. Boundary case: a shiny or dark surface creates a hole
in the depth map. Show uncertainty and explain rejection of the placement while retaining the
classical fallback mode.



























M23 • 01 Oct 2028 - 01 Nov 2028 • 75 hours                                                                        5 / 15
СтраницаPage 341 · Active levelling and the terrain operating
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Active levelling and the terrain operating
boundary

Relating body tilt to leg configuration
Levelling maintains a selected body orientation relative to gravity by changing leg positions within
reachability and load limits. The IMU estimates orientation, contact estimation describes support,
and kinematics converts desired body position into joint commands. Zero roll and pitch do not
mean the feet lie at the same height; on a slope, leg configurations may differ.
Map the constraints for each pose: joint travel, proximity to singularity, loaded torque, body
clearance, traction, contact quality and support margin. Estimate quasi-static joint torque using
T·f, where J is the foot Jacobian, f is force in newtons and the result is in N·m. Force allocation
J(q)
must satisfy equilibrium and contact constraints; equal forces on all six legs are only one special
case.

Task 7. Verify 120 seconds of standing
Start on a level surface in a previously verified configuration. 1) Run a short current and contact
check. 2) Stand independently for at least 120 seconds without the backup support carrying
weight. 3) Record roll and pitch errors, data freshness, minimum support margin and temperatures.
4) Repeat after cooling and restoring initial conditions, explicitly identifying every repeat.
Save stand_120s with raw log and video. The criterion is a complete continuous interval within
declared limits, without body support or unaccounted measurement losses. This verifies a
particular standing condition, not machine lifetime. Boundary case: tilt error decreases by
saturating one joint. Body-orientation error is small, but a constraint is violated, so the trial fails.

Task 8. Map slopes and uneven terrain
Before the physical trial, calculate admissible surface angles and commanded body orientations,
then test them in simulation with mass, friction and delay variations. On an adjustable rig with
suitable backup support, increase slope in steps from a verified value. For each angle, save
achieved body roll and pitch, currents, joint poses, contacts and stopping reason. Introduce
unevenness as a separate factor with measured height.
Save operating_envelope.csv: tested, untested and forbidden regions. Mark the ±10-15° design
target as achieved only from actual tests of the specific configuration. If the limit is smaller, identify
the limiting mechanism. Boundary case: traction is lost while torque remains admissible. Reducing
controller error does not solve a contact problem. Return to level ground and investigate
foot-surface interaction.
When expanding the M20 force allocator, update contact-set size, constraints and solver timing
measurements. In HIL, test infeasible constraints and solver-deadline overruns: retain the
previously tested classical fallback. The M21 policy is outside the mandatory physical result;
transfer from four legs to six requires separate verification of observations, actions and
applicability.


















M23 • 01 Oct 2028 - 01 Nov 2028 • 75 hours                                                                           6 / 15
СтраницаPage 342 · Reliability, energy and maintenance
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Reliability, energy and maintenance

A fault tree with a clear top event
Choose the top event: the robot loses admissible support or fails to stop on request. Divide causes
into power, bus, actuator, mechanical connection, state estimation and control logic. AND denotes
a combination of required events; OR denotes alternative sufficient paths. Do not assign branch
probabilities without data; a qualitative tree already helps select tests. A common power source or
configuration error links several legs, so do not silently assume independent failures.
With only five functioning legs, the system must first recognise the condition and restrict
behaviour. Continued walking depends on geometry, load and how the sixth leg failed. A freely
dangling leg, a leg jammed in the air and a leg jammed while supporting load require different
responses. The basic fallback to verify is stopping or lowering according to the design procedure.
Five-legged walking requires a separate justification.

Task 9. Component or leg failures and recovery
From the tree, select telemetry loss, a stopped node and incorrect contact. First inject them in
simulation or HIL, recording the stimulus time, detection and resulting state. Then reproduce only
permissible rig variants with the robot supported. Check that a recovered node cannot receive an
old command without state verification and an explicit resumption procedure.
Save fault_tree and fault_runs with a timeline. Check that every stimulus has an expected outcome
and measured detection time; behaviour must fit the remaining contacts and limits. Boundary
case: a common bus failure produces six identical warnings instead of recognising a shared cause.
Add aggregate status while retaining primary errors. Do not unplug a loaded connector by hand to
demonstrate a fault.

Task 10. Energy and maintainability
On a marked route, measure voltage U(t), supply current I(t) and distance d. Energy E = ∫U·I dt is in
joules; E/3600 is Wh, and E/d is J/m for a valid non-zero distance. Compare wave and ripple at
comparable speed, surface, mass and temperature. For a stationary robot, report power and
energy over a selected interval; do not divide by a near-zero distance.
Save energy_comparison.csv with integration boundaries, measurement gaps and repeats. Then,
with the system de-energised, replace an accessible service assembly according to its instructions,
measure the time, and repeat inspection and calibration. Save maintenance_runbook and a
reasonable spare-parts list based on actual failures. Boundary case: the mechanics are restored
but zero is lost. Restart is prohibited until the joint record is updated.
For thermal balance, tabulate every actuator's temperatures on the same route: initial, maximum
observed, rise and load duration. Identify a consistently overloaded leg and check zero, friction and
support allocation. Change only one admissible configuration or phase parameter and repeat;
reduced heating in one leg must not conceal increased heating elsewhere or compromised support.





















M23 • 01 Oct 2028 - 01 Nov 2028 • 75 hours                                                                         7 / 15
СтраницаPage 343 · The test series and six required boundary
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

The test series and six required boundary
cases

A repeat plan with a defined trial unit
Plan 40 attempts as a working target within the original 30-50+ guideline. Example allocation: 10
wave trials on level ground, 10 ripple trials on the same ground, 10 levelling trials on a verified
slope, and 10 transitions into restricted operation without a camera. Each attempt includes
restoring the starting pose, checking conditions, executing the specified scenario and recording the
outcome. Sensor samples and steps within one traversal are not independent attempts.
If equipment availability or cooling duration prevents this plan, justify a smaller sample and
narrower conclusion in advance. Do not replace unavailable difficult trials with many identical easy
ones while claiming the original coverage. Mark untested conditions explicitly. For comparisons, fix
the order or alternate modes so battery discharge is not mistaken for a gait advantage.

Control scenarios
T1. Camera loss during an admissible short route: enter a verified fallback or stop, without
selecting new unknown footholds. T2. One false contact during replay: the estimator accounts for
inconsistency and does not automatically expand support. T3. Nearly collinear surface points:
return poor-conditioning or invalidity status; do not present an arbitrary slope as a reliable
estimate.
T4. Stale state from one leg: do not authorise the next phase using an old pose. T5. Wave/ripple
switching in an inconvenient phase: defer the transition or pass through a stop, retaining an
admissible contact order. T6. A stopped node or bus loss in HIL: detection, restricted behaviour and
recovery proceed without unintended resumption. A physical variant requires impact analysis and
support verification first.

What the results can establish
Report N, successes, failures and unusable records separately by condition. Calculate a confidence
interval for success rate and explicitly state the assumption of independent trials. Even 40
successful tests do not prove absolute reliability or determine lifetime in hours. Temperature drift
and a shared defect in one assembly make trials dependent; discuss this limitation instead of
artificially increasing N.
The summary must include at least one negative scenario with the expected restriction of
behaviour and one real failure if one occurred. Analyse causes, add a regression test and repeat
the relevant test class. A version change during the series separates data into different
configurations; do not combine them into one v1.0 estimate without explanation.

The first 40 hours: expansion and gaits

Hours 1-10: decisions and calculations
1-2: check the M22 package and record PASS/HOLD for physical expansion. 3-4: compare four- and
six-legged CAD and map loads, service access and conflicts. 5-6: recalculate mass, centre of mass
and power scenarios. 7-8: assess BMS, DC-DC converters, protective branches and communication
margin for 18 actuators. 9-10: specify assembly, calibration and E-stop re-verification sequences.
Put unresolved specification parameters in a question table. For each, identify its decision impact:
blocks power-up, limits the tested mode or concerns future expansion. Separately assess the
effects of external covers or styling and unknown power-connection ratings. By the end of hour ten,
have a concrete task 1 work list and expected task 2 measurements.

Hours 11-20: expansion on the rig
11-14: assemble new hip frames and two legs; measure mass, add labels and check clearances.
15-17: staged connection, identification, signs and calibration of new joints. 18-19: communication
load and power measurements with 18 devices. 20: repeat independent stopping, inspect and
freeze the revision. If the entry decision is HOLD, use these hours to repair the quadruped and test
the six-legged model without physical expansion.
Post-assembly verification must include the original four legs: new harnesses or added mass can
impair previously working components. Repeating known M22 scenarios checks preservation of
earlier functions, but does not verify an untested six-legged gait. Update numerical limits only with
supporting evidence.

Hours 21-40: contacts and movement
21-22: phase state machine and duty factor. 23-24: support polygon, centre-of-mass projection and
permissible-lift criteria. 25-26: wave table and touchdown that does not occur when the timer
expects it. 27-28: ripple and allowed overlapping swings. 29-30: turning, sideways motion and gait
changes. For every 2-hour session, prepare one test or drawing needed in practice.
31-34: task 3 in simulation, support checks and a short hardware wave traversal after rig testing.
35-37: task 4, ripple and transition through an aligned phase. 38-39: separate turning and sideways
scenarios within the verified region. 40: analyse worst support margin and correct one transition
fault. Treat tripod as a possible extension; do not add it at the expense of unfinished touchdown
control.

Hours 41-75: terrain and evidence

Hours 41-50: four important distinctions
41-42: foot coordinate frames, gravity and the support plane. 43-44: least squares, residuals, rank
and nearly collinear contacts. 45-46: contact confidence, slip and body observability. 47-48: depth
uncertainty, image age and selection of a reachable foothold. 49-50: load and kinematic-constraint
maps on a slope, desired body orientation and conditions for restricting motion.
Explain four distinctions in writing: touching versus stationary support; the plane beneath the feet
versus the horizontal; body tilt versus surface slope; and no camera versus no sensors at all. If
these concepts are confused, postpone new-terrain trials and correct notation and tests.
Terminology must agree across code, plots and protocol.

Hours 51-60: the surface experiment
51-53: task 5 on synthetic data and the measured area, including an outlier and contact loss.
54-55: task 6, the saved depth map and the same scenario without a camera. 56-57: preliminary
and qualifying 120-second standing for task 7, with analysis. 58-60: stepped slope increases and
small measured terrain variations for task 8, only within the admissible region. Save every attempt,
but count it in the confirmation series only if it follows the predefined protocol.
A failed slope trial still yields a useful result: the operating boundary and its cause. Do not raise
current limits to reach a desired plot value without recalculating the complete power circuit and
thermal behaviour. Do not change foot size midway through a series without a new design revision
either: traction and the contact model then change.

Hours 61-75: reliability and release
61-62: fault tree, five functioning legs and admissible recovery. 63-64: energy metrics, a 30-50+
series or justified N, accounting for repeats and dependence. 65: readiness of scenarios,
instruments and criteria. These 5 analysis hours are split into 2 + 2 + 1.
66-68: task 9 and control faults first in HIL, then necessary rig checks. 69-71: the prepared series of
short trials, including attempts already accepted; resetting conditions and cooling are included.
72-73: task 10 energy measurements and a service operation on the de-energised machine. 74-75:
results table, success-rate interval, limitations and the six-legged robot v1.0 package, or a
candidate with release blockers. Do not shorten checks merely to reach a repeat count: revise
claimed precision and coverage.

СтраницаPage 346 · Acceptance, additional gaits and the M24
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Acceptance, additional gaits and the M24
handoff

Required evidence for v1.0
The package includes the six-legged-frame revision and 18-joint map; mass and centre of mass;
power and communication calculations and measurements; repeated independent-stop
verification; confirmed 120-second standing; wave and ripple with admissible phases; levelling
within a defined region; responses to camera loss and node failure; a test series with justified N; an
energy report; and inspection and maintenance instructions.
Every result has a raw file, configuration version and criterion. Holding level becomes a measured
roll/pitch error, surface condition and duration. Traversing uneven terrain requires measured
obstacle geometry and attempt count. Operation without a camera applies only to the tested
restricted mode. An unmeasured quantity remains unknown even when the video appears
convincing.

When to investigate tripod
Consider tripod only after verifying wave and ripple, actuator loading and feasibility of three-legged
support. Typical alternating groups for a symmetric six-legged body are LF/RM/LR and RF/LM/RR;
verify this convention against your names and geometry. For every phase, check contacts, margin
and transition conditions. A triangle's existence does not guarantee admissible torques, friction or
stability during swing.
Optional task if time permits: compare tripod and ripple phase tables in simulation with the same
input, saving minimum margin and errors. A physical run requires a separate positive decision for
that mode; it is outside the required M23 evidence. Similarly, five-legged walking remains research
unless its operating envelope is calculated and verified.

Defence and handoff package
Answer: why do 18 actuators change the communication deadline; why is six-legged load not
always shared equally; what does insufficient rank in plane estimation mean; how do loss of
contact and slip differ; why does zero tilt not guarantee an admissible pose; what response is
available for a jammed leg; what does E/d measure; and why do 40 successful attempts not mean
100% reliability? Demonstrate the answers using your data.
Pass to M24 requirements_candidates.csv, the attempt register, links to every raw log, assembly
and calibration instructions, limitations, known defects and repair priorities. Record the hand's
status and OPT results on a separate line. Do not rename an unfinished function as verified to meet
the shared date. G4 remains a separate 35-hour integration checkpoint after the modules; it is not
hidden within these 75 hours.

Assigned reading: six legs, contact and
reliability

The references may be in English; the exercises and definitions are presented here in English. Read
only the named sections before the associated work, within the existing 75 hours.

Core reading: contact and loading
1. R. Tedrake - Underactuated Robotics, MIT notes. Planning and Control through Contact →
(Autonomous) Hybrid Systems. For tasks 3-4, write out foot modes, transition conditions (guards)
and state changes on switching (reset); a phase transition requires a verified event. Retain the
remaining contact-optimisation material as reference.
2. K. Lynch, F. Park - Modern Robotics. 12.1.2 Contact Types; 12.1.3 Multiple Contacts; 12.2.1
Friction. For tasks 4-6, distinguish touching, slipping and contact loss. Apply the contact model to
feet; manipulation results do not directly establish six-legged stability.

A decision-making reference
3. NASA - Systems Engineering Handbook. 6.4 Technical Risk Management; 6.5 Configuration
Management. For task 9 and PASS/HOLD, connect the fault event, consequence, test and assembly
revision. Use a brief register without unsupported probabilities.

Documentation as needed
Actuator bus. DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0: Sync Read/Write, Bulk Read - only if it matches the real
protocol. For task 2, recalculate communication volume and time for 18 devices; spares are
excluded from active polling.
ROS diagnostics. README: diagnostic_updater, diagnostic_aggregator. For task 9, distinguish a
missing reply from one leg, common-channel failure and stale status; check the branch against
Jazzy.
NumPy. linalg.lstsq: rank, singular values, residuals. For task 5, assess geometric degeneracy in

Optional: architecture comparison
Kevin Ochs, ROS Hexapod Stack: Nodes and hexapod_controller. This historical ROS project is useful for

СтраницаPage 348 · Terms and definitions
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Terms and definitions

Gait phase. Normalised position within a repeating cycle; it specifies the contact plan but does not
confirm actual foot-surface contact.
Stance. An interval of planned leg contact during which admissible support force is constrained by
traction, geometry and actuators.
Swing. Movement of a foot to its next support without planned support-force transmission;
premature contact requires a separate response.
Wave gait. A slow sequential gait with legs swinging in turn; the specific order and admissible
overlaps are defined by a phase table.
Ripple gait. A gait with phase-shifted waves of swing; the selected table, rather than the name,
determines the number of simultaneous swings.
Tripod gait. A gait alternating two groups of three legs; group geometry alone does not guarantee
admissible forces.
Guard. A testable condition for changing a discrete mode, such as confirmed contact or a timeout;
activation is associated with a defined response.
Reset. A specified model or controller state change at a mode transition, such as clearing a timer
and initialising a new support point.
Support polygon. The convex hull of selected contact points in a planar model; its applicability
depends on assumptions about surface and forces.
Static stability margin. The minimum signed distance from the centre-of-mass projection to the
support-polygon boundary, positive inside. Its use is limited to a planar quasi-static model.
Duty factor β. The fraction of a cycle a leg spends in planned stance; a dimensionless quantity
between zero and one.
Surface normal. A unit vector perpendicular to a local plane; fix its direction and coordinate
frame to prevent sign reversal of the estimate.
System rank. The number of independent data or constraint directions; insufficient rank means
the selected plane parameters cannot be determined uniquely.
Slip. Relative tangential motion between a contacting foot and surface; a contact sensor may
remain active during slipping.
Active levelling. Changing leg commands to reduce body-orientation error while respecting
reachability, contacts and load limits.
Load redistribution. Changing forces among stance legs during movement or failure; additional
contacts do not automatically equalise forces.
Bus utilisation. The fraction of available channel time occupied by communication, including
overhead, pauses and retries; distinct from useful data throughput.
Specific energy E/d. Energy used per unit distance travelled, usually J/m; comparison requires
identical conditions and a non-zero measured distance.

Relationships: β = T_stance/T_cycle; E = ∫U(t)I(t)dt. Check: verified 120-second standing characterises the
completed trial, not every possible duration.

СтраницаPage 349 · Six-legged robot purchases and setup
ROBOTICS AND AI  /  M23  /  DETAILED STUDY PLAN

Six-legged robot purchases and setup

USE EXISTING EQUIPMENT
Use the accepted M22 quadruped with 12 working actuators and 2 separate spares, onboard
computer, MCU, IMU, camera, bus, instruments and support rig. For the existing 3D printer, choose
the exact-model profile; print new parts to the six-legged-frame revision.

BUY BEFORE EXPANSION - AFTER M22 PASS
6 additional working actuators from the same verified family and 2 additional spares. This
gives 18 installed + 4 separate spares if the earlier spares are unused. Update inventory when
replenishing used spares. The M7 actuator rig is excluded from this count.
1 set of parts for two legs and a new or reinforced frame, bearings, inserts, fasteners and
harnesses, with quantities from released CAD and BOM. If retaining M22 contact-sensing feet, add
2 channels for two feet: 4 + 2 = 6 total. Without the original four, select a separate six-channel
set after testing one foot.

OPTIONAL OR SUBJECT TO CALCULATION
Recalculate power, thermal behaviour and communication for the new mass and 18 devices.
Replace battery, BMS, charger, power disconnection, DC-DC converter, cables and protective
devices only when they fail the measured budget; upgrading the battery alone is insufficient.
Ratings depend on peaks and their durations, voltage drop and interruption currents, not the ratio
18/12.
Check the existing rig's load capacity and onboard-computer cooling. A second computer, CUDA
GPU and new actuator family are optional. Hardware tripod operation requires a separate check of
that mode after wave and ripple; do not expand while on HOLD.

INSTALL NOW
No new software stack is needed: pinned Ubuntu 24.04, ROS 2 Jazzy, ros2_control, NumPy and
SciPy. If diagnostics are not connected, add diagnostic_updater and diagnostic_aggregator from
ROS diagnostics for your version; check dependencies with rosdep. Retain the analysis and replay
environment on the Mac and in UTM.

INSTALLATION AND CONFIGURATION CHECK
Before applying torque: check 18 unique IDs, 18 correct URDF joints, the software simulator, replay
with a missing node and displayed diagnostics. Then measure communication cycle and stopping
on the support. For terrain, check degenerate point sets, REP-103 units and axes and SciPy
proportion_ci: method, confidence_level using the log of all attempts.

Preparation and checks fit within the existing 75 hours, replacing repeated reading and setup. Delivery waiting
time does not count as study time.
